nodes.title: EPIC: Adapter Pattern (post-v1)
nodes.description: Post-v1 implementations of the issuance adapter pattern (spec §10, roadmap Phase 9): an AWS Private CA adapter, a reference adapter SDK for third-party CAs, and the adapter health/observability and admin surface (CLI + UI + chaos/runbook obligations). Everything builds strictly on the v1 EntryIntake seam owned by ca-service (anchor entry-intake-trait, §10.2) — no ticket here redefines that trait. Per §1 non-goals (no production cloud spend) everything runs on a laptop against LocalStack and the local demo environment; CDK work is validated by `cdk synth` assertions only, and real-AWS validation is explicitly out of scope. All tickets are priority 3, phase 9.

nodes.title: EPIC: Admin Surface (CLI + UI + API)
nodes.description: Build the complete admin surface for the MTC CA: an axum admin API defined by OpenAPI (spec §17.2), the mtcctl CLI built with clap v4 (§17.3), and an htmx+Askama+SSE web UI embedded in the CA service binary (§17.4) — with enforced full CLI/UI parity so every operation is available on both surfaces (§17.1). Both consumers ride the foundation-owned OpenAPI codegen pipeline, and each admin operation lands vertically: OpenAPI change, server handler, CLI subcommand, UI view, and CLI-driven E2E test (§17.5, §19.13).

nodes.title: EPIC: Agent Harnessing
nodes.description: Agent Harnessing builds the repo's agent-first development scaffolding per spec §23: seeded `.claude/skills/` and `.claude/rules/`, the AGENTS.md entry-point guide, inner-loop make targets (agent-precheck, watch, verify-task, WORKING_SET.md), and outer-loop tooling (decision journal, Beads-journal integration, ADRs, pattern/anti-pattern library). It also ships the scaling-beyond-context-window aids — CODEMAP generation, hierarchical READMEs, search affordances, living Mermaid diagrams, and `make agent-context` — plus the §23.8 context-budget patterns as repo docs, so autonomous agents can navigate and extend this system without eroding its invariants (§23 thesis). CI enforcement of these local lint/check targets is owned by foundation-infra; the Beads board itself is already initialized.

nodes.title: EPIC: CA Service (Single-Region)
nodes.description: Build the single-region MTC CA service (Phase 3 MVP): the source-agnostic EntryIntake adapter seam (spec 10.2, 25.9), the native ACME endpoint as the first adapter, and the full write-path lifecycle (batch builder, index allocation, entry/tile writes, tree updater, HSM-backed checkpoint signer, and the linearization-point commit) per spec sections 10-11. It culminates in a laptop-runnable single-region issuance end-to-end demo against LocalStack + SoftHSM, with the section 11.2 critical invariants enforced and machine-checked where the spec demands (Kani for index allocation and the linearization point, Loom for intake/batch concurrency per 19.12). Multi-region lease/epoch protocol, admin surfaces, and non-ACME adapters belong to other epics.

nodes.title: EPIC: Cloud Abstraction Layer
nodes.description: Build the cloud abstraction layer (spec §9): the four cloud-agnostic traits (ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv, Hsm) in cloud-types, plus the cloud-memory, cloud-aws, cloud-localstack, and cloud-softhsm backend crates, wired through a Backend factory selected by runtime config and Cargo features. A shared cloud-test-suite crate guarantees behavioral consistency by running identical conformance suites against every backend — memory in unit tests, AWS via LocalStack, and SoftHSM2 via PKCS#11 — all runnable on a laptop with zero cloud spend (§1, §18).

nodes.title: EPIC: Core MTC Library
nodes.description: Clean-room Rust implementation of MTC spec primitives (draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs -03) in crates/mtc: domain newtypes, Merkle tree math (including tree-level range pruning per section 19.2), tiles, checkpoints, log entries, landmarks, and TLS-presentation wire formats, with ECDSA P-256 (v1) and feature-gated ML-DSA via qux-pqc. Ships with its own verification arsenal per spec sections 19.2-19.6 and 19.12: proptest invariant suite, per-format cargo-fuzz targets, conformance vector scaffolding, differential testing against the bwesterb/mtc Go oracle, and the first Kani harnesses for tree primitives. This epic is the critical-path root: core-mtc-types, tree-primitives, and mtc-serialization block nearly every downstream epic.

nodes.title: EPIC: Foundation & Infrastructure
nodes.description: Establish the repository's structural backbone per spec Phase 0 (§24): the Cargo workspace and strict lint regime (§22.12), CI/CD with the required checks of §22.13, the TypeScript CDK skeleton targeting cdk-synth correctness and LocalStack only (§1 non-goals, §4), the LocalStack+SoftHSM local dev environment (§18.1), the OpenAPI codegen pipeline that unblocks the admin surface (§17.2, §25.5), and license/supply-chain policy tooling (§6). Everything runs on a laptop with zero cloud spend; no real AWS deployment is in scope.

nodes.title: EPIC: Local Developer Experience
nodes.description: Everything in spec §18 built on top of the LocalStack dev environment: the 60-second `make demo`, a three-region local simulation with simulated CRR/Global Tables replication plus partition and failover exercises, FakeClock-based time travel, deterministic named fixtures, dual REPLs (evcxr and mtcctl), hot reload, and the self-documenting make target suite. Per §25.7 dev-experience tickets are first-class: this epic is the velocity substrate for every other epic, for both humans and agents, and everything runs on a laptop at zero cloud cost (§1).

nodes.title: EPIC: Multi-Cloud Backends (post-v1)
nodes.description: Post-v1 backlog implementing the §27 multi-cloud story: GCP, Azure, and on-premise backend implementations of the §9 cloud abstraction traits (ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv, Hsm), a Pulumi-based multi-cloud IaC track (§27.5), replication-lag-aware failover support (§27.2), and systematic portability validation (§27.6) via a cross-backend test matrix, a capability probe for long-tail clouds (§27.4), and portability documentation. Everything runs on a laptop against emulators (fake-gcs-server, Firestore emulator, Azurite, Cosmos stub/emulator, MinIO, etcd) and mocks — no real cloud accounts or spend, per §1 non-goals. Boundary: the v1 AWS/memory/LocalStack/SoftHSM backends belong to the cloud-abstraction epic, not here.

nodes.title: EPIC: Multi-Region Coordination
nodes.description: Implements the multi-region active-passive coordination layer for the MTC CA: the DynamoDB-backed lease/epoch protocol (spec 8.2-8.3), lease renewer, standby read-only mode, idempotent promotion, and old-primary recovery that together make split-brain impossible (spec 13). Delivers the manual failover surface (mtcctl failover CLI + admin UI), a laptop-scale three-region simulation with configurable replication lag and partition injection (spec 18.3), and the failover-specific chaos scenarios (spec 19.9). Trust-story-critical verification ships with the epic: mandatory Kani proofs of the lease/epoch invariants and Loom model checking of lease renewer vs batch builder concurrency (spec 19.12).

nodes.title: EPIC: Self-Auditor & Observability
nodes.description: Deliver the full observability layer for the MTC CA per spec §20 and roadmap Phase 6: the P0 self-auditor Lambda that substitutes for external transparency in a cosigner-free deployment (§25.8), including anomaly-triggered issuance freeze; structured logging/tracing/metrics foundations; dashboards and SLO alarms as CDK code with synth assertions; per-cert forensics, signed compliance reports (`mtcctl report`) with a Reports UI view, tree visualization in the admin UI, and the §20.5 health endpoints. Everything runs on a laptop against the memory backend and LocalStack — no real AWS deployment (§1 non-goals). Runbooks are explicitly out of this epic (operational-tooling).

nodes.title: EPIC: Operational Tooling
nodes.description: Operational tooling for the MTC CA: the full runbook library mandated by §21.2 (with template, structure linting, and drill validation against the local multi-region simulation), capacity planning documentation and calculator tooling per §21.1, the Phase 8 security review checklist and its execution, triage/trending tooling for chaos and soak results (§19.7/§19.9), and the final documentation polish pass. Failover/promotion CLI implementation and the chaos harness itself live in the multi-region and testing-infra epics respectively; this epic owns the operator-facing documents and analysis tooling layered on top of them.

nodes.title: EPIC: Pruning & Retention
nodes.description: Implements spec section 15 Pruning and Retention: a primary-only (lease-enforced) pruning workflow that records signed pruning checkpoints (pruned_range = [start, end) at tree_size T), advances a replicated watermark, and removes leaf objects only after S3 Object Lock (Compliance mode) retention has expired. Includes the OQ-7 orchestration decision (Step Functions vs Lambda chain), pruning-worker Lambda plus CDK synth-tested infrastructure, configurable retention policy (default 7 years; pruning checkpoints retained indefinitely), and end-to-end LocalStack validation of Object Lock semantics, plus the mtcctl prune CLI/admin surface (spec 17.3), post-pruning fixture, pruning-failure runbook, and observability hooks. Revocation is a separate parallel epic (25.6) and is out of scope here.

nodes.title: EPIC: Read Path
nodes.description: Implements the MTC read path per spec section 12: a stateless Lambda proof-server fronted by CloudFront (CDK synth-tested only, with a LocalStack-equivalent local serving mode), inclusion/consistency proof generation over stored tiles and checkpoints, a relying-party verification library covering the full 12.1 flow including the signatureless landmark optimization, and mtcctl log commands for proof inspection and verification. Everything runs on a laptop against LocalStack per section 1 non-goals; tree primitives and serialization come from core-mtc-library, storage layout from storage-facade.

nodes.title: EPIC: Revocation
nodes.description: Implement MTC log revocation end-to-end per spec section 16: the signed RevocationList format with revoked index ranges, the event-driven revocation-processor Lambda that generates and HSM-signs new lists, distribution via CloudFront-fronted S3 with hourly cadence plus push notification for near-real-time emergency refresh, and the operator-facing emergency revocation flow (CLI + admin UI + runbook). All work runs locally against LocalStack/SoftHSM with cdk-synth assertions for infra; pruning belongs to the pruning-retention epic.

nodes.title: EPIC: Storage Facade
nodes.description: Build the crates/storage facade the CA service consumes: it maps the S3 object layout (§8.1), S3 write-once/retention invariants, and the DynamoDB single-table access patterns (§8.2) onto the cloud-abstraction traits, with every mutating write epoch-conditioned per §8.3. It also owns the in-memory storage-adjacent state from §8.4: LRU tile cache, checkpoint cache, counter view, and CA state hydration on startup. It provides raw KV/lease-item access only — the lease/epoch protocol lives in the multi-region epic, and trait definitions live in cloud-abstraction. The entry intake queue (§8.4) is excluded: it is drained by the batch builder and belongs to ca-service.

nodes.title: EPIC: Testing Infrastructure
nodes.description: Shared testing harnesses, runners, fixture infrastructure, and CI wiring for the MTC CA per spec section 19: proptest conventions, four-layer fuzzing (19.3), conformance and differential runners against the bwesterb/mtc Go reference, fault-injection backends powering the adversarial (19.8) and chaos (19.9) suites, soak/perf/cross-version harnesses, Kani/Loom/Shuttle CI integration (19.12, 22.13), and the E2E-via-CLI harness (19.13). Component-specific tests ship with their component epics; this epic owns everything those tests plug into, all runnable on a laptop against LocalStack/SoftHSM/memory backends per section 1 non-goals (no cloud spend).

nodes.title: mtcctl CLI skeleton: clap v4 tree, generated client wiring, output formats
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/mtcctl` with the full clap v4 (derive) subcommand tree from §17.3, wired to the OpenAPI-generated Rust client, with the global output-format contract agents and scripts rely on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/mtcctl` binary with the complete §17.3 subcommand tree declared; unimplemented leaves exit non-zero with a clear 'not yet implemented' message
- Global flags: `--output human|json|yaml` (human default), `--endpoint`, `--yes`/`--confirm` plumbed through (enforcement in adm-privileged-confirm)
- Uses the OpenAPI-generated Rust client (§17.2) for all API calls; no hand-rolled HTTP
- Output layer: human tables, `--output json` and `--output yaml` via serde on the same response types
- `mtcctl status` returns live data from the health/version endpoint as first working command
- Errors map to distinct exit codes; stderr for diagnostics, stdout for payload

## Out of Scope
- Individual operation implementations (per-operation tickets)
- REPL and shell completion (adm-repl, adm-completion)
- Request signing (adm-auth-middleware)

## Testing
- Unit: clap parse tests (`Command::debug_assert`), output-format snapshot tests
- Integration: run binary against an in-process axum test server; assert JSON output is stable

## Demo
`mtcctl status --output json | jq .version` against `make demo` environment.

nodes.title: Admin API core: axum crate serving OpenAPI-generated server stubs
nodes.description:
## Goal
Stand up `crates/admin` as the admin API core (spec §17.2): an axum app mounting routes from OpenAPI-generated Rust server stubs. This is the single API both mtcctl and the UI consume, and the anchor for all admin-surface work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/admin` exists with `lib.rs` mounting API routes (axum), per the layout in §17.4
- Routes implemented against Rust server stubs generated from `api/admin.openapi.yaml` via `make api-gen` (foundation pipeline)
- Health/version endpoint implemented end-to-end as the first operation (spec -> stub -> handler)
- Shared JSON error model (problem-details style) with typed handler errors
- `AppState` seam injects CA-service state handles as trait objects so handlers run against the memory backend in tests
- API mounted in the CA service binary, reachable on localhost:8080 in dev mode

## Out of Scope
- IAM auth middleware (adm-auth-middleware)
- UI routes/templates (adm-ui-shell)
- Business operations beyond health/version (per-operation tickets)
- The codegen pipeline itself (foundation-infra: openapi-codegen-pipeline)

## Testing
- Unit: handler tests against in-memory AppState (§19.1, no external deps)
- Integration: axum/tower test client over the mounted router; check that regenerated code compiles in CI

## Demo
`cargo run -p ca-service` (dev mode) then `curl localhost:8080/api/healthz` returns JSON status.

nodes.title: Inner-loop tooling: make agent-precheck, make watch, make verify-task, WORKING_SET.md
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the §23.4 inner-loop tooling — `make agent-precheck`, `make watch`, `make verify-task`, and the `WORKING_SET.md` convention — the fast-feedback loop every agent task runs inside.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `make agent-precheck` verifies required tools (Rust toolchain, docker, beads CLI), prints recent `docs/journal.md` entries, runs workspace lint and fast unit tests; non-zero exit on any failure; completes in ~60s on a warm laptop
- PR 2: `make watch` runs lint+test on save (bacon or cargo-watch) with fast incremental feedback; `make verify-task` runs lint, the fast test suite, and doc/skill/rules lints as the pre-done acceptance gate
- PR 2: `WORKING_SET.md` template checked in (files touched, decisions made, open questions), working copies gitignored, convention documented
- Everything runs offline on a laptop (§1 non-goals, §18)

## Out of Scope
- CI required checks (foundation-infra ci-pipeline)
- `make agent-context` (agent-context-summary); journal implementation (agent-journal-tooling)

## Testing
- E2E smoke (§19.13): each target invoked in a clean checkout by a test script; unit tests for nontrivial script logic; shellcheck

## Demo
On a fresh clone: `make agent-precheck` prints environment status, recent journal entries, and lint+test results, then `make verify-task` passes.

nodes.title: Seed docs/journal.md decision journal with make journal append tooling
nodes.description:
## Goal
Establish the decision journal per §23.5/§23.7: `docs/journal.md` plus `make journal` append tooling and documented conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/journal.md` seeded with the §23.7 entry template (ticket, PR, decisions, rejected alternatives, open questions) and one initial real entry
- `make journal msg="..."` appends a timestamped entry; handles quoting and multiline text safely
- Conventions documented in the journal header: when to journal (task completion, non-trivial decisions), entry format, ordering (chosen and stated)
- Invocation with missing/empty `msg` errors clearly and leaves the file untouched

## Out of Scope
- Beads auto-append on ticket close (agent-beads-journal-hook)
- ADRs (agent-adr-scaffold)

## Testing
- Script smoke tests (§19.13 spirit): append twice, assert ordering and timestamp format; malformed invocation leaves the file unchanged; shellcheck on scripts. No §19.1 code layers apply beyond make-target smoke.

## Demo
`make journal msg="hello from demo"` then `tail docs/journal.md` shows the new timestamped entry in template form.

nodes.title: Scaffold .claude/skills/ framework: template, authoring guide, skill-lint
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create the `.claude/skills/` framework per §23.1 — directory, authoring template, and local validation — so subsystem skills can be seeded as their subject code lands.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `.claude/skills/README.md` documents purpose and the required skill structure: Goal, Files involved (3–5 pointers), Pattern, Common pitfalls (§23.1)
- `_template.md` skill template checked in
- `make skill-lint` validates every skill file has the required sections and that "Files involved" paths exist; fails loudly on violations
- Skill-driven scoping (~5 files per skill) documented as a context-budget pattern (§23.8)

## Out of Scope
- The eight §23.1 subsystem skills themselves (seeded by later tickets as their subject code lands)
- CI wiring of skill-lint (foundation-infra ci-pipeline)

## Testing
- Script smoke (§19.13 spirit): skill-lint passes on the template, fails on a fixture missing a required section and on a dangling file path; shellcheck

## Demo
`make skill-lint` passes; copy `_template.md`, delete a section, and watch it fail with a clear message.

nodes.title: Cargo workspace scaffolding with pinned toolchain and workspace lints baseline
nodes.description:
## Goal
Establish the Rust Cargo workspace at the repo root per §4 (repo split: `crates/` Rust, `infra/` TS) and the §9.3 crate-layout conventions, so every downstream epic can add crates without re-deciding structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Root `Cargo.toml` defines `[workspace]` (resolver 2), `workspace.package` (edition, rust-version, license, repository) and `workspace.dependencies` pinning the §4 baseline: tokio, serde, thiserror, eyre/color-eyre, tracing, proptest, pretty_assertions, mockall
- `rust-toolchain.toml` pins a stable toolchain with rustfmt + clippy components
- `crates/` exists with one small placeholder lib crate that inherits `lints.workspace = true`, has a doctest, and passes `cargo test`
- Initial `[workspace.lints]` table with `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (§22.12)
- `cargo build` and `cargo test` are green from a fresh clone

## Out of Scope
- Strict clippy/rustfmt configuration (fnd-rust-lint-config)
- CI wiring (ci-pipeline); domain crates (core-mtc-library epic); cloud crates of §9.3 (cloud-abstraction epic)

## Testing
- Unit: placeholder crate test + doctest prove the `cargo test` and `cargo test --doc` harnesses work (§19.1)

## Demo
Fresh clone → `cargo test` green; `cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq .workspace_members` shows the workspace.

nodes.title: CI pipeline with core required Rust checks (fmt, clippy, test, doctest)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Stand up the CI workflow (GitHub Actions) implementing the core required checks of §22.13 so every PR is gated on fmt, clippy, and the full test suite from day one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Workflow triggers on PRs and pushes to main; jobs: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo test --doc` (§22.13)
- Rust build caching (e.g., Swatinem/rust-cache) keeps a green run under ~10 minutes on the placeholder workspace
- Concurrency group cancels superseded runs per branch
- The list of required status checks (for branch protection) is documented in `docs/`
- A deliberately broken scratch PR shows red; reverting shows green

## Out of Scope
- cargo deny/audit jobs (fnd-license-policy); API spec check (fnd-ci-api-spec-check); Kani gate (fnd-ci-kani-gate); infra lane (fnd-ci-infra-checks); LocalStack integration lane (fnd-ci-integration-lane)

## Testing
- CI-level: validated by a passing test PR and a deliberately failing one (fmt violation) before merge

## Demo
Open a trivial PR → `gh pr checks` lists all four Rust checks green; push an unformatted file → fmt check fails.

nodes.title: Makefile target-suite skeleton with self-documenting help and stub targets
nodes.description:
## Goal
Establish the top-level Makefile target suite (§18.8) as the single entry point for all dev workflows: every target from the spec table is declared up front, delegating to `scripts/` or cargo, so later tickets across all epics wire in implementations without restructuring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Top-level `Makefile` declares every target in the §18.8 table (`demo`, `demo-multiregion`, `test*`, `repl`, `fixture-load/save`, `time-advance`, `partition-region`, `api-gen`, `codemap`, `agent-context`, `agent-precheck`, `verify-task`, `journal`, `lint`, `fmt`, `audit`, `bench`, `doctor`) plus lifecycle companions `dev`, `demo-down`, `demo-multiregion-down`
- Implemented targets delegate to `scripts/<name>.sh` or cargo; unimplemented targets print "not implemented yet — tracked in beads" and exit non-zero
- `make help` (default target) self-documents all targets from `##` comments
- Parameterized targets accept args per spec (`name=X`, `days=N`, `msg="..."`)
- Conventions documented in `docs/dev-environment.md` so other epics add targets consistently

## Out of Scope
- Implementations behind any target (owned by follow-on tickets across epics)
- CI job definitions (§22.13, foundation-infra)

## Testing
- E2E: shell smoke test in `tests/e2e/make-targets.sh` asserts `make help` lists all §18.8 targets and stubs exit non-zero

## Demo
`make help` shows the full annotated target catalog; `make demo` prints a friendly not-implemented pointer to its beads ticket.

nodes.title: LocalStack + SoftHSM2 compose-based local dev environment
nodes.description:
## Goal
Deliver the zero-cost local simulation environment of §18.1 and §1 non-goals: a compose file bringing up LocalStack (S3 with versioning + Object Lock, DynamoDB) and SoftHSM2, with init scripts matching the §8 data model.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docker-compose.yml` with a pinned LocalStack version and healthcheck
- Init script creates the log bucket (versioning + Object Lock enabled) and the DDB coordination table per §8.1/§8.2
- SoftHSM2 provisioned (container or scripted local install) with an initialized token and an ECDSA P-256 keypair per the §4 HSM dev row and §14
- Endpoint/env-var contract documented (`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, credentials, PKCS#11 module path) consistent with fnd-cdk-ssm-config-handoff's local-override doc
- Reset/teardown script restores a clean slate; cold start to healthy in under ~60s on a laptop (§18.1)

## Out of Scope
- `make demo` orchestration and CA service startup (local-dev-experience epic)
- Multi-region simulation (§18.3, multi-region epic); the Rust SoftHSM PKCS#11 crate (cloud-abstraction epic)

## Testing
- Integration: smoke script asserts Object Lock config via awslocal, describes the DDB table, and lists SoftHSM slots via pkcs11-tool (§19.1)

## Demo
`docker compose up -d && ./scripts/dev-env-smoke.sh` prints all checks green.

nodes.title: OpenAPI spec seed + Rust code generation pipeline (server stubs, client)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `api/admin.openapi.yaml` and the Rust side of the §17.2 codegen pipeline: an axum-compatible server-stub crate and a Rust client crate. Critical path: blocks all admin UI/CLI work (§25.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Seed spec defines `/healthz`, `/readyz` (§20.5) and a minimal `/status` (§17.3) with typed schemas
- Spec lint (redocly or spectral) configured and passing
- One regeneration entrypoint (`scripts/api-gen.sh` or cargo xtask) generates an axum-compatible Rust server-stub crate and a Rust client crate (§17.2)
- Generated code is committed; regeneration is deterministic so drift is detectable by diff
- Generated Rust crates compile in the workspace; a trivial test round-trips a `/status` response type through the client types

## Out of Scope
- TypeScript client, HTML API docs, and the §17.5 workflow doc (fnd-openapi-ts-client-docs)
- Real endpoint implementations and UI/CLI wiring (admin-surface epic)
- `make api-gen` target (local-dev-experience); CI enforcement (fnd-ci-api-spec-check)

## Testing
- Unit: generated crates compile + type round-trip test; spec lint runs in the regen entrypoint (§19.1)

## Demo
Add a field to the `/status` schema, run `./scripts/api-gen.sh`, watch the server stub and client types regenerate deterministically.

nodes.title: Admin UI shell: htmx + Askama layout, rust-embed static assets
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the basic admin UI shell (roadmap Phase 0; spec §17.4): Askama compile-time templates, vendored htmx, static assets embedded via rust-embed, served from the same axum app as the API.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/admin/templates/` with `layout.html`, `partials/`, `pages/` structure per §17.4; `templates.rs` holds Askama template structs
- `static/` with vendored `htmx.min.js` and `styles.css`, embedded via `rust-embed` and served from the binary (no external CDN, no JS build toolchain)
- UI routes mounted in `crates/admin` `lib.rs` alongside API routes
- Dashboard placeholder page renders with nav linking every planned view from the §17.4 table (stub pages OK)
- Askama compile-time checking active: a template referencing a missing field fails the build

## Out of Scope
- SSE real-time updates (adm-sse-stream)
- Real data on any page (per-operation tickets)
- Tree visualization (observability epic)

## Testing
- Unit: template render tests for layout and placeholder pages
- Integration: axum test client asserts 200 + text/html for each route and embedded asset

## Demo
`make demo` then open `localhost:8080` — dashboard shell with nav renders, assets load offline.

nodes.title: Scaffold docs/adr/: template, grep-able index, make adr target
nodes.description:
## Goal
Stand up `docs/adr/` per §23.5–23.6: template, grep-able index, and scaffolding target, so non-trivial decisions are preserved as standalone artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/adr/` contains an MADR-style template (context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences)
- `docs/adr/README.md` index lists all ADRs with one-line summaries — the §23.6 "ADR index" agents grep before re-deciding
- ADR-0001 recorded: adoption of the ADR process itself
- `make adr title="..."` scaffolds the next-numbered ADR from the template and adds an index row
- The `document-decisions` rule (§23.2) cross-links here

## Out of Scope
- Backfilling ADRs for decisions already made in the spec
- CI freshness check on the index (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Script smoke (§19.13 spirit): `make adr` creates a sequentially numbered file and index entry; markdown lint; shellcheck

## Demo
`make adr title="Demo decision"` then show the new numbered file and the updated index row.

nodes.title: Seed AGENTS.md top-level agent guide
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create the repo-root `AGENTS.md` per §23.3: the starting point every agent reads before any task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `AGENTS.md` exists at repo root with the six §23.3 sections: repository tour, how to start a task (precheck, branch, test, journal), standard patterns, where to find what, common commands, gotchas
- Repository tour reflects the actual Cargo workspace crate layout and points to subsystem READMEs and `CODEMAP.md`
- "How to start a task" documents `make agent-precheck`, `make watch`, `make verify-task`, `make journal msg=...`, and the `WORKING_SET.md` convention (§23.4–23.5)
- Documents the strict-module-privacy navigation convention (a crate's `lib.rs` is the surface to learn deeply) and the spec-by-test convention (grep test names for behavior; E2E tests authored as shell scripts driving `mtcctl`) per §23.6/§19.13
- Links to `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, `docs/journal.md`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/patterns/`
- Markdown lint passes; all intra-repo links resolve

## Out of Scope
- The make targets themselves (agent-inner-loop-targets)
- Subsystem READMEs (agent-readme-hierarchy); CODEMAP generation (agent-codemap-generator)

## Testing
- No §19.1 code layers apply; validated by markdown lint and a local link-check make target

## Demo
Open `AGENTS.md` and follow its "start a task" steps verbatim on a clean checkout — every referenced command succeeds.

nodes.title: Seed .claude/rules/ with the sixteen §23.2 repo rules
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed `.claude/rules/` with the sixteen repo-specific rules listed in §23.2 so agents inherit the project's guardrails from day one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1 (code discipline): `always-test-with-pr`, `no-systemtime-now-in-prod`, `no-unwrap-in-prod`, `no-unsafe`, `use-newtypes`, `thiserror-for-libs-eyre-for-bins`, `no-sdk-types-in-domain`, `prefer-generics-on-hot-paths` — each citing its §22 subsection
- PR 2 (workflow): `fips-boundary-preserved`, `cli-ui-parity`, `document-decisions`, `run-precheck-first`, `update-codemap-on-structure-change`, `single-pr-acceptance`, `kani-for-critical-paths`, `spec-pin-and-track`
- Each rule file states: the rule, rationale, one compliant and one non-compliant example, and how it is enforced (lint, CI gate, or review)
- Rules referencing commands (`make agent-precheck`, `make codemap`) use the spec-defined target names (§23.4, §23.6) so they stay valid even if seeded before those targets land

## Out of Scope
- Clippy/CI enforcement of the rules (foundation-infra ci-pipeline)
- Skills and AGENTS.md (separate tickets)

## Testing
- No §19.1 code layers; markdown lint plus a `make rules-lint` check that every rule file has the required headings

## Demo
`ls .claude/rules/` shows all 16 rules; open any file and see rule/rationale/examples/enforcement sections.

nodes.title: Implement make codemap generating CODEMAP.md crate summary
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `make codemap` per §23.6: generate `CODEMAP.md` summarizing every crate's purpose, public API, dependencies, and dependents, giving agents navigation without loading all files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: generator (script or cargo xtask) walks `cargo metadata` and emits per-crate blocks in the §23.6 format (CRATE / PURPOSE / PUBLIC API / DEPENDS ON / USED BY); PURPOSE sourced from Cargo.toml `description`
- PR 2: PUBLIC API section lists `pub` items exported from each crate's `lib.rs` (top-level surface only, honoring §23.6 strict module privacy)
- `CODEMAP.md` checked into the repo; `make codemap-check` fails when regeneration would change the committed file
- Deterministic, stably ordered output so diffs are meaningful

## Out of Scope
- CI enforcement of codemap freshness (foundation-infra ci-pipeline)
- Non-Rust artifacts (CDK app) — later enhancement

## Testing
- Unit tests for the generator against a small fixture workspace; E2E smoke (§19.13): run against the real workspace and assert format and determinism

## Demo
`make codemap && git diff --exit-code CODEMAP.md`, then open CODEMAP.md and jump from a crate entry to its `lib.rs` API.

nodes.title: AWS CDK TypeScript app skeleton in infra/ (synth-only, stack split per spec)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create the CDK TypeScript app skeleton in `infra/` per §4: separate `MtcLogStorageStack` and `MtcComputeStack` behind construct-level abstractions, targeting `cdk synth` correctness only — no real AWS deploys per §1 non-goals.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `infra/` npm project with pinned Node version and `aws-cdk-lib`; `tsc --strict`, eslint, prettier configured and passing
- `bin/` app instantiates `MtcLogStorageStack` and `MtcComputeStack` as separate stacks (initially near-empty) per the §4 abstraction note enabling a future Pulumi port
- `npx cdk synth` produces valid CloudFormation for both stacks
- Assertions test harness (`aws-cdk-lib/assertions`) in place with at least one Template test per stack
- `infra/README.md` states the synth-only / LocalStack policy and that no real AWS account is ever targeted (§1, §5 cost notes)

## Out of Scope
- Real resource modeling (fnd-cdk-storage-stack, fnd-cdk-compute-stack)
- CI wiring (fnd-ci-infra-checks); SSM config handoff (fnd-cdk-ssm-config-handoff); any `cdk deploy` to real AWS

## Testing
- Unit: CDK assertions + snapshot tests via the project's JS test runner (§19.1 unit layer)

## Demo
`cd infra && npm ci && npm test && npx cdk synth` renders both stacks' templates to stdout.

nodes.title: make doctor: dev environment diagnostics with actionable remediation
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `make doctor` (§18.8): diagnose the dev environment and print actionable remediation so onboarding failures are self-explaining instead of mysterious.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `scripts/doctor.sh` (wired to `make doctor`) checks: Docker daemon reachable, Compose v2 present, required ports free (LocalStack 4566, admin UI 8080), rustc/cargo match `rust-toolchain.toml`, `cargo-watch` and `evcxr_repl` installed, SoftHSM2 library present, LocalStack image pulled, sufficient free disk
- Each check prints PASS/FAIL/WARN with a one-line copy-pasteable remediation command
- Exit code 0 only when all hard checks pass; WARN-only exits 0
- Runs in <10 s; no network calls beyond the local Docker socket
- Check list is data-driven so later tickets append checks in one place

## Out of Scope
- Auto-fixing the environment (doctor only diagnoses)
- CI environment validation (ci-pipeline owns its own images)

## Testing
- Unit: check functions exercised with stubbed commands (bats/shell harness)
- E2E: `make doctor` runs green in the CI container

## Demo
On a fresh machine run `make doctor` — see failing checks with copy-pasteable fixes; after applying them, all green.

nodes.title: CI check: API spec validation, breaking-change detection, codegen drift
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §22.13 required check "API spec validates (no breaking changes without explicit override)" plus a generated-code drift gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI job lints `api/admin.openapi.yaml` (same linter as the pipeline)
- Breaking-change detection (e.g., oasdiff) compares the PR spec against main and fails on breaking changes
- Override mechanism: a documented PR label (e.g., `api-breaking-approved`) allows the check to pass, with the override recorded in the job log
- Drift check: regenerate code in CI and fail if the committed generated code differs
- Job added to the documented required-checks list; negative-tested with a scratch PR that removes a response field

## Out of Scope
- The codegen pipeline itself (openapi-codegen-pipeline)
- Versioning/publishing of clients (post-v1)

## Testing
- CI-level: one passing PR, one breaking-change PR without label (fails), same PR with label (passes)

## Demo
PR renaming a `/status` response field → check fails with the oasdiff report; apply the override label → check passes.

nodes.title: CI lane for infra/: tsc, eslint, CDK assertions, cdk synth
nodes.description:
## Goal
Gate PRs touching `infra/` on the TypeScript toolchain and synth correctness, extending the §22.13 required-checks philosophy to the CDK side.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Path-filtered CI job runs on changes under `infra/`: `npm ci`, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, assertions tests, `npx cdk synth` for all stacks
- node_modules caching keeps the lane under ~5 minutes
- Job added to the documented required-checks list for infra-touching PRs
- A scratch PR with a TypeScript type error demonstrates the lane failing

## Out of Scope
- cdklocal deployment verification (fnd-cdklocal-deploy)
- Rust CI jobs (ci-pipeline)

## Testing
- CI-level: validated with one passing and one deliberately failing test PR touching `infra/`

## Demo
Open a PR touching `infra/` → `gh pr checks` shows the infra lane running and green; a docs-only PR skips it.

nodes.title: CI integration lane: cargo test --features integration against LocalStack
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add the §19.1 integration-test lane to CI: spin up the LocalStack dev environment and run feature-gated integration tests, proving the plumbing before real suites arrive.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI job starts the compose environment (LocalStack service container) and runs `cargo test --features integration` (§19.1 gating convention)
- The `integration` Cargo feature convention is documented in `docs/`
- A canary integration test ships: S3 put/get and one DDB conditional write against LocalStack
- Lane completes in under ~10 minutes and is on the documented required-checks list
- Failure of LocalStack startup fails the job with actionable logs

## Out of Scope
- Real integration suites (cloud-abstraction, storage-facade, ca-service epics)
- SoftHSM in CI (follow-up when softhsm-backend lands)

## Testing
- Integration: the canary test itself; CI-level validation via a test PR

## Demo
`gh pr checks` shows the integration lane green; locally `docker compose up -d && cargo test --features integration` passes the canary.

nodes.title: License and supply-chain policy: cargo-deny + cargo-audit as required checks
nodes.description:
## Goal
Encode the §6 licensing constraints as machine-enforced policy and add the `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` required checks of §22.13.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `deny.toml` allows MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause (plus common permissive variants as needed); explicitly denies AGPL-3.0 and other copyleft licenses per the §6 mtc-bridge constraint
- Advisory checks and duplicate-dependency checks configured in deny.toml (§22.13)
- `cargo audit` configured (advisory DB, ignore-list file empty with policy note)
- Both wired as CI jobs on every PR and added to the documented required-checks list
- Policy rationale documented in `docs/`, citing the §6 license table
- Negative test performed on a scratch branch: adding a GPL-licensed crate fails `cargo deny check`

## Out of Scope
- The repository's own LICENSE file (fnd-repo-scaffolding)
- npm-side license auditing for `infra/` (follow-up ticket if needed)

## Testing
- CI-level; local negative test with a copyleft crate demonstrates enforcement

## Demo
`cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` pass locally; `gh pr checks` shows both as required checks on a test PR.

nodes.title: OpenAPI pipeline: TypeScript client, HTML API docs, add-an-endpoint workflow doc
nodes.description:
## Goal
Extend the §17.2 codegen pipeline to emit the TypeScript client and HTML API documentation, and document the §17.5 add-an-endpoint workflow so admin UI/CLI work has a complete contract surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The existing regeneration entrypoint additionally generates a TypeScript client package from `api/admin.openapi.yaml` (§17.2); `tsc --noEmit` passes on the generated package
- HTML API docs generated (e.g., redoc/redocly build) with a single command; output location documented
- Generated TS output is committed and deterministic so drift is detectable by diff (same convention as the Rust side)
- `docs/` page documents the §17.5 workflow: update OpenAPI → regenerate → implement server method → wire into CLI command and UI handler
- One entrypoint still regenerates everything (Rust + TS + docs) in a single run

## Out of Scope
- Admin UI/CLI consumption of the clients (admin-surface epic)
- CI drift/breaking-change enforcement (fnd-ci-api-spec-check)

## Testing
- Unit: `tsc --noEmit` over the generated client; deterministic-output check by double-run diff (§19.1)

## Demo
Run `./scripts/api-gen.sh`, then open the generated HTML docs page showing `/healthz`, `/readyz`, and `/status`.

nodes.title: Repo scaffolding: README, LICENSE, editorconfig, directory conventions, CONTRIBUTING
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the top-level repo scaffolding so humans and agents share one map of the repository, reflecting the §1 premise (reference blueprint, no production deployment) and the §4 repo split.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `README.md`: project premise and explicit §1 non-goals (no production deployment, zero cloud spend), repo layout table (`crates/`, `infra/`, `api/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `tests/e2e/` per §4 and §19.1), quickstart pointer
- `LICENSE` file (permissive, consistent with the §6 licensing posture); `workspace.package.license` matches
- `.editorconfig` covering Rust, TypeScript, YAML, Markdown; `.gitignore` covers Rust target/, node_modules, cdk.out, LocalStack volumes
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` summarizing §25.3 PR practices: single reviewable/revertable unit, 200-500 line target, tests in the same PR, rollback plan in every PR description

## Out of Scope
- `AGENTS.md` / `.claude/` content (agent-harnessing epic)
- Makefile and make targets (local-dev-experience epic)

## Testing
- Docs-only: no §19.1 code layers apply; validated by review plus a markdown link check if trivially available in CI

## Demo
Repo landing page renders the README with layout table and non-goals; `cat CONTRIBUTING.md` shows the PR rules.

nodes.title: Strict Rust lint configuration (clippy pedantic/nursery/cargo, rustfmt, unwrap bans)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §22.12 linting setup so the compiler and clippy act as agent guardrails (§6, §23 rationale) from the first real crate onward.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `clippy.toml` and `rustfmt.toml` committed with strict settings per §22.12
- Workspace lint tables enable `clippy::pedantic`, `clippy::nursery`, `clippy::cargo`; `missing_docs` warned on all public items; `clippy::unwrap_used` and `clippy::expect_used` denied in non-test code (test code exempt via documented pattern)
- `unsafe_code = "forbid"` retained, with the documented exception policy for future PKCS#11 FFI crates (§22.12)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass across the workspace
- A short doc in `docs/` explains each deviation/allow and how to request one

## Out of Scope
- Custom dylint lints (fnd-dylint-custom-lints)
- CI job wiring (ci-pipeline)

## Testing
- Unit-level: lint config exercised by running clippy/fmt over the whole workspace; a deliberate `unwrap()` in a scratch branch demonstrates denial

## Demo
`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes; adding `foo.unwrap()` to library code makes it fail with the configured lint.

nodes.title: mtcctl shell completion (bash, zsh, fish)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl completion` per §17.3 so operators and agents get shell completion for the full subcommand tree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl completion bash|zsh|fish` emits a valid completion script via `clap_complete` derived from the real command tree
- Completion output goes to stdout so it can be sourced or installed (`mtcctl completion bash > ...`)
- Unsupported shell arguments produce a clear error listing supported shells
- README/CLI help documents installation per shell

## Out of Scope
- Dynamic completion of server-side values (batch IDs, indices)
- REPL tab-completion (adm-repl)

## Testing
- Unit: generation succeeds for all three shells; snapshot test that bash output contains top-level subcommands
- E2E: shell script sources the bash completion under bash and asserts no syntax error

## Demo
`source <(mtcctl completion bash)` then tab-complete `mtcctl lo<TAB>` to `log`.

nodes.title: Seed docs/architecture/ living Mermaid diagrams
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed `docs/architecture/` with living Mermaid diagrams per §23.6 so agents get GitHub-rendered visual system context without reading the full spec.

## Acceptance Criteria
- At least three Mermaid diagrams derived from the spec: system overview (components and data flow), write-path sequence (intake → batch builder → tree updater → checkpoint signer), multi-region active-passive topology
- Diagrams render on GitHub (valid Mermaid, no external assets)
- Each diagram page states its source-of-truth spec section and when it must be updated
- `make diagrams-check` validates Mermaid syntax locally (offline-capable after first tool install)

## Out of Scope
- CI drift detection between diagrams and code (foundation-infra ci-pipeline)
- Auto-generation of diagrams from code

## Testing
- E2E smoke (§19.13 spirit): `make diagrams-check` passes on the seeded diagrams and fails on a fixture with broken Mermaid syntax

## Demo
Open `docs/architecture/` on GitHub (or a local Mermaid preview) and view the rendered system-overview diagram.

nodes.title: Beads-journal integration: ticket close auto-appends journal entry
nodes.description:
## Goal
Integrate Beads with the decision journal per §23.5: closing a Beads ticket auto-appends a journal entry so future agents inherit context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make done id=<beads-id> msg="..."` (or a native beads hook if the installed version supports one) closes the ticket and appends a journal entry containing ticket ID, title, and message
- Appended entry follows the §23.7 template skeleton
- If the ticket close fails, no journal entry is written (no half-applied state)
- Workflow documented in AGENTS.md's task-completion steps

## Out of Scope
- Journal file and `make journal` target (agent-journal-tooling)
- Beads board setup (already initialized)

## Testing
- Script smoke (§19.13 spirit) against a scratch beads ticket: successful close appends the entry; forced failure leaves `docs/journal.md` untouched; shellcheck

## Demo
Create a throwaway beads ticket, run `make done id=... msg="demo"`, show the ticket closed and the journal entry appended.

nodes.title: make agent-context token-budgeted summary plus context-budget docs
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `make agent-context` and document the context-budget patterns per §23.8, giving agents a bounded orientation snapshot when relevant context exceeds the window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `make agent-context` prints a budget-bounded summary: current branch + dirty files, last N `docs/journal.md` entries, open Beads issues (via `bd` CLI), and last test results when cached
- Output stays within a configurable line/char budget even with a large journal or board (truncates with explicit markers)
- Runs offline; degrades gracefully when journal or beads data is absent
- PR 2: `docs/context-budget.md` documents the four §23.8 strategies — skill-driven scoping, `make agent-context`, Beads ticket file-scoping, scoped test runs — with concrete command examples; AGENTS.md links to it

## Out of Scope
- `make agent-precheck` (agent-inner-loop-targets)
- Exact token counting — line/char budget approximation is sufficient

## Testing
- Script smoke (§19.13 spirit): budget enforcement against an oversized fixture journal; E2E: run in the repo and assert all sections present; shellcheck

## Demo
`make agent-context` prints branch, dirty files, recent journal entries, and open beads within the stated budget.

nodes.title: Hierarchical README convention: template plus per-crate READMEs
nodes.description:
## Goal
Establish the hierarchical README convention per §23.6: root README points at subsystem READMEs; each crate README states purpose, public API, internal structure, and gotchas — cheap context before agents dive into code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Subsystem README template checked in with the four §23.6 sections (purpose / public API / internal structure / gotchas)
- Every existing crate gains a README following the template
- Root README gains a subsystem map linking to each crate README
- Convention documented so new-crate checklists (rules/AGENTS.md) require a README
- A make target lints README presence for every crate and fails if one is missing

## Out of Scope
- `CODEMAP.md` generated navigation (agent-codemap-generator)
- READMEs for non-crate directories (cdk/, docs/) — follow-up

## Testing
- Script smoke (§19.13 spirit): README-presence lint passes on the workspace and fails against a fixture crate without one; markdown lint

## Demo
From the root README, click through to any crate README and see the four template sections filled in.

nodes.title: Pre-built search targets: find-tests, find-callers, find-impl, find-todo
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the §23.6 pre-built search affordances so agents locate tests, callers, implementations, and TODOs without burning tokens reading files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make find-tests path=X` lists test files/functions relevant to a path
- `make find-callers symbol=Y` lists call sites; `make find-impl iface=Z` lists trait implementations
- `make find-todo` lists TODO/FIXME comments with `file:line`
- All targets are ripgrep-based, run offline, and emit `file:line`-prefixed output agents can consume directly
- Documented in AGENTS.md's "where to find what" section (follow-up edit)

## Out of Scope
- Semantic/LSP-accurate indexing — rg heuristics are acceptable at this repo size

## Testing
- Script smoke (§19.13 spirit): each target run against known workspace symbols returns the expected hits; empty-result and missing-arg cases exit cleanly; shellcheck

## Demo
`make find-impl iface=<any workspace trait>` prints each implementation location; `make find-todo` lists open TODOs.

nodes.title: MtcComputeStack skeleton: Fargate service + Lambda placeholders per component table
nodes.description:
## Goal
Skeleton `MtcComputeStack` reflecting the §5/§7 component split: ECS Fargate for the write path, Lambda placeholders for read/event components — synth-only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Stack accepts storage references via props typed as `aws-cdk-lib` interfaces (`IBucket`, `ITable`) exported by `MtcLogStorageStack`; no hand-rolled types shared across stacks (§4)
- Placeholder Fargate task definition + service construct for the CA service write path (§5)
- Placeholder Lambda constructs for proof-server, self-auditor, revocation-processor, pruning-worker, orphan-cleanup (§7 component table)
- Assertions verify each construct synthesizes with expected logical IDs; `npx cdk synth` clean
- Placeholders clearly marked; container image / Lambda asset wiring stubbed with dummy assets

## Out of Scope
- Real container images and Lambda code (ca-service, read-path, observability epics)
- ALB/Route53/CloudFront details (read-path and multi-region epics); real deploys

## Testing
- Unit: CDK assertions (§19.1)

## Demo
`npx cdk synth MtcCompute*` lists one Fargate service and five placeholder Lambdas matching §7.

nodes.title: TS-to-Rust config handoff: SSM parameter publication convention and constructs
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §4 config-handoff decision (SSM Parameter Store + env vars) as a documented naming contract plus a small CDK helper construct, keeping the TS↔Rust boundary at the deployment edge with no type sharing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Parameter naming convention (e.g., `/mtc/<env>/<component>/<key>`) documented in `docs/` as the contract Rust services read via figment layering (§4 config row)
- CDK helper construct publishes stack outputs as `AWS::SSM::Parameter` resources under the convention
- `MtcLogStorageStack` publishes its bucket name and table name via the helper; assertions verify the exact parameter names and values in the synthesized template
- Contract doc lists the corresponding env-var override names for local dev (LocalStack endpoints, §18)

## Out of Scope
- Rust-side config loading (service epics)
- Compute-stack outputs (wired when real resources land in that stack)
- Secrets handling (HSM credentials belong to cloud-abstraction/ca-service epics)

## Testing
- Unit: CDK assertions on synthesized SSM parameters (§19.1)

## Demo
`npx cdk synth` shows `AWS::SSM::Parameter` resources whose names match the documented contract.

nodes.title: MtcLogStorageStack: S3 log bucket + DynamoDB coordination table modeled in CDK
nodes.description:
## Goal
Model the storage layer in `MtcLogStorageStack` per §8: the immutable log bucket (S3 with versioning + Object Lock) and the DynamoDB coordination table — validated purely via synth assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- S3 bucket construct with versioning and Object Lock enabled, lifecycle/retention surface configurable via props, matching the §8.1 layout and S3 invariants (§8 "S3 invariants")
- Bucket prefix layout of §8.1 documented alongside the construct
- DynamoDB table construct matching the §8.2 schema (key schema, attributes, PITR enabled); Global Tables replication and CRR/RTC expressed as configurable props only — never deployed (§1 non-goals)
- Assertions tests verify: ObjectLockEnabled, versioning status, table key schema, PITR
- `npx cdk synth MtcLogStorage*` clean

## Out of Scope
- Runtime access code (cloud-aws backend, storage-facade epics)
- Actual multi-region replication behavior (multi-region epic); real deploys

## Testing
- Unit: CDK assertions on the synthesized template (§19.1)

## Demo
`cd infra && npm test` green; `npx cdk synth` output shows the bucket with `ObjectLockEnabled: true` and the DDB `KeySchema` from §8.2.

nodes.title: Deploy MtcLogStorageStack to LocalStack via cdklocal with smoke assertions
nodes.description:
## Goal
Validate the CDK storage stack beyond synth by deploying it to LocalStack with `cdklocal`, honoring the §1 non-goal of zero real-AWS spend while proving templates are actually deployable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `scripts/cdklocal-deploy.sh` bootstraps and deploys `MtcLogStorageStack` to a running LocalStack
- Smoke assertions after deploy: bucket exists with versioning + Object Lock, table exists with the §8.2 key schema
- Script is idempotent (re-run succeeds without manual cleanup)
- Known LocalStack emulation gaps (e.g., Object Lock fidelity, Global Tables) documented in `infra/README.md`

## Out of Scope
- Compute stack deployment (no real images yet)
- CI wiring (optional follow-up); any real AWS account usage

## Testing
- Integration: deploy + assertion script against LocalStack (§19.1)

## Demo
`docker compose up -d && ./scripts/cdklocal-deploy.sh` then `awslocal s3api get-object-lock-configuration --bucket <log-bucket>` shows Object Lock enabled.

nodes.title: Custom dylint lint infrastructure + no-direct-time lint
nodes.description:
## Goal
Stand up the custom dylint lint infrastructure of §22.12 with the first repo-specific lint: forbid `SystemTime::now()` / `Instant::now()` / `chrono::Utc::now()` outside test code, enforcing the injected `Clock` trait rule (§4, §22.11).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dylint lint library under `lints/` with pinned toolchain compatible with the workspace
- `no_direct_time` lint flags direct time calls in non-`#[cfg(test)]` code with a diagnostic pointing to the `Clock` trait (§22.11)
- UI tests cover: violation in lib code (fails), usage in test module (allowed), Clock-trait usage (allowed)
- Runner script executes dylint across the workspace; CI job added and on the documented required-checks list
- `docs/` page explains how to add the next custom lint

## Out of Scope
- Additional repo-specific lints (future tickets as patterns emerge)
- The `Clock` trait itself (core-mtc-library epic)

## Testing
- Unit: dylint UI tests (§19.1); CI-level validation on a scratch PR containing `SystemTime::now()`

## Demo
Add `SystemTime::now()` to a library target → dylint fails locally and in CI with the Clock-trait guidance message.

nodes.title: Create crates/mtc with domain newtypes and core spec primitive types
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create the `crates/mtc` library crate and domain newtypes per spec sections 22.1 and 22.5: `Index`, `TreeSize`, `Epoch`, `HashOutput([u8; 32])`, and phantom-typed string IDs (`Id<T>` with `LogTag`/`BatchTag` giving `LogId`/`BatchId`), plus shared library error types via `thiserror` (section 28).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/mtc` builds in the workspace with lints per section 22.12; no vendor SDK types anywhere (section 22.8)
- Derives per section 22.1: integer newtypes are `Copy + Clone + PartialEq + Eq + Hash + Debug`; string IDs are `Clone` but not `Copy`
- `Id<T>` phantom-type pattern per section 22.5: `LogId` and `BatchId` are distinct compile-time types, identical at runtime
- trybuild compile-fail test proving an `Epoch` cannot be passed where a `TreeSize` is expected (section 22.1 guarantee)
- Error enums use `thiserror`; no `unwrap()` in library code
- Rustdoc on every public item citing the section-2 concept it models

## Out of Scope
- Wire-format serialization (mtc-serialization)
- Tree operations (tree-primitives); cloud/storage types (cloud-abstraction epic)

## Testing
- Unit tests; trybuild compile-fail tests (spec 19.1 unit layer)

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc types` passes; `cargo doc -p mtc --open` shows documented newtype module.

nodes.title: Clock trait, SystemClock, and thread-safe FakeClock crate
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the injected `Clock` trait, `SystemClock`, and a thread-safe `FakeClock` with controllable advancement (§22.11) — the foundation for time travel (§18.4) and deterministic time-dependent tests across all epics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New crate `crates/clock`: `pub trait Clock: Send + Sync { fn now(&self) -> SystemTime; }` plus `SystemClock` and `FakeClock`
- `FakeClock::advance(Duration)` and `set(SystemTime)`; monotonicity enforced (never goes backward); `Arc<FakeClock>` shareable across threads
- Optional tokio feature: fake-clock-driven sleep/interval helpers for cadence-based loops
- Clippy `disallowed-methods` denies `SystemTime::now()`/`Instant::now()` outside `crates/clock` and test code (§22.12, rule `no-systemtime-now-in-prod` §23.2)
- Docs show the injection pattern (`Arc<dyn Clock>`, §22.7) with a worked example

## Out of Scope
- Migrating other crates' call sites (adopting epics own that)
- Admin API control endpoints (`dev-time-advance`)

## Testing
- Unit: advancement, monotonicity, cross-thread visibility
- Loom: concurrent advance/now interleavings on FakeClock internals
- Property: a sequence of advances yields the same final `now()` regardless of interleaving order

## Demo
`cargo test -p clock`; doc example shows a batch-cadence loop firing instantly under FakeClock instead of waiting wall-clock time.

nodes.title: TLS-presentation serialization framework with bounded parsing
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the wire-format codec framework for spec structures (section 19.3 risk area): `TlsSerialize`/`TlsParse` traits with generic `<W: Write>` writers (section 22.7 hot-path row), and bounded readers that never panic on untrusted bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Primitives: u8/u16/u24/u32, fixed-size opaque, variable-length vectors with length prefixes per TLS presentation language
- Parser refuses inputs claiming impossible sizes (no unbounded allocation) and has bounded recursion depth (section 19.3 asserted properties)
- Parsing is single-pass and time-bounded by input length, not content (section 19.3)
- Parse of arbitrary bytes returns `Err`, never panics: initial proptest over random byte strings
- Round-trip helper macro `assert_roundtrip!` reused by every subsequent spec-type ticket (section 19.2: parse(serialize(x)) == x)
- Codec errors are structured (`thiserror`), reporting offset and expected/found

## Out of Scope
- Per-type codecs for Checkpoint/entries/tiles (their own tickets)
- Fuzz targets (mtclib-fuzz-targets); serde/JSON for admin API (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property per sections 19.1-19.3 layer 1

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc serialization` shows round-trip and malformed-input rejection tests passing.

nodes.title: Merkle tree core: domain-separated hashing, append, root, subtrees
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the Merkle tree math (spec section 2): generic `Hasher` trait with SHA-256 default using static dispatch per section 22.7 (hot path), leaf/interior hash domain separation, empty-tree root constant, in-memory tree construction, append, root computation, and subtree decomposition of ranges [start, end).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `<H: Hasher>` generic on tree ops per section 22.7 table (tree updater hash function row); SHA-256 via RustCrypto (section 28)
- Leaf hashes and interior-node hashes use distinct domain-separation prefixes; property test that they never collide (sections 19.2, 19.6)
- Empty tree root hash is well-defined and constant, locked by a unit test (section 19.6)
- Two trees built from the same leaf sequence produce identical roots (section 19.2); appending never changes existing node hashes
- Property test on subtree decomposition of any [start, end): returned subtrees are disjoint, cover exactly [start, end), and number at most 2*log2(tree size)
- PR split: (1) hashing + domain separation + empty root; (2) tree build/append/root; (3) subtree ranges

## Out of Scope
- Inclusion/consistency proofs (mtclib-inclusion-proofs); tiles (mtclib-tiles); range pruning (mtclib-tree-pruning)
- Persistence of tree data (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property (proptest) per sections 19.1-19.2; Kani harnesses land in mtclib-kani-harnesses

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example tree_demo` builds a 1000-leaf tree and prints its root hash deterministically.

nodes.title: Path-filtered cargo kani CI gate for critical-path crates
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the conditional §22.13 required check: `cargo kani` runs for PRs touching critical-path crates, so formal verification proofs gate exactly the code they protect (§19.12, §22).

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI config holds an explicit list of critical-path crates/paths (initially tree primitives; lease/epoch crates added by the multi-region epic later)
- Job installs a pinned Kani version and runs `cargo kani` for the affected crates only when those paths change
- PRs not touching critical paths skip the job (and it does not block them)
- Runtime budget and the procedure for adding a crate to the critical list documented in `docs/`
- Validated against the first merged Kani harness

## Out of Scope
- Writing Kani harnesses (core-mtc-library and multi-region epics own their proofs)
- Loom/Shuttle CI lanes (testing-infrastructure epic)

## Testing
- Kani: executes existing harnesses; CI-level validation with one critical-path PR and one unrelated PR

## Demo
PR touching a critical crate → `gh pr checks` shows the kani job running proofs; a docs-only PR shows it skipped.

nodes.title: Checkpoint type with typestate builder, serialization, sign and verify
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `Checkpoint` — the signed (tree size, root hash) commitment (section 2) — with the section 22.2 typestate builder, TLS-presentation serialization, and sign/verify over the mtclib-signing abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `CheckpointBuilder` typestate per section 22.2: `.build()` unreachable until log_id, root_hash, tree_size, signed_at are set; trybuild compile-fail test proves it
- Serialization round-trip proptest exactly as sketched in section 19.3 Layer 1 (`checkpoint_roundtrip`)
- Parse of arbitrary bytes returns Err, never panics; size fields bounded (section 19.3)
- Sign via any `SignatureScheme`; verify rejects wrong signature, wrong key, mutated tree_size or root_hash
- Checkpoint for the empty tree is well-defined and constant-rooted (section 19.6)
- PR split: (1) type + builder + serialization; (2) sign/verify + negative tests

## Out of Scope
- HSM-backed checkpoint signer service (ca-service epic, checkpoint-signer anchor)
- Checkpoint storage/publication (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property + trybuild per sections 19.1-19.3; crypto invariants per section 19.6

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example checkpoint_demo` builds, signs, serializes, re-parses, and verifies a checkpoint.

nodes.title: Spec conformance suite scaffolding with clean-room test vectors
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the section 19.4 conformance scaffolding: a versioned test-vector file format, a harness that auto-discovers and runs vectors, and an initial set of clean-room vectors derived from the draft text (section 6 clean-room constraints), pinned to draft revision -03 (section 28 spec-tracking workflow).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Vector format (JSON with hex fields) carrying: draft revision, spec section reference, input bytes, expected output/root/error
- Harness discovers vectors under `crates/mtc/tests/vectors/`; adding a vector file requires no Rust changes
- Initial vectors: empty-tree root, small-tree roots (1..=8 leaves), null_entry bytes, entry round-trip, checkpoint round-trip, inclusion proof verify (positive and negative), MTCProof end-to-end verify
- Failing vector output names the vector file and spec section for fast triage
- Vectors authored from spec text, not derived from mtc-bridge output (AGPL boundary, section 6)
- PR split: (1) format + harness; (2) initial vector corpus

## Out of Scope
- Cross-language differential oracle (mtclib-differential-go-oracle)
- CI gate wiring (testing-infra epic); daily draft-diff job (section 28, foundation/testing-infra)

## Testing
- Conformance layer per section 19.4; vectors double as fuzz corpus seeds

## Demo
After merge: `make conformance` runs the vector suite green and prints a per-section coverage summary.

nodes.title: cargo-fuzz targets for every externally-parseable wire format
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create the per-format fuzz targets required by section 19.3: unstructured (Layer 2) targets for each externally-parseable type owned by this epic, a structured (Layer 3) `arbitrary`-driven target for post-parse proof verification, and seed corpora under `fuzz/corpus/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cargo fuzz` targets: `parse_checkpoint`, `parse_log_entry`, `parse_tile`, `parse_mtc_proof`, `parse_trust_anchor_id` — each asserts no panic, no UB, no excessive allocation (section 19.3 Layer 2 pattern)
- Structured target: `verify_proof` fed by an `arbitrary`-derived semi-valid proof input reusing the mtclib-proptest-suite generators; verification must not panic (section 19.3 Layer 3)
- Seed corpora checked in at `fuzz/corpus/<target>/`, seeded from serialized valid examples and proptest regression seeds (conformance vectors folded in as they land); corpus-management flow from section 19.3 documented (minimized crashers become permanent unit-test regressions)
- `make fuzz TARGET=<name> DURATION=60` runs any target locally; all targets survive a 60s local smoke run
- PR split: (1) fuzz crate + parse targets; (2) structured verify target + corpora + make target

## Out of Scope
- CI/nightly fuzzing orchestration (testing-infra epic, per boundary rules)
- `RevocationList` target (revocation epic) and ACME request body target (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Fuzz layer per section 19.3; regression fixtures feed the unit layer

## Demo
After merge: `make fuzz TARGET=parse_checkpoint DURATION=60` runs clean on a laptop.

nodes.title: Inclusion and consistency proof generation and verification
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement inclusion proofs (sibling hashes from leaf to subtree root, section 2) and consistency proofs between tree sizes, including generation and verification plus their wire formats. This is the math the section 12.1 relying-party flow and Phase 4 read path build on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- For any tree size N and any leaf 0 <= i < N, generated inclusion proof verifies (section 19.2)
- Consistency proofs verify between any two tree sizes N1 <= N2 (section 19.2)
- Appending preserves all previously-valid inclusion proofs (section 19.2)
- Verification recomputes leaf-to-root path with domain-separated hashing and compares against expected root
- Negative tests: wrong leaf index, tampered sibling, truncated proof, proof for size > tree all fail cleanly
- Proof wire format round-trips via the mtc-serialization framework

## Out of Scope
- Checkpoint signature verification (mtclib-checkpoint); landmark verification (mtclib-landmarks)
- Proof-serving Lambda and tile fetching (read-path epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property per section 19.2; Kani coverage lands in mtclib-kani-harnesses

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example prove_and_verify` issues a proof for a random leaf and verifies it.

nodes.title: First Kani harnesses for critical tree primitives
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add the first Kani model-checking harnesses for tree primitives per sections 19.12 and 24 Phase 1: absence of panics, integer overflow, and assertion violations in hashing, append, and the inclusion-proof generate/verify pair.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Harnesses under `crates/mtc/proofs/` (convention per section 23.7 journal example): (1) leaf/interior hashing and append never panic or overflow for bounded inputs; (2) for any leaf in any bounded-size tree, generate-then-verify inclusion proof succeeds (section 19.12: proof verifies for any leaf in any tree size); (3) domain-separated leaf and interior encodings are disjoint for bounded inputs
- Each harness documents its unwind/size bounds and why they are representative
- `make kani-mtc` runs all harnesses locally and passes
- Harness runtime kept laptop-feasible (minutes, not hours) via bounds
- PR split: (1) no-panic/overflow harnesses; (2) proof round-trip harness + docs

## Out of Scope
- Lease/epoch Kani verification (multi-region epic, section 19.12)
- CI integration of Kani runs (testing-infra epic)

## Testing
- Kani layer per section 19.12; complements property tests, does not replace them

## Demo
After merge: `make kani-mtc` completes with all harnesses verified; README snippet shows sample output.

nodes.title: TBSCertificateLogEntry, claims, and null_entry
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `TBSCertificateLogEntry` per the draft (section 2: per-cert log entry using public key hash, not raw key), its claim/assertion types (DNS names, IP addresses), the spec-defined `null_entry` placeholder that fills gaps from abandoned batches (sections 2, 13.3), and entry-to-leaf hashing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `TBSCertificateLogEntry` holds a public-key hash newtype; API makes storing a raw key unrepresentable
- Typestate builder for entry construction per section 22.2 pattern; incomplete build is a compile error (trybuild test)
- `null_entry` is a well-defined constant whose serialization matches the draft; unit test locks its bytes
- TLS-presentation round-trip via mtc-serialization for entries and claims (section 19.2); malformed bytes return Err, never panic
- Entry-to-leaf-hash uses the domain-separated leaf hashing from tree-primitives

## Out of Scope
- Batch assembly and issuance pipeline (ca-service epic); EntryIntake adapter seam (ca-service)
- X.509/ACME mapping of claims (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property + trybuild per sections 19.1-19.2; fuzz target lands in mtclib-fuzz-targets

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc log_entry` passes; example prints the hex leaf hash of a sample entry and of null_entry.

nodes.title: MTCProof: certificate assembly and end-to-end verification path
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `MTCProof` — the certificate as entry plus inclusion proof to a signed checkpoint (section 2) — and the full relying-party verification path of section 12.1: recompute leaf hash, walk the inclusion path, compare roots, verify checkpoint signature.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `MTCProof` composes TBSCertificateLogEntry + inclusion path + checkpoint reference; wire format round-trips via mtc-serialization
- `verify()` implements the section 12.1 flow and returns structured errors distinguishing bad-entry, bad-path, root-mismatch, and bad-signature
- Property test: proofs assembled for any leaf of any tree size verify against that tree's signed checkpoint (section 19.2)
- Negative tests: swapped entries, path from a different leaf, checkpoint from a different tree all fail
- Serialized proof size test documenting the ~736-byte order of magnitude claim from section 2

## Out of Scope
- Signatureless/landmark verification (mtclib-landmarks)
- Proof-server Lambda, CloudFront, and the standalone verification-library packaging (read-path epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property per section 19.2; differential coverage arrives via mtclib-differential-go-oracle

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example issue_and_verify` builds a tree, signs a checkpoint, assembles an MTCProof for a leaf, and verifies it end-to-end.

nodes.title: Consolidated proptest invariant suite and Arbitrary impls for all spec types
nodes.description:
## Goal
Consolidate the section 19.2 Merkle/serialization invariant list and the library-level section 19.6 crypto invariants into a named property-test suite, with proptest `Arbitrary` implementations for every spec type and an extended-iteration profile (10,000+ cases, section 19.3 Layer 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- One named property test per section 19.2 bullet: inclusion proofs for all (N, i); consistency proofs; append preserves proofs; identical leaves give identical roots; pruning a range (via mtclib-tree-pruning) keeps unpruned proofs verifying; round-trip for every spec type; leaf/interior hash domain separation
- Section 19.6 library invariants: same tree size implies same root; empty-tree root constant; domain-separation prefixes consistent
- `Arbitrary` impls for Checkpoint, TBSCertificateLogEntry, Tile, MTCProof, TrustAnchorId, reusable by fuzz targets
- `PROPTEST_CASES` env-driven extended profile; `make proptest-extended` runs 10k+ cases locally
- Failure seeds persisted and replayable; regression seeds checked in

## Out of Scope
- CI job wiring for extended runs (testing-infra epic)
- HSM-related 19.6 invariants (cloud-abstraction epic)

## Testing
- Property layer per sections 19.2-19.3

## Demo
After merge: `make proptest-extended` completes with all invariants green; `cargo test -p mtc properties` runs the fast profile.

nodes.title: Signature scheme abstraction plus ECDSA P-256 (v1 algorithm)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Define the algorithm-agnostic signing abstraction (`SignatureScheme` trait, algorithm identifiers, `Signature`/`VerifyingKey` newtypes) and implement ECDSA P-256 via RustCrypto as the v1 algorithm (section 24 Phase 1, section 28).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Traits take and return domain types only, no vendor types (section 22.8); designed so the cloud `Hsm` trait can back a signer later without changing callers
- Algorithm identifier registry matching the draft's codepoints; unknown IDs parse to a structured error
- PR split: (1) traits + algorithm IDs + newtypes; (2) `p256` implementation with tests
- ECDSA P-256 sign/verify round-trip tests; verify rejects tampered message, tampered signature, and wrong key
- Known-answer tests from published P-256 test vectors
- `#[must_use]` on verification results per section 22.10

## Out of Scope
- ML-DSA (mtclib-ml-dsa-quxpqc); HSM-backed signing (cloud-abstraction epic, checkpoint-signer)
- Checkpoint signing flow (mtclib-checkpoint)

## Testing
- Unit + known-answer vectors per section 19.1; crypto invariants per section 19.6

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc signing` passes including KATs; example signs and verifies a sample payload with a fresh P-256 key.

nodes.title: Tile structures per tlog-tiles: build, index, and serialize 256-leaf tiles
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the `Tile` type per the tlog-tiles format (sections 2, 28): fixed 256-leaf chunks of the tree, tile coordinates (level, index, partial width), building tiles from leaves/nodes, extracting hashes, and computing which tile set an inclusion path needs (supports section 12.2 step 3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Tile` type with coordinate newtypes; partial (right-edge) tiles handled correctly
- Tile bytes serialize/parse via mtc-serialization; round-trip property test; parse of truncated/oversized tile bytes returns Err, never panics
- Function mapping a (leaf index, tree size) inclusion path to the minimal set of tile coordinates
- Tile coordinate to canonical path-string formatting per tlog-tiles convention, matching the section 8.1 layout (e.g. tiles/000/000.tile)
- Rebuilding tree hashes from a full tile set reproduces the root computed directly from leaves (cross-check test)

## Out of Scope
- Storing/fetching tiles in S3 and the LRU tile cache (storage-facade epic, section 8)
- Proof-server tile fetch logic (read-path epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property per section 19.2; fuzz target lands in mtclib-fuzz-targets

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example tiles_demo` builds a 1000-leaf tree, emits its tiles, and reconstructs the root from tiles alone.

nodes.title: Spec conformance suite runner and test-vector infrastructure
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the clean-room spec conformance suite (spec 19.4, roadmap Phase 1): a test-vector format plus a runner that serves as an ongoing CI gate for MTC wire-format and verification behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `conformance/vectors/` directory with a documented JSON+hex fixture format for spec structures (checkpoints, proofs, entries) and a README describing how to add vectors
- Runner discovers every vector and asserts parse/serialize/verify expectations, including must-reject vectors with expected error class
- Failure output identifies vector ID and shows a structural diff, not just an assertion failure
- Suite runs on every PR under `cargo test --all-features` (required check per 22.13)
- Seeded with clean-room vectors: checkpoint and inclusion-proof happy paths plus at least 3 invalid cases

## Out of Scope
- Cross-language differential comparison (test-differential-runner)
- Vectors for structures not yet implemented (added by component tickets)

## Testing
- Unit tests for the vector loader; the suite itself is the conformance layer (19.4)

## Demo
`make conformance` prints per-vector pass/fail and total counts.

nodes.title: Differential test runner (Rust vs Go reference) with nightly CI job
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the differential runner comparing our parser/verifier against the Go reference shim (spec 19.3 Layer 4, 19.5): agreement on accept, agreement on reject, structural equality of parsed forms — run nightly in CI due to cross-language tooling cost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Runner semantics per 19.3 Layer 4: both accept -> assert structural equality (canonical JSON compare); both reject -> pass; disagreement -> fail with the offending input persisted
- Input sources: conformance vectors, proptest-generated cases, and `fuzz/corpus/` entries when present
- Dual-path verification hook per 19.5: verify the same proof via our logic and via the shim, fail on disagreement
- Nightly scheduled CI job with mismatch inputs uploaded as artifacts; `make differential INPUT=<file>` reproduces locally
