## Out of Scope
- Building the Go shim (test-go-ref-shim)
- Per-issuance differential checks inside the CA service (component epics reuse this runner)

## Testing
- Unit tests for the comparator; the suite itself is the differential layer (19.5)

## Demo
`make differential` runs the full corpus locally against the built shim and prints agree/disagree counts.

nodes.title: cargo-fuzz scaffolding, corpus management, and CI wiring
nodes.description:
## Goal
Stand up the unstructured fuzzing layer (spec 19.3 Layer 2) and its corpus-management workflow: `fuzz/` workspace, checked-in corpora, crash-to-regression promotion, and CI jobs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo-fuzz `fuzz/` setup with one exemplar target `parse_checkpoint` asserting no panic on arbitrary bytes, plus a documented template for the one-target-per-parseable-type convention (Checkpoint, MTCProof, RevocationList, TBSCertificateLogEntry, Tile, ACME body — remaining targets ship with component epics)
- `fuzz/corpus/<target>/` checked into the repo, seeded with hand-crafted seeds plus conformance vectors once available (19.3 corpus management)
- Documented promotion workflow: minimized crash inputs become permanent unit-test regression fixtures
- CI: PR job replays corpus (no exploration) per target; nightly job fuzzes each target for a fixed budget with minimized crash artifacts uploaded
- Allocation/RSS limits and per-input timeout configured so unbounded-allocation and unbounded-depth inputs fail (19.3 asserted properties)

## Out of Scope
- Structured `arbitrary`-bridge targets (test-structured-fuzz)
- Fuzz targets for types owned by other epics

## Testing
- Fuzz (self); unit test proving the exemplar corpus replays clean

## Demo
`cargo +nightly fuzz run parse_checkpoint -- -runs=10000` completes with no crashes.

nodes.title: Go reference shim wrapping bwesterb/mtc for cross-language testing
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide a small Go CLI shim around `bwesterb/mtc` exposing parse/verify subcommands, the invocation helper on the Rust side, and the CI build step — the foundation for differential testing per spec 19.3 Layer 4 and 19.5 (refer to the Go code, never copy it, per roadmap Phase 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tools/mtc-go-shim/` Go module with subcommands `parse-checkpoint`, `parse-proof`, `verify-inclusion`: bytes on stdin, canonical JSON on stdout, nonzero exit plus machine-readable error on reject
- `bwesterb/mtc` version pinned in go.mod; `make go-shim` builds locally
- CI job builds and caches the shim binary for downstream jobs
- Rust wrapper in mtc-testutil spawns the shim with a timeout and typed result (the `call_go_binary` seam from 19.3 Layer 4)
- Ships as 2 PRs: (1) Go shim + CI build/cache, (2) Rust invocation wrapper

## Out of Scope
- The differential runner and mismatch handling (test-differential-runner)
- Nightly job wiring (test-differential-runner)

## Testing
- Unit test for the Rust wrapper; integration test round-tripping one known vector through the shim

## Demo
`make go-shim && echo <hex-vector> | tools/mtc-go-shim/bin/shim parse-checkpoint` emits parsed JSON.

nodes.title: Kani CI integration with critical-path gating
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire `cargo kani` into CI per spec 19.12 and the 22.13 required-check rule (critical-path PRs must pass proofs), with conventions and a sentinel proof so component epics (tree primitives, lease/epoch, write-path linearization) add harnesses that run unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI job installs a pinned Kani release with toolchain caching and runs `cargo kani` across crates opted in via a documented marker
- Path-filter gating per 22.13: the check is required only when critical-path crates change; a nightly job runs all proofs unconditionally
- Sentinel harness in mtc-testutil (`#[cfg(kani)]` module, small provable property with unwind bound) proves the wiring end-to-end and stays green
- Conventions doc: harness placement in `#[cfg(kani)]` modules, naming scheme, unwind-bound annotations, and how to opt a crate in

## Out of Scope
- Real Kani harnesses (core-mtc-library and multi-region epics own their proofs per 19.12)
- Loom/Shuttle wiring (test-loom-shuttle-ci)

## Testing
- Kani (sentinel harness); CI-config validation on a critical-path-touching PR

## Demo
Open a PR touching an opted-in crate: the `cargo kani` check appears and passes; `cargo kani -p mtc-testutil` reproduces locally.

nodes.title: Shared test-support crate with fixtures and proptest conventions
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/mtc-testutil`: shared fixture builders, deterministic RNG/temp-dir helpers, and the proptest conventions layer required by spec 19.2 and 19.3 Layer 1, so component epics write property tests against one common toolkit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New dev-dependency crate `crates/mtc-testutil` with seeded-RNG helper, temp-dir/env helpers, and fixture builders for checkpoints, log entries, and tree-leaf sequences (built on core-mtc-types)
- Shared proptest strategy helpers and a documented `Arbitrary` convention (impls live with each spec type behind a `testing` feature flag)
- CI wiring runs proptest with extended iterations for spec types (PROPTEST_CASES >= 10,000 per 19.3 Layer 1) while local default stays fast (<30s unit budget per 19.1)
- `proptest-regressions/` seed files checked in; convention documented in crate docs
- One exemplar property test (round-trip on a core type) exercising the helpers

## Out of Scope
- Component property tests themselves (ship with component tickets per epic boundary)
- Fuzz targets and corpus (test-fuzz-harness)
- Fault-injection wrappers (test-fault-injection)

## Testing
- Unit tests for helpers; exemplar property test per 19.2

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-testutil`, then `PROPTEST_CASES=10000 cargo test` showing extended-iteration mode.

nodes.title: Seed docs/patterns/ pattern library and docs/anti-patterns.md
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed the pattern library (`docs/patterns/`) and anti-patterns doc (`docs/anti-patterns.md`) per §23.5 so agents reference canonical patterns instead of pattern-matching to arbitrary code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `docs/patterns/` with a pattern template plus at least three seeded patterns referencing real merged code: newtype construction/validation (§22.2), injected `Clock` usage, thiserror-for-libs / eyre-for-bins error discipline (§22, §23.2)
- Each pattern lists: intent, path-referenced example, when to use, pitfalls
- PR 2: `docs/anti-patterns.md` seeded with at least six entries (`SystemTime::now()` in prod code, `unwrap()` outside tests, SDK types in domain signatures, type aliases for identifiers, swallowed errors, `Arc<dyn Trait>` on hot paths), each with a "do this instead" pointer
- Cited file paths verified by a path-existence lint (same mechanism as skill-lint)

## Out of Scope
- Task-oriented skills (`.claude/skills/`); rule text (agent-claude-rules-seed)

## Testing
- No §19.1 code layers; markdown lint plus path-existence check for all cited examples

## Demo
Open `docs/patterns/` and the newtype pattern; every cited path resolves to real code in the workspace.

nodes.title: Seed skills: add-fixture.md and update-spec-version.md
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed the two conformance-lifecycle skills from §23.1: `add-fixture.md` (capture and document a test fixture) and `update-spec-version.md` (track a new MTC draft revision).

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `add-fixture.md` — Goal, the 3–5 files involved in the conformance/test-vector suite, the capture-and-document pattern, common pitfalls (undocumented provenance, fixtures not tied to a draft revision)
- PR 2: `update-spec-version.md` — steps to bump the pinned draft revision, rerun conformance and differential suites, and file Beads tickets for non-trivial divergences per the `spec-pin-and-track` rule (§23.2)
- Both pass `make skill-lint` (required sections, existing file paths)
- Each skill fits the ~5-file scoping budget (§23.8)

## Out of Scope
- The conformance/differential suites themselves (testing-infrastructure epic)
- Rule text for spec-pin-and-track (agent-claude-rules-seed)

## Testing
- `make skill-lint`; a manual dry-run of each skill's steps recorded in the PR description (§19.13 spirit)

## Demo
Follow `add-fixture.md` to add a scratch fixture end-to-end, run the suite, then revert.

nodes.title: make repl: evcxr Rust REPL with workspace crates pre-loaded
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship `make repl` (§18.6, §18.8): an `evcxr` Rust REPL with workspace crates pre-loaded for ad-hoc human exploration (OQ-10 resolution: evcxr provided; CLI REPL is primary for agents).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make repl` verifies/installs `evcxr_repl` and launches it with an init file (`scripts/repl-init.evcxr`)
- Init pre-loads core workspace crates via `:dep` path dependencies and a prelude importing common types (tree, serialization, clock)
- Startup banner shows how to build a toy tree and compute an inclusion proof in ~3 lines
- `scripts/check-repl-init.sh` fails if the init references a crate missing from the workspace (kept honest as crates are added)
- Documented in `docs/dev-environment.md` with known evcxr limitations

## Out of Scope
- `mtcctl repl` CLI shell (`dev-repl-cli`)
- Jupyter kernel setup

## Testing
- Unit: none (glue)
- E2E: nightly-lane CI job evaluates the init file headlessly and runs one tree-building snippet

## Demo
`make repl` → paste the banner snippet → see a Merkle root computed interactively.

nodes.title: Rustdoc, spec cross-reference map, and clean-room provenance docs for crates/mtc
nodes.description:
## Goal
Document the mtc crate as a first-class deliverable (section 25.7 dev-experience tickets): rustdoc with doctest examples on every public item, a README mapping each type to its draft section, and a clean-room provenance statement per section 6.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `#![warn(missing_docs)]` raised to deny in crate lints; `cargo doc -p mtc` completes with zero warnings
- Doctests for the three core flows: build tree and compute root; assemble and verify an MTCProof; sign and verify a checkpoint — all passing under `cargo test --doc -p mtc`
- README table mapping every public type to its section-2 concept and draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs -03 section, with pinned revision stated (section 28 spec-tracking workflow)
- Provenance note: bwesterb/mtc read for design patterns only, mtc-bridge AGPL never read into code (section 6 licensing constraints)
- Feature-flag matrix (ml-dsa) documented

## Out of Scope
- Runbooks and operator docs (observability epic); AGENTS.md/skills seeding (agent-harnessing epic)

## Testing
- Doctests (unit layer, section 19.1); doc build gate

## Demo
After merge: `cargo doc -p mtc --open` shows the documented crate; `cargo test --doc -p mtc` passes.

nodes.title: Differential testing harness against the bwesterb/mtc Go binary
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement section 19.3 Layer 4 and section 19.5: a small Go oracle binary wrapping `bwesterb/mtc` (BSD-3-Clause, section 28) with parse/verify subcommands, and a Rust harness that runs both implementations on the same inputs and asserts agreement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Go wrapper under `tools/mtc-oracle/` pinned to a specific bwesterb/mtc commit via go.mod; built by `make oracle`
- Rust harness implements the section 19.3 differential_parse pattern: both-accept requires structural equality; both-reject passes; accept/reject mismatch fails with input hex dumped for investigation
- Differential verify (section 19.5 Path B): proofs our library produces are verified by the Go oracle, and vice versa where formats allow
- Corpus: conformance vectors, plus any fuzz corpora present under `fuzz/corpus/`, replayed through the differential harness
- Mismatch findings get minimized and checked in as regression vectors
- PR split: (1) Go oracle binary; (2) Rust differential harness + corpus replay

## Out of Scope
- Nightly CI job scheduling (testing-infra epic, section 19.3 Layer 4 notes cross-language tooling cost)
- Copying Go code into our implementation (clean-room rule, section 6)

## Testing
- Differential layer per sections 19.3/19.5; runs locally on a laptop with the Go toolchain

## Demo
After merge: `make differential` builds the oracle and replays the corpus through both parsers, reporting agreement stats.

nodes.title: Landmark selection and signatureless verification
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement landmarks — predistributed subtree hashes enabling signatureless verification (section 2, goal in section 1) — including landmark selection for a given tree size per the draft and the section 12.1 step 6' variant: verify a computed subtree root against a landmark hash instead of a checkpoint signature.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Landmark selection function: for a tree size, produce the spec-defined landmark subtree set; deterministic and unit-tested against hand-computed small cases
- `Landmark` wire format round-trips via mtc-serialization
- Signatureless verify path on `MTCProof`: proof to subtree root compared against a supplied landmark, no signature check (section 12.1 step 6')
- Property test: any entry under a landmark verifies signaturelessly; entries outside it fail with a structured landmark-miss error enabling fallback to full verification
- PR split: (1) selection + serialization; (2) signatureless verify path

## Out of Scope
- Landmark distribution cadence and publication (open question OQ-4; read-path/observability epics)

## Testing
- Unit + property per section 19.2

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example signatureless_demo` verifies a proof against a landmark with signature verification disabled.

nodes.title: ML-DSA via qux-pqc behind a feature flag
nodes.description:
## Goal
Integrate ML-DSA (FIPS 204) via `qux-pqc` as a `SignatureScheme` implementation, gated behind an `ml-dsa` cargo feature until production-ready (section 24 Phase 1, section 28). This is what makes the post-quantum story real (section 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ml-dsa` feature flag; default build excludes qux-pqc entirely; `cargo build -p mtc` and `cargo build -p mtc --features ml-dsa` both succeed
- ML-DSA sign/verify round-trip tests; verify rejects tampered inputs
- Known-answer tests against FIPS 204 test vectors
- ML-DSA algorithm identifier wired into the registry from mtclib-signing; feature-off builds still parse the ID and return an unsupported-algorithm error rather than panicking
- Signature size assertions documenting the ~40x-vs-ECDSA size premium noted in section 2

## Out of Scope
- Making ML-DSA the default checkpoint algorithm (v1 is ECDSA per section 24)
- HSM-backed ML-DSA (cloud-abstraction epic)

## Testing
- Unit + known-answer vectors per section 19.1; feature-matrix build check

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc --features ml-dsa ml_dsa` passes; default `cargo test -p mtc` is unchanged.

nodes.title: Tree-level range pruning that preserves proofs for unpruned entries
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the tree-math prune operation required by the section 19.2 invariant "pruning a range and verifying a proof for an unpruned entry still works": `prune(range)` drops pruned leaf data while retaining the interior hashes needed so unpruned entries remain provable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `prune(&mut self, range)` on the in-memory tree; root hash is unchanged by pruning (unit test)
- Property test (section 19.2): after pruning any range, inclusion proofs for every unpruned leaf still generate and verify
- Proof generation for a pruned leaf returns a structured `Pruned` error, never panics
- Pruning is idempotent; overlapping prune calls compose (property test)
- Edge cases unit-tested: empty range, whole tree, tile-aligned and non-aligned boundaries

## Out of Scope
- Pruning Step Functions workflow and Object Lock retention (pruning-retention epic, Phase 7)
- Persistence of pruned state (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property per sections 19.1-19.2

## Demo
After merge: `cargo run -p mtc --example prune_demo` prunes a range from a 1000-leaf tree and verifies a proof for an unpruned leaf.

nodes.title: TrustAnchorID type per draft-ietf-tls-trust-anchor-ids
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the Trust Anchor ID — the stable CA identifier (section 2) — per draft-ietf-tls-trust-anchor-ids (section 28): binary encoding, human-readable text form, parsing, and equality/ordering semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `TrustAnchorId` newtype with binary serialization via mtc-serialization and dotted text formatting/parsing
- Round-trip property tests for both binary and text forms (section 19.2)
- Parsing arbitrary bytes/strings returns Err, never panics; length bounded (section 19.3 properties)
- Ordering and equality well-defined and tested (needed for stable log identity)
- Draft revision pinned and cited in rustdoc (section 28 spec-tracking workflow: track OQ-2 instability)

## Out of Scope
- TLS handshake negotiation of trust anchors (out of project scope)
- Embedding into ACME/issuance flows (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property per section 19.2; fuzz target lands in mtclib-fuzz-targets

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc trust_anchor` passes; example parses and reprints a sample Trust Anchor ID in both forms.

nodes.title: Structured fuzzing helpers via the arbitrary bridge
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the structured-fuzzing layer (spec 19.3 Layer 3): shared `arbitrary`-based generators producing semi-valid structures so fuzzing reaches post-parse verification paths that byte-level fuzzing misses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Arbitrary` impls/helpers for structured inputs (e.g., `ArbitraryProofInput`) in mtc-testutil behind a feature flag
- Exemplar structured target per 19.3: construct a proof from arbitrary structured input, run verification, assert no panic
- Structured targets run under the same PR-replay and nightly CI wiring as byte-level targets
- Docs: decision guidance for structured vs unstructured targets, added to the fuzz template README

## Out of Scope
- Structured targets for component-owned types (ship with those epics)
- Byte-level target scaffolding (test-fuzz-harness)

## Testing
- Fuzz (structured, 19.3 Layer 3); unit test for generator validity bounds

## Demo
`cargo +nightly fuzz run verify_proof_structured -- -runs=10000` exercises post-parse verification without panics.

nodes.title: Define cloud-types crate: ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv, Hsm traits
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-types` with the four async cloud-capability traits, common DTOs, and error taxonomy per spec §9.1/§9.3, including `is_fips_validated()` on `Hsm` per §14.4. This is the critical-path anchor that blocks all storage and CA service work (§25.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate `cloud-types` exists with modules `object_store.rs`, `object_lock.rs`, `replicated_kv.rs`, `hsm.rs`, `errors.rs` (§9.3)
- `ObjectStore`: `put/get/head/list/delete`; `PutOptions` supports if-not-exists (no-overwrite) semantics upholding the append-only invariant (§8, §9.7 `test_overwrite_fails`)
- `ObjectLock`: `put_with_retention`, `extend_retention`, `get_retention` (§9.1)
- `ReplicatedKv`: `get`, conditional `put`, `atomic_update`, `transact`, `query` plus `Key`/`Item`/`Value`/`Condition`/`UpdateExpression`/`Operation` DTOs (§9.1)
- `Hsm`: `sign`, `get_public_key`, `generate_key`, and `is_fips_validated() -> bool` (§14.4)
- Error taxonomy distinguishes `NotFound`, `ConditionFailed`, `AlreadyExists`, `RetentionViolation`, and retryable transport errors
- All traits object-safe and usable as `Arc<dyn Trait>` with `Send + Sync` bounds (§9.4)
- Rustdoc on every method states the required capability bar from §9.5

## Out of Scope
- Any backend implementation (memory/AWS/SoftHSM tickets); `Backend` factory (cloud-backend-factory); storage facade and tile cache (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): compile-time object-safety assertions (`Arc<dyn Trait>` usage), error-classification helper tests; no external dependencies

## Demo
`cargo doc -p cloud-types --open` shows the four documented traits; `cargo test -p cloud-types` green.

nodes.title: cloud-memory: pure in-memory implementation of all four cloud traits
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `crates/cloud-memory` — pure-memory implementations of all four `cloud-types` traits so every downstream crate can unit test with zero external dependencies (§9.3, §9.6). Second cloud-abstraction priority on the critical path (§25.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `MemoryObjectStore`: map-backed put/get/head/list/delete; rejects overwrite with `AlreadyExists` when `PutOptions` requires if-not-exists (§9.7)
- `MemoryObjectLock`: retention windows enforced against an injectable `Clock` (§22.11, §18.4 pattern); `extend_retention` forward-only; delete during retention rejected with `RetentionViolation` (§9.5)
- `MemoryReplicatedKv`: conditional put, `atomic_update`, all-or-nothing `transact`, prefix `query`; shareable as `Arc<dyn ReplicatedKv>` across tokio tasks with interior locking, no `unsafe`
- Property test: 100 concurrent tokio tasks racing conditional puts on one key yield exactly one `Ok` per round; `transact` with one failing condition applies zero ops (§19.2)
- `MemoryHsm`: ECDSA P-256 via RustCrypto `p256` (§14.1); `generate_key`/`sign`/`get_public_key`; `is_fips_validated() == false` (§14.4)
- Zero external dependencies: no Docker, no LocalStack, no SoftHSM (§9.6)
- Full crate test run completes fast enough for the <30s unit budget (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Shared conformance suite definitions (cloud-test-suite tickets); `Backend` factory wiring; persistence of any kind

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1) per trait impl
- Property (`proptest`, §19.2): concurrent conditional CAS admits exactly one winner; `transact` never partially applies

## Demo
With Docker stopped: `cargo test -p cloud-memory` — all green, sub-second.

nodes.title: DDB item schema: typed items and epoch condition builder
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §8.2 single-table schema as typed Rust structs with conversions to/from `cloud-types` KV items: `counter`, `primary-region-lease`, `latest-checkpoint`, `latest-revocation`, `batch#{batchId}`, `audit#{tree_size}`, all under PK `log#{logId}`. Include the shared epoch `ConditionExpression` builder used by every mutating write (§8.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- One struct per SK pattern with exactly the §8.2 attributes (batch items include `source_type`/`source_id` for the adapter pattern, §10)
- `to_item`/`from_item` round-trip for every struct; unknown attributes tolerated on read (forward compat)
- SK strings match §8.2 patterns exactly; PK built from `LogId` newtype
- `epoch_condition(Epoch)` helper produces a `Condition` reusable by counter, batch, checkpoint, and revocation writers
- Malformed items produce typed decode errors, never panics

## Out of Scope
- Any network calls; this is pure item (de)serialization
- Lease renewal/takeover semantics (multi-region epic)

## Testing
Unit; property (`proptest` round-trip per item type, §19.2).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage ddb_schema`; doctest showing a batch item rendered to attribute map.

nodes.title: S3 key layout module: fixed-width zero-padded object naming
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §8.1 object key scheme as a pure module: `checkpoints/{tree_size}.signed`, `tiles/{level}/{...}.tile`, `entries/{...}.entry`, `revocations/{tree_size}.signed`, all fixed-width zero-padded so lexicographic order equals numeric order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Typed constructors: checkpoint key from tree size, tile key from (level, tile index), entry key from entry index, revocation key from tree size — taking domain newtypes, not raw u64 (§22)
- Parsers invert every constructor; `parse(render(k)) == k`
- Rendered keys match §8.1 examples byte-for-byte (e.g. tree size 256 → `checkpoints/0000000000000256.signed`; entry 0 → `entries/000/000/000000.entry`)
- Property test: for random index pairs, numeric ordering == lexicographic ordering of rendered keys (§8.1 invariant)
- No I/O in this module; pure functions only

## Out of Scope
- Actually writing objects (stor-write-once-objects)
- CloudFront/read-path URL mapping (read-path epic)

## Testing
Unit; property (`proptest` round-trip + ordering, §19.2).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage key_layout` and a doctest table showing example index → key renderings.

nodes.title: Storage facade crate: Storage trait, error taxonomy, S3DdbStorage wiring
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/storage`: the `Storage` facade trait with the full method surface used by the CA service pseudocode (§11.4, §13.3: `read_lease`, `allocate_indices`, `persist_batch_state`, `write_entries`, `write_tiles`, `commit_checkpoint`, `read_latest_checkpoint`, `query_pending_batches`, `mark_batch_abandoned`), a `StorageError` taxonomy, and the `S3DdbStorage` struct wired from `Backend` trait objects (§9.4). This is the seam sub-tickets fill in (§23.6 codemap: crate `storage`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/storage` in workspace; depends only on `cloud-types` and core MTC types, never a provider SDK (§9.3–9.4)
- `trait Storage` declared with the full §11.4/§13.3 method surface, doc comments citing spec sections
- `StorageError` enum with `LostLease`, `AlreadyExists`, `NotFound`, `InvalidState`, `Unimplemented`, `Backend(..)` variants via `thiserror` (§22)
- `S3DdbStorage::new(Arc<Backend>, StorageConfig)`; config carries bucket, table, `log#{logId}` PK, retention policy; unimplemented methods return the typed `Unimplemented` error (replaced by sub-tickets), never panic
- Constructor + error-mapping tests run over the pure-memory backend with zero external deps (§9.6)

## Out of Scope
- Real method implementations (per-pattern sub-tickets)
- Lease/epoch protocol logic (multi-region epic); cloud trait definitions (cloud-abstraction epic)

## Testing
Unit (memory backend, §19.1); no integration needed yet.

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage` green from a clean clone with no Docker running.

nodes.title: cloud-aws crate: S3ObjectStore and S3ObjectLock implementations
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-aws` and implement `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` over `aws-sdk-s3` (§9.3), exercised exclusively against LocalStack — no real AWS spend (§1 non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate scaffolding with `s3_object_store.rs` and `s3_object_lock.rs` per the §9.3 layout
- `S3ObjectStore`: put (If-None-Match for no-overwrite semantics), get, head, paginated list, delete
- `S3ObjectLock`: retention via S3 Object Lock; COMPLIANCE-mode semantics and any LocalStack emulation caveats documented in rustdoc (§9.5 retention bar)
- SDK errors mapped onto the `cloud-types` error taxonomy (retryable vs terminal, `ConditionFailed`/`AlreadyExists` on precondition failure)
- Client construction accepts injected endpoint/credentials config so LocalStack and (hypothetically) real AWS use the same code path
- Integration tests gated behind `--features integration` (§19.1) and green against LocalStack

## Out of Scope
- DynamoDB `ReplicatedKv` (cloud-aws-ddb-kv); CloudHSM (cloud-aws-cloudhsm); running the shared suites in CI (cloud-aws-conformance); S3 bucket layout/schema (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): error-mapping and request-shaping tests without network
- Integration (§19.1): LocalStack-backed tests behind `--features integration`

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-aws --features integration` green.

nodes.title: Run shared conformance suites against cloud-aws via LocalStack in CI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire the shared `cloud-test-suite` suites (ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv) against the `cloud-aws` backend through `cloud-localstack`, per the §9.7 pattern, and run them in a CI integration lane — guaranteeing behavioral consistency between memory and AWS backends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cloud-aws/tests/` invokes `run_object_store_suite`, `run_object_lock_suite`, and `run_replicated_kv_suite` with factories built via `cloud-localstack` (§9.7)
- All suites green against LocalStack, gated `--features integration` (§19.1)
- CI gains an integration job with a LocalStack service container running these suites on every PR touching cloud crates
- Any genuine behavioral divergence (e.g., LocalStack Object Lock gaps) is either fixed in the backend or skipped via `#[ignore = "reason"]` carrying a tracking-ticket reference — shared suites are never edited to accommodate one backend

## Out of Scope
- Hsm suite vs SoftHSM (cloud-softhsm-conformance); chaos/failure-injection scenarios (testing-infrastructure epic, §19.9); performance benchmarks (§19.11)

## Testing
- Integration (§19.1): this ticket IS the integration coverage; reuses unit-proven suites

## Demo
CI run shows the `cloud-integration` job green; locally `docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-aws --features integration` runs the identical suites.

nodes.title: cloud-aws: DynamoDB ReplicatedKv implementation
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `ReplicatedKv` over `aws-sdk-dynamodb` in `cloud-aws/src/ddb_replicated_kv.rs` (§9.3), providing the conditional and transactional writes the lease/epoch protocol and write-path linearization require (§9.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Condition` DTOs translated to DynamoDB `ConditionExpression`s; `ConditionalCheckFailedException` maps to `ConditionFailed` (never a panic or opaque error)
- `atomic_update` → `UpdateItem` with `UpdateExpression`; returns the updated `Item`
- `transact` → `TransactWriteItems`, all-or-nothing including per-op conditions
- `query` → prefix query against the table key schema; pagination handled
- Item/Value serialization to and from DynamoDB `AttributeValue` covered by round-trip tests
- Integration tests gated `--features integration`, green against LocalStack DynamoDB (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Global Tables replication semantics and multi-region simulation (multi-region epic); DDB table schema for batches/leases (storage-facade epic, §8.2); shared-suite CI wiring (cloud-aws-conformance)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): expression translation + AttributeValue round-trips
- Integration (§19.1): conditional write, atomic update, transact tests vs LocalStack

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-aws --features integration` shows DDB KV tests passing.

nodes.title: Backend struct and build_backend factory with Memory provider
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §9.4 `Backend` factory: the struct of four `Arc<dyn Trait>` handles plus `build_backend(BackendConfig)` with a `Provider` enum, shipping `Provider::Memory` first so downstream CA-service work can start immediately against a fully wired backend.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Backend { object_store, object_lock, replicated_kv, hsm }` as `Arc<dyn ...>` fields exactly per §9.4
- `Provider` enum with `Memory`, `Aws`, `Localstack` variants (§9.4); non-memory variants return a clear `Unimplemented` error until cloud-backend-factory-aws lands
- `build_backend` returns a working all-memory `Backend`; consumers depend only on `cloud-types` + factory, never name a concrete backend (§9.3, §9.4)
- Cargo features gate backend crate dependencies so memory-only consumers do not compile the AWS SDK (§9.3 "wired via Cargo features")
- `BackendConfig` deserializes from config file/env (serde); unknown provider strings rejected with actionable error
- Doc example shows a service constructor taking `Arc<Backend>` (§9.4 `CaService::new` shape)

## Out of Scope
- Aws/Localstack/SoftHSM wiring (cloud-backend-factory-aws); GCP/Azure/on-prem variants (multi-cloud epic, §27); storage facade construction (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config deserialization, memory build round-trip (put/get through `Backend`), feature-flag compile checks in CI matrix

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-backend` green with no Docker; doc example compiles via doctest.

nodes.title: cloud-localstack helper crate: endpoint-configured AWS backends for dev/test
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-localstack` — thin wrappers that configure the `cloud-aws` implementations with LocalStack endpoints, credentials, and path-style addressing (§9.3), so dev and test code never hand-rolls SDK endpoint config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cloud_localstack::build(cfg)` returns `cloud-aws` ObjectStore/ObjectLock/ReplicatedKv instances pointed at LocalStack (§9.4 `Provider::Localstack` target)
- Endpoint resolution: explicit config first, then `LOCALSTACK_ENDPOINT`-style env fallback with sane compose defaults (§18.1)
- Dummy-credential and path-style-addressing quirks handled here, not by callers
- Helper used by `cloud-aws` integration tests to construct clients (replacing ad-hoc config)
- Rustdoc quickstart: two-line example constructing a LocalStack-backed store

## Out of Scope
- The docker-compose LocalStack environment itself (foundation-infra localstack-dev-env); Backend factory wiring (cloud-backend-factory-aws); multi-region multi-instance LocalStack simulation (multi-region epic, §18.3)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config/endpoint resolution logic
- Integration (§19.1): smoke test constructing each client and performing one round-trip vs LocalStack, gated `--features integration`

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-localstack --features integration` green.

nodes.title: Run shared Hsm suite against SoftHSM2 in CI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire `run_hsm_suite` from `cloud-test-suite` against `cloud-softhsm` (§9.7) and run it in the CI integration lane, proving the PKCS#11 backend behaves identically to `MemoryHsm`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cloud-softhsm/tests/` invokes `run_hsm_suite` with a factory that provisions a fresh SoftHSM2 token per run (§9.7 pattern), gated `--features integration` (§19.1)
- CI integration job installs/initializes SoftHSM2 (reusing the softhsm-backend bootstrap script) and runs the suite on every PR touching HSM crates
- Suite invoked with `expected_fips == false` for SoftHSM (§14.4)
- Token setup/teardown leaves no state between test runs (idempotent re-runs)

## Out of Scope
- New suite cases (extend cloud-test-suite-hsm instead); CloudHSM validation (cloud-aws-cloudhsm, untestable without spend per §1); checkpoint-signer E2E (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Integration (§19.1): this ticket is the SoftHSM integration coverage, reusing the unit-proven shared suite

## Demo
CI shows the HSM integration job green; locally `./scripts/softhsm-init.sh && cargo test -p cloud-softhsm --features integration` runs the shared suite.

nodes.title: cloud-test-suite: shared Hsm conformance suite
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add `run_hsm_suite` to `cloud-test-suite` (§9.7) so every HSM backend (memory, SoftHSM, later CloudHSM) proves identical signing behavior, validated against `MemoryHsm`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suite covers: `generate_key(EcdsaP256)` → `get_public_key` → `sign` → signature verifies with a RustCrypto `p256` verifier (§14.1, §19.6 cryptographic invariant style)
- Signing with an unknown `KeyHandle` returns a typed error, never a panic
- Suite signature takes `expected_fips: bool` and asserts `is_fips_validated() == expected_fips` (§14.4); memory run passes `false`
- Deterministic message set plus a small randomized message property case
- Suite wired in `cloud-memory/tests/` and passing

## Out of Scope
- SoftHSM/PKCS#11 execution of this suite (cloud-softhsm-conformance); key rotation and cross-region key replication ceremonies (multi-region epic, §14.2); ML-DSA (v2, core-mtc-library feature flag)

## Testing
- Unit + light property (§19.1, §19.2) against memory backend; becomes the integration suite for cloud-softhsm

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-memory` shows `hsm_suite` sign/verify round-trip passing.

nodes.title: cloud-test-suite: shared ReplicatedKv conformance suite
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add `run_replicated_kv_suite` to `cloud-test-suite` (§9.7) covering the conditional-write and transactional semantics the lease/epoch protocol and write path depend on (§8.3, §9.5), validated against `cloud-memory`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suite covers: get/put round-trip; conditional put success and `ConditionFailed` on violated condition; `atomic_update` with condition expression; `transact` is all-or-nothing when one op's condition fails; `query` returns all items under a prefix
- Property test (`proptest`, §19.2): N concurrent conditional CAS attempts on the same key yield exactly one success per round — the invariant multi-region leasing builds on (§9.5 "Conditional KV writes")
- Suite wired in `cloud-memory/tests/` and passing
- Failure-mode assertions use the shared `cloud-types` error taxonomy, not backend-specific errors

## Out of Scope
- Running against DynamoDB/LocalStack (cloud-aws-conformance); lease/epoch protocol itself (multi-region epic); Kani harnesses for index allocation (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property (§19.1, §19.2) against memory backend; reused as integration suite by backend crates

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-memory` shows `replicated_kv_suite` cases including the concurrent-CAS property test passing.

nodes.title: cloud-test-suite: shared ObjectStore + ObjectLock conformance suites
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-test-suite` with the factory-closure suite pattern from §9.7 and ship the `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` suites, validated against `cloud-memory`. Every backend (current and future GCP/Azure) must pass these identical tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate `cloud-test-suite` with generic `run_object_store_suite(factory)` matching the §9.7 signature shape
- ObjectStore suite covers: put/get round-trip, overwrite-fails under if-not-exists, list-with-prefix, head metadata, delete, get-missing returns `NotFound`
- `run_object_lock_suite` covers: `put_with_retention` + `get_retention` round-trip, extend forward-only (shortening rejected), delete during retention rejected (§9.5 append-only bar)
- Both suites wired in `cloud-memory/tests/` and passing (§9.7)
- Suite helpers usable from other crates' `tests/` dirs without copy-paste

## Out of Scope
- ReplicatedKv and Hsm suites (cloud-test-suite-kv, cloud-test-suite-hsm); running suites against AWS/SoftHSM backends (conformance tickets)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): suites executed against the memory backend prove the suite itself; suites become the integration layer when backend crates adopt them

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-memory` output shows `object_store_suite` and `object_lock_suite` cases passing.

nodes.title: Fixture snapshot/restore engine for LocalStack S3 and DynamoDB state
nodes.description:
## Goal
Core fixture snapshot/restore engine (§18.5): capture LocalStack S3 and DynamoDB state as a named, versioned artifact and restore it byte-identically — the substrate for every named fixture and bug-repro workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/dev-fixture` library + CLI: `fixture save <name>` dumps all S3 buckets (object versions and Object Lock metadata included) and all DDB tables into `fixtures/<name>/` with a manifest (schema version, per-file checksums, created-at, generator provenance)
- `fixture load <name>` wipes target LocalStack state and restores; idempotent; verifies manifest checksums before applying and aborts on mismatch
- Round-trip: save → load → save produces identical checksums
- Clear error naming the schema version on unsupported manifests
- Payloads stored as compressed tarballs; storage policy (git-lfs vs regenerate-on-demand) documented in `docs/dev-environment.md`

## Out of Scope
- SoftHSM token capture and `make` wiring (`dev-fixture-targets`)
- Named fixture content (million-entries etc. — separate tickets per §25.6)

## Testing
- Unit: manifest serialization, checksum verification
- Integration: round-trip against LocalStack; S3 versioning + Object Lock metadata survive restore (§19.1)

## Demo
Write objects/rows to the local stack, `fixture save scratch`, wipe, `fixture load scratch` → endpoint listings show identical state.

nodes.title: SoftHSM token capture and make fixture-save/fixture-load wiring
nodes.description:
## Goal
Complete the fixture workflow (§18.5, §18.8): capture the SoftHSM token directory alongside storage state and wire `make fixture-save name=X` / `make fixture-load name=X`, so a restored fixture is a fully working CA (signing keys included).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixture engine extended to include the SoftHSM token directory in the payload and manifest; restore reinstates it so checkpoint signing works immediately after load
- `make fixture-save name=X` / `make fixture-load name=X` wired per Makefile conventions; missing `name=` fails with usage help
- Loading while services run follows a documented safe sequence (quiesce/restart hint printed) rather than silently corrupting state
- Round-trip: demo state saved, wiped, loaded → `mtcctl status` reports the identical tree head and signing works

## Out of Scope
- Engine internals for S3/DDB (`dev-fixture-engine`)
- Multi-region fixture topologies

## Testing
- Integration: SoftHSM token round-trip; post-restore signing succeeds (§19.1)
- E2E: `tests/e2e/fixture-roundtrip.sh` save/wipe/load smoke via the make targets (§19.13)

## Demo
Issue a few certs in the demo env, `make fixture-save name=scratch`, wipe, `make fixture-load name=scratch` → identical state via `mtcctl status`.

nodes.title: Seeded deterministic synthetic entry generator
nodes.description:
## Goal
A seeded, deterministic synthetic entry generator producing valid MTC assertion/entry inputs for fixtures (§18.5), the demo issuance loop (§18.1), and soak/perf tests — same seed, byte-identical stream, every run, every platform.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/dev-entrygen`: `EntryGen::new(seed)` yields an infinite iterator of valid entries (domains, keys, claims) using a seeded RNG (e.g. `rand_chacha`)
- Determinism: same seed produces identical serialized bytes across runs and platforms
- Generated entries pass domain-type validation and serialization round-trip (§19.2)
- Supports shaped generation: fixed count, DNS name patterns, key-type mix
- CLI shim (`cargo run -p dev-entrygen -- --seed 42 --count 1000`) emitting JSONL

## Out of Scope
- Driving the CA pipeline (fixture generator tickets own that)
- Malformed/adversarial inputs (fuzzing, §19.3, testing epic)

## Testing
- Unit: shape parameters honored; count semantics
- Property: determinism across seeds; every generated entry satisfies `parse(serialize(x)) == x`

## Demo
Run the CLI shim twice with `--seed 42 --count 3` → byte-identical output; pipe entries into the intake path once it exists.

nodes.title: cloud-softhsm: PKCS#11 Hsm implementation against SoftHSM2
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-softhsm` implementing the `Hsm` trait over PKCS#11 (via `cryptoki`) against SoftHSM2 — the dev-mode stand-in for CloudHSM (§9.3, §14, §18.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `generate_key` creates an ECDSA P-256 keypair (v1 algorithm, §14.1) and returns a stable `KeyHandle` (token label/ID based)
- `get_public_key` exports SPKI DER; `sign` produces a signature that verifies with a RustCrypto `p256` verifier; signature encoding choice documented for checkpoint-signer consumers
- Slot/token/PIN configuration via config struct with env fallback; token bootstrap script (init token + PIN) usable by both tests and `make demo` (§18.1)
- `is_fips_validated() == false` — dev-only, explicitly non-FIPS (§14.4)
- Concurrent signing: integration test spawns 8 tokio tasks signing in parallel; all signatures verify and no PKCS#11 `CKR_*` errors occur (sessions pooled or per-operation, never shared across threads)
- Integration tests gated `--features integration`, green with SoftHSM2 installed

## Out of Scope
- CloudHSM wiring (cloud-aws-cloudhsm); cross-region key replication ceremony (multi-region epic, §14.2); checkpoint signer component (ca-service epic); ML-DSA keys (v2)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config parsing, handle encoding, error mapping (mock-free logic only)
- Integration (§19.1): sign/verify round-trip vs SoftHSM2; latency smoke assertion far under the 100ms p99 target (§14.3)

## Demo
`./scripts/softhsm-init.sh && cargo test -p cloud-softhsm --features integration` green.

nodes.title: Batch item lifecycle: persist, transition, query pending, abandon
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `batch#{batchId}` access patterns (§8.2): `persist_batch_state` (§11.4 step 4), epoch-conditioned status transitions, `query_pending_batches` and `mark_batch_abandoned` (§13.3 promotion step 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `persist_batch_state` writes Pending with `start_index`, `end_index`, `leaf_count`, `epoch`, `created_at`, `source_type`, `source_id` (§8.2, §10)
- Status transitions form a validated state machine: Pending → Committed | Abandoned; illegal transitions (e.g. Committed → Abandoned) → `InvalidState`
- Every mutating write includes the epoch condition (§8.3); mismatch → `LostLease`
- `query_pending_batches` prefix-queries `batch#` and returns only Pending items; `committed_at` set on commit
- `mark_batch_abandoned` idempotent (promotion is idempotent, §13.3)

## Out of Scope
- The commit transaction itself (stor-checkpoint-commit owns the linearization point)
- Batch building logic (ca-service epic)

## Testing
Unit; property (`proptest` over random transition sequences — invalid sequences always rejected); LocalStack via stor-conformance-suite (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage batch_state`; test output shows a Pending batch abandoned then rejected for commit.

nodes.title: commit_checkpoint: transactional linearization point + read_latest_checkpoint
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement §11.4 step 8, the linearization point: write the signed checkpoint object (write-once, retention), then a `ReplicatedKv::transact` atomically updating `latest-checkpoint` and flipping the batch to Committed, both epoch-conditioned (§8.2, §8.3). Also implement `read_latest_checkpoint` (§13.3 step 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Checkpoint object written to `checkpoints/{tree_size}.signed` before the KV transact; an orphan object with no pointer flip is harmless and recoverable (§11.2, §11.3)
- Transact updates `latest-checkpoint` (`tree_size`, `s3_key`, `signed_at`, `epoch`) and batch status Committed atomically — both or neither
- Epoch mismatch → `LostLease` with no visible mutation of either item
- `latest-checkpoint.tree_size` never regresses (condition enforces monotonicity)
- `read_latest_checkpoint` returns typed record; `NotFound` on empty log
- Integration test against LocalStack DDB+S3 behind `--features integration` (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Checkpoint construction/HSM signing (ca-service checkpoint-signer)
- Revocation pointer (stor-revocation-audit-access)

## Testing
Unit, property (pointer monotonic under random interleaved commits, §19.2), integration (LocalStack).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage --features integration checkpoint_commit`; example prints the latest checkpoint record after two commits.

nodes.title: Facade conformance suite: memory vs LocalStack behavioral parity
nodes.description:
## Goal
Apply the §9.7 shared-suite pattern at the facade level: one behavioral suite run against `S3DdbStorage` over the memory backend (plain `cargo test`) and over LocalStack AWS backends (`--features integration`, §19.1), guaranteeing the facade behaves identically regardless of backend. This is where the tickets that deferred LocalStack coverage (write-once, lease, batch, entry, tile, revocation/audit, hydration) get their integration runs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suite covers the facade invariants: write-once enforcement on all object categories (§8.1), epoch condition on every mutating KV op (§8.3), counter monotonic/non-overlapping, batch state machine legality, checkpoint and revocation pointers monotonic, hydration consistency
- Memory run completes in the <30s unit budget with zero external deps (§19.1)
- LocalStack run gated behind `--features integration` and wired into CI's integration job
- One factory-parameterized suite — a new backend is one factory closure (§9.7)
- Failures name the invariant violated, not just the assertion line

## Out of Scope
- Cross-backend suites for raw cloud traits (cloud-abstraction owns cloud-test-suite)
- Chaos/soak scenarios (testing-infrastructure epic)

## Testing
Unit + integration by construction; property assertions reused from per-ticket tests (§19.2).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage` then `make integration-storage` (LocalStack up) — same suite, both green.

nodes.title: Counter UpdateItem with epoch check: allocate_indices + init + counter view
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement atomic index allocation per the §25.4 exemplar ticket: `Storage::allocate_indices(n, epoch)` via `ReplicatedKv::atomic_update` on the `counter` item with epoch `ConditionExpression` (§8.2, §8.3), plus idempotent counter initialization and the optimistic local counter view (§8.4: authoritative read happens during UpdateItem, never from the local view).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `allocate_indices(&self, n, epoch) -> Result<(Index, Index), StorageError>` returns a contiguous, exclusive-end range
- Conditional-check failure maps to `StorageError::LostLease` (§25.4)
- `init_counter()` creates the item if absent; safe to call repeatedly
- Local counter view is advisory only; a stale view never causes overlapping ranges
- Property test: many concurrent allocations produce non-overlapping ranges
- Kani harness `verify_no_overlapping_allocations` in `crates/storage/proofs/` (§23.7)
- Integration test against LocalStack DDB behind `--features integration` (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Lease renewer and lease-check policy (multi-region epic)
- Batch persistence (stor-batch-state)

## Testing
Unit, property, integration (LocalStack DDB), Kani.

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage counter`; `cargo kani -p storage` proves the no-overlap harness.

nodes.title: write_entries: parallel write-once entry objects
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `write_entries(start, &batch)` (§11.4 step 5): serialize each entry (mtc-serialization) and write it write-once at its §8.1 entry key, in parallel with bounded concurrency.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Entry at index `start + i` lands at exactly the §8.1 key for that index
- Parallel writes with a configurable concurrency bound; partial failure surfaces an aggregate error naming failed indices
- Retry after crash is idempotent: identical bytes → success, differing bytes → `AlreadyExists` (§8.1 invariant, §11.3)
- `read_entry(index)` counterpart returns the exact bytes written

## Out of Scope
- Entry validation/construction (ca-service batch builder)
- Tile derivation from entries (stor-tile-writer / tree-updater)

## Testing
Unit; property (for random batches, every entry readable at its index and byte-identical, §19.2); LocalStack via stor-conformance-suite (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage entry_writer`; example writes a 100-entry batch to the memory backend and lists the resulting keys in §8.1 shape.

nodes.title: FakeStorage test double with failure injection
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the `FakeStorage` test-only implementation of `Storage` (§23.6 codemap lists it explicitly) with scriptable failure injection, so ca-service unit tests can exercise failure modes (§11.3) without composing real backends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `FakeStorage` implements the full `Storage` trait; gated behind a `test-util` feature (usable from other crates' tests, excluded from release builds)
- Per-method failure injection: fail-once, fail-always, delayed response — enough to simulate lost lease, write timeouts, and crash-between-steps scenarios from §11.3
- Internal state (entries, tiles, checkpoints, batch items) inspectable by tests
- Registered as a factory in the facade conformance suite (§9.7); the suite's memory-mode run passes against `FakeStorage` with no injection active, keeping the double behaviorally honest

## Out of Scope
- Chaos testing scenarios themselves (testing-infrastructure epic)
- The memory cloud backend (cloud-abstraction epic — this is a facade-level double)

## Testing
Unit self-tests for injection semantics; conformance suite memory run (§19.1).

## Demo
Doctest in the crate README: inject `LostLease` on `commit_checkpoint` and assert the caller surfaces `IssueError`-shaped failure.

nodes.title: Raw lease item access: typed read and conditional write helpers
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the raw `primary-region-lease` item access (§8.2) the multi-region protocol will drive: typed `read_lease()` (used by §11.4 step 1) and conditional-write helpers (CAS on epoch/holder/expires_at) — mechanics only, no protocol.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `read_lease()` returns typed `Lease { region, expires_at, epoch, holder_id }` per §8.2
- `write_lease_conditional(lease, conditions)` surfaces condition failure as a typed error (not a panic, not a generic backend error)
- Condition helpers cover: expected epoch, expected holder, expiry-before-timestamp — the building blocks §8.3 semantics require
- Missing lease item → typed `NotFound` so bootstrap can detect first-run

## Out of Scope
- Renewal cadence (20s/60s TTL), takeover eligibility, epoch increment on takeover — all §8.3 protocol logic belongs to the multi-region epic (`claim_lease` semantics land there)
- Standby monitoring behavior

## Testing
Unit + property over memory backend; LocalStack coverage via stor-conformance-suite (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage lease_access`; doctest reading and conditionally updating a lease against the memory backend.

nodes.title: In-memory CA state hydration on startup
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement startup hydration of the CA service's in-memory state (§8.4) and the consistency check promotion relies on (§13.3 step 1): read the latest checkpoint, verify the tile snapshot is consistent (recomputed root from stored tiles equals the checkpoint root — `tile_snapshot_consistent`), warm the tile cache with right-edge tiles, and initialize the local counter view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `hydrate()` returns a typed `HydratedState { checkpoint, counter_view, ... }` on a consistent store
- Root recomputed from tiles (tree-primitives) equals the checkpoint root; mismatch/missing tiles → typed `TilesInconsistent` error so callers can `wait_for_crr` (§13.3) rather than proceed
- Empty log (no checkpoint item) hydrates to a well-defined empty state (bootstrap path)
- Right-edge tiles for the current tree size are resident in the tile cache after hydration
- Counter view initialized from the counter item but marked advisory (§8.4)

## Out of Scope
- Checkpoint signature verification and promotion/gap-fill logic (§13.3 steps in ca-service/multi-region)
- CRR waiting/polling behavior (multi-region epic)

## Testing
Unit (memory backend); property (build random logs, hydrate, recomputed root always matches, §19.2); integration via stor-conformance-suite.

## Demo
`cargo run -p storage --example hydrate_demo` seeds a memory-backend log, hydrates, and prints tree size, root, and cache warmth.

nodes.title: LRU tile cache with read-through and hit/miss instrumentation
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the in-memory LRU tile cache (§8.4): tiles are immutable so caching is unconditionally safe; read-through over `read_tile` (stor-tile-writer); shared via `Arc<TileCache>` (§11.4 CaService field); hit/miss instrumented (§20.1: tile cache hit/miss is a named signal; OQ-5: start LRU, profile later).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Configurable capacity (bytes or tile count); LRU eviction order verified by a deterministic access-sequence test
- `get(level, index)`: cache hit returns without backend I/O (asserted via a call-counting backend); miss fetches via `read_tile`, populates, returns
- Concurrency stress test: 8+ tasks x 1k random `get`s over a 100-tile keyspace complete without deadlock and every returned tile is byte-identical to backend bytes
- Concurrent misses for the same tile store at most one entry; capacity accounting stays exact under the stress test
- Hit/miss/eviction counters exposed for the metrics layer (§20.1)
- Cached bytes always identical to backend bytes (immutability means no invalidation path exists — assert none is added)

## Out of Scope
- CloudFront/CDN caching (read-path epic)
- Checkpoint cache (stor-checkpoint-cache)
- Eviction-policy tuning beyond LRU (OQ-5 follow-up)

## Testing
Unit; property (cache-backed reads == direct backend reads for arbitrary access patterns, §19.2); multi-threaded stress test under `cargo test`.

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage tile_cache`; example runs 10k reads over a 100-tile log and prints hit ratio.

nodes.title: write_tiles: tile persistence at the §8.1 tile layout
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `write_tiles(&new_tiles)` (§11.4 step 6): persist tiles produced by tree-primitives at their `tiles/{level}/{...}.tile` keys (§8.1), write-once, plus the `read_tile(level, index)` fetch counterpart used by the cache and hydration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- (level, tile index) → key mapping via stor-s3-key-layout; level 0 is leaves (§8.1)
- Tiles serialized via the core library's tile wire format (tree-primitives)
- Re-writing an identical tile succeeds (idempotent retry); differing bytes at the same key → `AlreadyExists` (§8.1 invariant)
- `read_tile` returns typed tile or `NotFound`; round-trip write→read is byte-identical
- Multi-tile batches write in parallel with bounded concurrency

## Out of Scope
- Tree update logic computing which tiles changed (ca-service tree-updater)
- Caching (stor-tile-cache)

## Testing
Unit; property (random tile sets round-trip; second divergent write always rejected, §19.2); LocalStack via stor-conformance-suite (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage tile_writer`; example builds a small tree, writes its tiles, reads one back and prints its key.

nodes.title: Write-once object writer with Object Lock retention
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the immutable-object write path enforcing the §8.1 S3 invariants at the facade layer: put-if-absent, bytes never change after write, retention applied via `ObjectLock::put_with_retention` (§9.1) using the configured retention policy (§15.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `put_immutable(key, bytes)` writes with `retain_until` computed from `StorageConfig` retention policy
- Second write with different bytes → `StorageError::AlreadyExists`; second write with identical bytes → `Ok` (idempotent, safe for crash-retry per §11.3 failure modes)
- All object categories (checkpoints, tiles, entries, revocations) route through this path — no direct `ObjectStore::put` for log objects elsewhere in the crate
- Read counterpart `get_object(key)` with typed NotFound

## Out of Scope
- Lifecycle/pruning deletion (pruning epic)
- Retention extension workflows (pruning epic)

## Testing
Unit + property over memory backend (arbitrary write sequences never mutate stored bytes); LocalStack S3 Object Lock coverage lands via stor-conformance-suite (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage write_once`; test log shows an overwrite attempt rejected.

nodes.title: Fault-injection wrappers for cloud abstraction backends
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide decorator backends implementing the cloud traits that inject configurable faults — the shared machinery behind the adversarial suite (spec 19.8), chaos scenarios (19.9), and component-level failure tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `FaultInjecting<T>` wrappers for `ObjectStore`, `ObjectLock`, `ReplicatedKv`, and `Hsm`: error injection, latency injection, replication-stall simulation, and a wrong-signature HSM mode (19.8)
- Faults are scriptable and deterministic: triggered by operation count, key pattern, or explicit toggle; seedable for reproduction
- Test-clock utility supporting forced clock skew for lease-related tests (19.8, 19.9)
- Ships as a dev-dependency consumable by all component epics; wraps the memory backend with zero external dependencies (19.1 unit-test constraint)
- Unit tests cover every injector mode

## Out of Scope
- Scenario definitions built on top (test-chaos-harness, adversarial tickets)
- Process-level fault actions like killing a region (test-chaos-harness)

## Testing
- Unit + property (injector determinism given a seed)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-testutil fault_injection` shows a wrong-signature HSM causing checkpoint verification to fail cleanly.

nodes.title: Seed skill: add-storage-method.md
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed `.claude/skills/add-storage-method.md` per §23.1: how to extend the Storage interface with a new operation across all backends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Skill has Goal, Files involved (trait definition, memory backend, AWS backend, shared cloud-test-suite, storage facade — 3–5 pointers), Pattern (worked example from an actually merged method), Common pitfalls
- Pitfalls cover: implementing in one backend only, skipping the shared test suite, leaking vendor SDK types across the boundary (§22.8)
- States the requirement that the shared test suite runs the new method against every backend (§24 Phase 2)
- Passes `make skill-lint`

## Out of Scope
- Any storage code changes; the add-admin-endpoint skill (separate ticket)

## Testing
- `make skill-lint`; skill validated by tracing an existing storage method through every listed file, noted in the PR (§19.13 spirit)

## Demo
Open the skill and confirm each "Files involved" path resolves to real code across trait, backends, and test suite.

nodes.title: Wire Aws and Localstack providers into build_backend
nodes.description:
## Goal
Complete the §9.4 factory: `Provider::Aws` → `cloud_aws::build`, `Provider::Localstack` → `cloud_localstack::build`, with SoftHSM wired as the HSM for dev/Localstack profiles so a full four-trait `Backend` is buildable outside memory mode.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `build_backend` with `Provider::Localstack` returns a `Backend` backed by LocalStack S3/DDB via `cloud-localstack` and SoftHSM for `hsm` (§14: SoftHSM in dev)
- `Provider::Aws` path implemented and feature-gated; HSM slot documented as CloudHSM-pending (no real AWS spend, §1) with config validation only
- Backend crates remain feature-gated: memory-only builds compile without AWS SDK or PKCS#11 deps (§9.3)
- `BackendConfig` gains `aws`/`localstack` sections matching §9.4's `cfg.aws`/`cfg.localstack`
- Integration smoke test: `build_backend(localstack cfg)` then one put/get and one HSM sign through the `Backend` handles

## Out of Scope
- CloudHSM implementation (cloud-aws-cloudhsm); GCP/Azure/on-prem providers (multi-cloud epic); dev-env compose orchestration (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): provider dispatch + config validation
- Integration (§19.1): LocalStack+SoftHSM smoke test gated `--features integration`

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && ./scripts/softhsm-init.sh && cargo test -p cloud-backend --features integration` builds a live `Backend` and round-trips all four capabilities.

nodes.title: Document capability bar and how-to-add-a-backend guide
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write the cloud-abstraction documentation the spec assigns this layer: the capability requirements table (§9.5), what is deliberately NOT abstracted and why (§9.2), and a step-by-step guide for adding a new backend validated by the shared suites (§9.7) — the on-ramp for post-v1 GCP/Azure/on-prem work (§27 pointer only).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/cloud-backends.md` (linked from README/AGENTS.md) containing: the §9.5 capability table with required behaviors and rationale; the §9.2 abstraction boundary principle ("abstract inside the service binary, not the deployment topology"); honest cost accounting summary (§9.8)
- "Adding a backend" walkthrough: implement the four traits, pass every `cloud-test-suite` suite, wire the `Backend` factory + Cargo feature — with `cloud-memory` as the worked example
- Crate-level rustdoc for `cloud-types` links to this doc; `cargo doc` renders without warnings
- Statement that a backend lacking any §9.5 capability "isn't a fit" — abstractions do not paper over missing capabilities

## Out of Scope
- Actual GCP/Azure/on-prem implementations (multi-cloud epic); storage facade docs (storage-facade epic); runbooks (§21, observability/ops epics)

## Testing
- Doc build check (`cargo doc` warning-free) and link check in CI docs lane; doctest for any embedded code snippets (§19.1 unit)

## Demo
Open `docs/cloud-backends.md` in the repo; `cargo doc -p cloud-types --open` shows the linked guide.

nodes.title: Checkpoint cache: last N checkpoints by tree size
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the checkpoint cache from §8.4: keep the last N checkpoints keyed by tree size in memory so status surfaces and proof paths avoid repeated backend reads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Configurable N; inserting beyond capacity evicts the smallest tree size
- `get(tree_size)` and `latest()` lookups; `latest()` agrees with `read_latest_checkpoint` after insert
- Checkpoints are immutable once signed — cache never mutates an entry; divergent re-insert for the same tree size is rejected as an invariant violation
- Thread-safe via `Arc`: a concurrent insert/get stress test (multiple tasks, interleaved operations) completes without panics, and every checkpoint among the N largest inserted remains retrievable afterward

## Out of Scope
- Checkpoint signature verification (core library / ca-service)
- Tile cache (separate ticket)

## Testing
Unit; property (for random insert sequences, cache contents are exactly the N largest tree sizes inserted, §19.2); multi-threaded stress test under `cargo test`.

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage checkpoint_cache`; doctest showing eviction of the oldest checkpoint at capacity.

nodes.title: Storage crate docs: README, CODEMAP entry, add-storage-method guide
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the documentation obligations §23.5–23.6 place on this crate: a hierarchical README (purpose, public API, gotchas), the CODEMAP entry, and the `add-storage-method.md` pattern/skill doc (§23.4) so agents can extend the `Storage` interface correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/storage/README.md` states purpose, public API surface (`Storage`, `S3DdbStorage`, `FakeStorage`), and the two critical invariants: objects are write-once (§8.1) and every KV write is epoch-conditioned (§8.3)
- `make codemap` output includes the storage crate entry matching the §23.6 format (PURPOSE / PUBLIC API / DEPENDS ON / USED BY)
- `add-storage-method.md` walks the full touchpoint list: trait, `S3DdbStorage` impl, `FakeStorage`, conformance suite case, tracing span, README/CODEMAP refresh
- Docs cite spec section numbers so agents can jump to authority

## Out of Scope
- ADRs for storage decisions (written when decisions occur, per §23.5)
- Skills-infrastructure scaffolding (foundation/agent-harnessing epics)

## Testing
CI docs checks (link/lint) as available; `make codemap` runs clean. No code layers apply (§19.1).

## Demo
`make codemap` shows the storage entry; a fresh agent following `add-storage-method.md` can list every file a new method touches.

nodes.title: Raw access: latest-revocation pointer, revocations/ objects, audit items
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide raw access patterns for the remaining §8.1/§8.2 surfaces: `revocations/{tree_size}.signed` objects, the `latest-revocation` pointer item, and `audit#{tree_size}` items written by the self-auditor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `write_revocation(tree_size, bytes)`: write-once object at the §8.1 revocation key, then epoch-conditioned update of `latest-revocation` (`tree_size`, `s3_key`, `signed_at`, `epoch` per §8.2)
- `read_latest_revocation` typed read; `NotFound` before first revocation list
- `put_audit_record(tree_size, record)` / `query_audit_records(range)` over the `audit#` SK pattern (§20.2 self-auditor step 6)
- All mutating KV writes carry the epoch condition (§8.3); pointer tree_size monotonic

## Out of Scope
- Revocation list format, signing, and distribution (revocation epic, §16)
- Self-auditor verification logic (observability epic, §25.8)

## Testing
Unit + property (memory backend, §19.2); LocalStack via stor-conformance-suite (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p storage revocation_audit`; doctest writing a revocation object and reading back the pointer.

nodes.title: Tracing spans and cache metrics on every facade operation
nodes.description:
## Goal
Instrument the storage facade per §20.1: every DDB and S3 call is a `tracing` span, and tile cache hit/miss is instrumented, so issuance is traceable end-to-end once the CA service exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every `Storage` method opens a span with structured fields: operation, object key or SK, epoch where applicable, byte counts
- Tile cache exposes hit/miss/eviction as span events/counters consumable by the metrics layer (§20.1)
- Error paths record the `StorageError` variant on the span
- No secrets or entry payload bytes in span fields
- Overhead bounded: instrumented unit-test suite still completes within the §19.1 <30s budget

## Out of Scope
- OTel exporter wiring, dashboards, SLOs (observability epic)
- HSM spans (ca-service checkpoint-signer)

## Testing
Unit with a capturing `tracing` subscriber asserting span names/fields per method (§19.1).

## Demo
`RUST_LOG=storage=trace cargo run -p storage --example hydrate_demo` prints a readable span tree for one hydration.

nodes.title: cloud-aws: CloudHSM Hsm implementation via PKCS#11 (config-validated, no cloud spend)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add `cloudhsm.rs` to `cloud-aws` (§9.3): an `Hsm` implementation reusing the PKCS#11 core from `cloud-softhsm`, configured for the CloudHSM client library — keeping the v1 production design honest (§14) without violating the no-AWS-spend constraint (§1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `CloudHsm` implements `Hsm` by delegating to the shared PKCS#11 session layer with CloudHSM-specific module path, cluster cert, and CU credential config (§14.2 Option A context documented)
- `is_fips_validated() == true` for this backend, per §14.4 (FIPS comes from the HSM itself); rustdoc states validation is inherited from hardware, not the binary
- Config validation unit-tested: missing cluster cert / bad module path produce typed errors
- Crate compiles and passes `cargo clippy` with the feature enabled; explicitly marked untested-against-real-hardware in rustdoc and README (§1 non-goals: no production deployment)
- SoftHSM-backed test exercises the shared PKCS#11 code path this impl delegates to

## Out of Scope
- Real CloudHSM cluster provisioning or CDK for HSM (no spend, §1); cross-region key replication ceremony (multi-region epic, §14.2); FIPS CI release gates (§14.4, foundation-infra/ca-service hardening)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config validation, module resolution; shared-path coverage via SoftHSM integration tests

## Demo
`cargo build -p cloud-aws --features cloudhsm && cargo test -p cloud-aws cloudhsm` shows config-validation tests green.

nodes.title: Batch builder: intake queue + cadence/size batch emission
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the in-memory entry intake queue (spec 8.4) and the batch builder that drains it: accumulate `LogEntry` values and emit a batch on cadence (2-5s, dev-configurable faster per spec 18.1) or when full at 256 entries (spec 11.1 step 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Bounded mpsc-backed queue implements `EntryIntake`; overflow returns `IntakeError::QueueFull` (backpressure, no silent drops)
- Batch emitted when cadence timer fires (via injected Clock) or size reaches 256, whichever first
- Per-entry completion handles let submitters await their assigned Index/certificate after commit (feeds spec 11.1 step 9 delivery)
- FIFO order preserved: entries appear in batches in submission order
- Cadence/size limits configurable; dev profile uses faster cadence
- Graceful drain on shutdown: queued entries emitted or failed with `Shutdown`

## Out of Scope
- Index allocation, lease checks, tree update (downstream tickets)
- Lease renewer interaction (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Unit; property: arbitrary submit sequences place every entry in exactly one batch, order preserved (spec 19.2)
- Loom: concurrent submitters vs builder drain interleavings (spec 19.12)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-ca-service batch_builder`; example bin feeds 1000 entries and prints batch boundaries/cadence behavior.

nodes.title: Injected Clock abstraction (SystemClock + FakeClock)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the injected `Clock` interface the CA service requires (spec 11.4 struct field, 18.4 time travel): a `Clock` trait plus `SystemClock` and a controllable `FakeClock`, so batch cadence, lease-expiry guards, and checkpoint timestamps are deterministic in tests and time-travel-ready in dev.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Clock` trait with `now()`; `SystemClock` for prod, `FakeClock` with `set`/`advance` for dev/test
- All CA-service time reads go through `Clock` (no direct `SystemTime::now` in ca-service crates, enforced by a clippy `disallowed-methods` deny in CI)
- Dev-mode wiring can select `FakeClock` via config
- FakeClock is `Send + Sync` and safely shareable across the batch builder and signer tasks

## Out of Scope
- Admin API control of the fake clock (admin-surface epic)
- `make time-advance` target wiring (local dev experience epic, spec 18.4)

## Testing
- Unit: FakeClock advance/set semantics; trait-object usage from async tasks

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-ca-service clock`; example test shows advancing FakeClock triggers a batch-cadence tick.

nodes.title: Commit: linearization point (S3 checkpoint + DDB transaction)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 8, the linearization point (spec 11.1-11.2): PutObject of the signed checkpoint at its deterministic key, then a DDB TransactWriteItems that updates the latest-checkpoint pointer and marks the batch Committed, all epoch-conditioned.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `commit_checkpoint(cp, batch_id, epoch)` enforces S3-first-DDB-second ordering (spec 11.2)
- DDB transaction failure leaves only a harmless orphan S3 checkpoint; test proves readers still see the old latest-checkpoint (spec 11.3 row 8)
- Re-commit of the same checkpoint is idempotent (deterministic key, identical bytes)
- Epoch mismatch on either txn item returns `LostLease`; no partial commit possible
- Kani harness: the latest-checkpoint transition is atomic - any observer sees the old or new pointer, never an intermediate state (spec 19.12)

## Out of Scope
- Orphan-cleanup Lambda (observability/pruning epics)
- Lease/epoch protocol itself (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Unit with memory-backend fault injection at each sub-step; integration (LocalStack S3+DDB); Kani

## Demo
After a demo batch: `awslocal s3 ls checkpoints/` and the DDB latest-checkpoint item agree on tree_size; kill the txn via fault flag and observe the orphan being ignored.

nodes.title: Single-region issuance end-to-end demo + E2E test
nodes.description:
## Goal
Deliver the Phase 3 exit criterion (spec 24): single-region issuance end-to-end on a laptop. Extend `make demo` (spec 18.1) to launch the CA service in dev mode against LocalStack + SoftHSM with a sample ACME client auto-issuing certs in a loop, plus a shell E2E test (spec 19.13 style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo` brings up CA service + sample ACME client on the localstack-dev-env compose; seed step initializes counter and dev lease
- Certs issue continuously; checkpoints advance in S3 (`checkpoints/` grows, latest-checkpoint pointer follows)
- `tests/e2e/single-region-issuance.sh`: issue via ACME client -> assert entry object exists -> assert cert inclusion verifies against the latest checkpoint (verification via a small helper bin since mtcctl belongs to admin-surface)
- Script wired into `make test-e2e` (spec 18.8) and CI integration job
- Cold `make demo` reaches first issued cert within the 60-second target (spec 18.1)

## Out of Scope
- Admin UI and self-auditor panes of the demo (their epics)
- Multi-region simulation `make demo-multiregion` (multi-region epic, spec 18.3)

## Testing
- E2E (shell, spec 19.13); integration (compose bring-up smoke)

## Demo
`make demo` then `make test-e2e`; watch the ACME client loop print issued serials while checkpoints advance.

nodes.title: Atomic index allocation via counter UpdateItem with epoch check
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 3 (spec 11.1): atomic index-range allocation against the `counter` item (spec 8.2) via UpdateItem with `ConditionExpression epoch = :epoch`, upholding the counter-never-decreases invariant (spec 11.2). Mirrors the exemplar ticket in spec 25.4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `allocate_indices(n, epoch) -> Result<(Index, Index), AllocateError>` on the storage facade
- Returns `AllocateError::LostLease` on conditional check failure (spec 11.3 row 3)
- Counter is monotonic: abandoned ranges are never reused (gaps handled by ca-abandoned-batch-recovery)
- Idempotent counter bootstrap initializes `next_index=0` for an empty log
- Property test: concurrent allocations produce non-overlapping ranges (spec 25.4)
- Kani harness: no two successful allocations overlap (spec 19.12, 25.4)

## Out of Scope
- Lease renewer (multi-region epic)
- Null-entry gap filling (ca-abandoned-batch-recovery)

## Testing
- Unit, property (proptest), integration (LocalStack DDB), Kani

## Demo
`cargo test --features integration allocate`; `awslocal dynamodb get-item` shows the counter advancing after a demo batch.

nodes.title: CaService issue_batch orchestrator (steps 1-9 wired)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire the full `issue_batch` pipeline of spec 11.4: lease check, index allocation, batch state, entry writes, tree update, checkpoint signing, commit, and delivery, with the `IssueError` taxonomy and the failure handling of the spec 11.3 table.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `CaService` struct per spec 11.4 with injected Storage, Hsm, Clock, TileCache, intake receiver
- Every spec 11.3 failure row has a test asserting the specified effect and recovery (lease fail -> NotPrimary; counter fail -> batch abandoned/stand down; S3 partial -> retry remaining; HSM fail -> backoff; DDB txn fail -> orphan tolerated)
- Epoch captured once per batch and used in every conditional write (spec 11.2)
- In-memory checkpoint cache holds the last N checkpoints by tree_size, updated after each commit (spec 8.4)
- Lease-check-to-commit window is lock-free: no locks held across awaits (spec 11.4)
- Tracing spans per lifecycle step for later observability wiring

## Out of Scope
- ACME endpoint and service binary (separate tickets)
- Standby 503 mode and lease renewal (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Unit: full pipeline on memory backend; integration: full pipeline on LocalStack + SoftHSM; Loom/Shuttle: intake submission concurrent with batch emission (spec 19.12)

## Demo
`cargo test --features integration issue_batch_e2e` issues a batch and asserts the checkpoint advanced and certs verify.

nodes.title: Checkpoint signer: typestate builder + HSM signing
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 7 (spec 11.1): a typestate `CheckpointBuilder` (spec 22.2) over (log_id, tree_size, root_hash, signed_at), canonical `checkpoint_signing_input` bytes, and signing via the `Hsm` trait with ECDSA P-256 (v1 per spec 14.1), with retry/backoff on HSM failure (spec 11.3 row 7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Builder rejects incomplete checkpoints at compile time (spec 22.2)
- Signing input serialization is deterministic; pinned test vector guards it
- Signature verifies against the HSM public key; checkpoint object bytes match spec 8.1 `checkpoints/{tree_size}.signed` format
- Transient HSM failure retried with backoff; persistent failure surfaces a distinct alert-worthy error
