- Benchmark measures signing latency against SoftHSM with the <100ms p99 target (spec 14.3) reported via `make bench`

## Out of Scope
- ML-DSA (v2 algorithm, feature-flagged in core-mtc-library)
- CloudHSM/production keys and rotation ceremonies (spec 14.2)
- Commit of the signed checkpoint (ca-commit-transaction)

## Testing
- Unit (fake Hsm); integration (SoftHSM PKCS#11); performance bench (spec 19.11)

## Demo
`cargo test --features integration checkpoint_signer`; `make bench` prints a signing latency histogram vs the 100ms p99 target.

nodes.title: make demo: 60-second single-region demo orchestration with dev-mode profile
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the 60-second demo (§18.1): `make demo` brings up LocalStack, SoftHSM2, the CA service in dev mode, and the admin UI from a fresh clone with one command — the flagship promise of §1 and the Phase 3 roadmap exit criterion (§24).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo` orchestrates: compose bring-up (via localstack-dev-env), SoftHSM token init + key generation, resource provisioning (buckets/tables), CA service launch with dev-mode profile, admin UI reachable at `localhost:8080`
- Dev-mode profile (`config/dev.toml`): fast batch cadence (seconds), SoftHSM PKCS#11, looser timing — consumed by the CA service's config loading
- Readiness gating: returns only when health endpoints (§20.5) report ready, with per-component progress output
- `make demo-down` tears down cleanly; re-running `make demo` is idempotent
- Warm start (images pulled, workspace built) completes in <60 s on a dev laptop
- Any component failure names the component and points at `make doctor`

## Out of Scope
- Auto-issuing ACME loop (`dev-demo-issuance-loop`); self-auditor wiring (`dev-audit-demo-wiring`)
- FakeClock wiring (`dev-time-advance`); multi-region topology (`dev-multiregion-harness`)

## Testing
- Integration: provisioning scripts against LocalStack
- E2E: bring-up/tear-down smoke (formal CI gate lands in `dev-demo-smoke`)

## Demo
`git clone && make demo` → open `localhost:8080`, watch batches advance; `mtcctl status` shows a live CA.

nodes.title: Define EntryIntake trait and LogEntry types (adapter seam)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Establish the source-agnostic Stage-1/Stage-2 seam from day one (spec 10.2, 10.4, 25.9): `LogEntry` (tbs_cert bytes, source_type, source_id, submitted_at), a `SourceType` enum, and the async `EntryIntake` trait every adapter (including native ACME) funnels through.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate exports `LogEntry`, `SourceType`, `EntryIntake` matching spec 10.2 semantics
- `submit_entry(entry) -> Result<Index, IntakeError>` resolves with the assigned index; `IntakeError` covers QueueFull, NotPrimary, Shutdown
- `source_type`/`source_id` flow through so batch state can persist them (spec 8.2, 10.2 audit traceability)
- No ACME-specific types leak into the trait; ACME is one adapter among many (spec 10.4)
- Rustdoc documents the adapter contract of spec 10.3

## Out of Scope
- Queue implementation (batch-builder)
- ACME endpoint (ca-acme-core, ca-acme-issuance)
- Non-ACME adapters (post-v1 adapter-pattern epic)

## Testing
- Unit: trait usable via mock impl; error taxonomy exercised
- Property: SourceType/LogEntry serde round-trip (spec 19.2)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-ca-service intake` green; `cargo doc` shows the documented adapter seam.

nodes.title: Tree updater: incremental tile computation and persistence
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 6 (spec 11.1): given the current tree size and a batch of new leaves, compute affected interior nodes with tree-primitives, produce the new root and the set of new/updated tiles, reading existing tiles through the storage facade's LRU tile cache (spec 8.4) and writing new tiles to S3 (spec 8.1 layout).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `update_tree(start, entries) -> (new_root, new_tiles)` touches only tiles affected by the append
- Partial right-edge tiles handled correctly across batch boundaries (growing rightmost tile rewritten; full tiles immutable thereafter)
- Root matches a reference in-memory Merkle tree for arbitrary append sequences
- Tiles written via storage facade `write_tiles`; tile key layout matches spec 8.1
- Full (immutable) tiles served from the LRU cache unconditionally; the growing right-edge partial tile is re-read on each batch and never served stale from cache (spec 8.4)

## Out of Scope
- Inclusion-proof serving (read-path epic)
- Checkpoint signing (checkpoint-signer)
- Kani proofs of tree primitives themselves (core-mtc-library epic)

## Testing
- Unit; property: append preserves previously-valid inclusion proofs, identical leaves yield identical roots (spec 19.2); integration (LocalStack S3)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-ca-service tree_updater`; example appends 10k leaves across batches and prints root evolution plus tile-write counts.

nodes.title: Admin API auth: SigV4 verification middleware + CLI request signing
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement authentication for the admin surface per §17.3: AWS IAM via signed requests on the API, with mtcctl signing requests from the standard AWS credential chain, plus a dev-mode bypass so everything still runs on a laptop (§1 non-goals, §18).

## Acceptance Criteria
- tower middleware on `crates/admin` API routes verifies SigV4 signatures; unauthenticated requests get 401 with the shared error model
- Privileged operations are tagged in `api/admin.openapi.yaml` (e.g. `x-privileged: true`) and the middleware enforces an elevated principal for them (403 otherwise)
- mtcctl signs requests using the AWS default credential chain; works against LocalStack-style dummy credentials
- Dev bypass requires BOTH a `dev-auth` cargo feature and `MTC_DEV_AUTH=off` config; a test asserts a build without the feature returns 401 regardless of the config flag
- htmx UI form posts hit the same middleware-protected API routes; dev bypass covers them in `make demo`; non-dev browser auth is documented as out of scope for v1 (laptop-only, §1)

## Out of Scope
- CLI confirmation prompts (adm-privileged-confirm)
- Real IAM policy authoring / CDK roles (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit: signature verification accept/reject, privileged-tag enforcement, dev bypass gating
- Integration: mtcctl against test server with dummy creds; tampered signature rejected

## Demo
`mtcctl status` succeeds with dummy AWS creds; `curl` without signature gets 401 (dev bypass off).

nodes.title: Batch operations: mtcctl batch list/inspect + Batches UI page
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl batch list` and `mtcctl batch inspect` plus the Batches UI view with status and drill-down (§17.3, §17.4 key views).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: list recent batches (paginated, newest first) and get batch by ID with full details (entry count, tree range, checkpoint ref, timestamps, status)
- Handlers read via the storage facade; work against memory backend and LocalStack
- `mtcctl batch list` human table + `--output json`; `mtcctl batch inspect <id>` shows full details; unknown ID exits non-zero with a clean error
- Batches UI page lists batches with status and links to a drill-down partial (hx-get); list auto-updates on batch-sealed SSE events when the stream exists
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented (§17.5)

## Out of Scope
- Tree visualization of batch contents (observability epic)
- Per-cert lookup (adm-cert-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers with seeded memory-backend batches; pagination edges (empty log, single batch)
- Integration: against LocalStack-backed facade
- E2E: `tests/e2e/batch-list.sh` — issue certs, assert new batch appears via CLI

## Demo
`make demo`, wait one batch cadence, `mtcctl batch list` then `mtcctl batch inspect <id>`; same drill-down in UI.

nodes.title: Cert operations: mtcctl cert issue/lookup + Cert lookup UI page
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl cert issue` (test issuance via the ACME adapter) and `mtcctl cert lookup` (per-cert info by index or PEM), plus the Cert lookup UI view (§17.3, §17.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: trigger test issuance for a domain; lookup cert by index or uploaded PEM returning TBSCert contents, batch ref, checkpoint, and current status
- `mtcctl cert issue --domain X` outputs the issued cert (PEM to stdout); `mtcctl cert lookup --index N` / `--pem FILE` renders details, `--output json` stable for scripting (§19.13 example)
- Cert lookup UI page: form (index or PEM paste) rendering the same fields (parity)
- Nonexistent index returns 404 -> non-zero CLI exit with clean message
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Full forensics fields — served-proof audit trail, pruning status (§20.2; observability epic extends this endpoint)
- `cert revoke` (adm-revocation-ops)
- The ACME endpoint itself (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers with memory backend; PEM parse failure paths
- Integration: issue-then-lookup against LocalStack demo stack
- E2E: `tests/e2e/issuance-and-verification.sh` per §19.13

## Demo
`mtcctl cert issue --domain test.example.com > /tmp/cert.pem && mtcctl cert lookup --pem /tmp/cert.pem`.

nodes.title: SSE stream: real-time state push into the UI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the Server-Sent Events stream (§17.4): CA service state changes (new batches, lease events, audit results) push into the UI without polling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/admin/src/handlers/sse.rs` exposes an SSE endpoint on the admin app (axum `Sse` responder)
- Typed event enum (batch-sealed, lease-changed, audit-completed, checkpoint-signed) serialized as named SSE events with JSON data
- Bridged from the CA service's in-process notification channel via the AppState seam; slow consumers are dropped/lagged without blocking the service (broadcast semantics)
- Layout wires the htmx SSE extension so subscribed partials refresh on matching events; browser reconnect works (retry + Last-Event-ID tolerated)
- Heartbeat/keepalive comments prevent idle proxy timeouts

## Out of Scope
- Producing the events inside the CA service (ca-service epic)
- Per-page partials consuming specific events (per-operation tickets)

## Testing
- Unit: event serialization, broadcast lag/drop behavior
- Integration: test client subscribes, injects events via AppState, asserts stream frames; disconnect/reconnect test

## Demo
`make demo`, open dashboard, watch batch tiles update live as the sample ACME client issues certs — no page refresh.

nodes.title: Status + log inspect: mtcctl status, log inspect, live dashboard
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the Phase 3 'Admin API + CLI + UI for status/inspection' slice: `mtcctl status` (service status, lease, checkpoint) and `mtcctl log inspect` (log size, recent batches), plus a dashboard showing overall health, current state, and growth rate (§17.3, §17.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations for status and log-state added to `api/admin.openapi.yaml`; `make api-gen` regenerates cleanly (§17.5 flow)
- Server handlers read live CA state: role, latest checkpoint (age, tree size), recent batch summaries; the lease block renders a 'single-region' placeholder value until lease-epoch-protocol lands (adm-lease-ops replaces it)
- `mtcctl status` and `mtcctl log inspect` render human tables and stable `--output json|yaml`
- Dashboard page shows the same fields (parity) plus growth rate computed as entries/hour over the last N batches; auto-refresh via `hx-trigger` polling, with SSE swap-over tracked in adm-sse-stream
- CLI help text and UI tooltips document each field (§17.5 step 7)

## Out of Scope
- Batch drill-down (adm-batch-ops)
- Proof operations (adm-proof-ops)
- Failover readiness (adm-failover-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against memory backend with seeded state
- Integration: LocalStack-backed service, CLI asserts real values
- E2E: `tests/e2e/status.sh` drives mtcctl per §19.13

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl status` and `mtcctl log inspect`; dashboard shows matching numbers.

nodes.title: ACME server core: directory, nonces, accounts, JWS verification
nodes.description:
## Goal
Lay the RFC 8555 foundation for the native ACME adapter (spec 10, 24 Phase 3): axum routes for directory, new-nonce, and new-account, with ES256 JWS verification, anti-replay nonce handling, and an ACME problem-document error type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Axum routes: `/acme/directory`, new-nonce, new-account per RFC 8555 sections 7.1.1, 7.2, 7.3
- JWS (ES256) verified: signature, protected header (alg/nonce/url) checks, account key binding; failures return ACME problem documents (badNonce, badSignatureAlgorithm, malformed)
- Nonces are single-use: replaying a consumed nonce returns badNonce and every response carries a fresh Replay-Nonce header
- Account store keyed by JWK thumbprint (RFC 7638); re-registering an existing key returns the existing account
- Fuzz target for JWS/request-body parsing added per spec 19.3 (no panic on arbitrary bytes)

## Out of Scope
- Orders, authorizations, challenges (ca-acme-orders)
- finalize/cert issuance (ca-acme-issuance)
- External account binding; admin surfaces (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit; fuzz (cargo-fuzz JWS/body target, spec 19.3); integration: in-process client fetches directory, obtains nonce, registers account

## Demo
Run the service and `curl localhost:PORT/acme/directory`; scripted client registers an account and demonstrates a rejected replayed nonce.

nodes.title: ACME finalize -> EntryIntake -> MTC cert delivery
nodes.description:
## Goal
Bridge ACME to the log pipeline as one adapter among many (spec 10.4): finalize validates the CSR against the ready order, builds a spec-compliant TBSCertificateLogEntry, submits via `EntryIntake` with source_type "native-acme", awaits the committed index, and serves the assembled MTC certificate (spec 11.1 step 9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- finalize moves order processing -> valid only after the entry commits; cert URL serves the assembled MTC certificate
- LogEntry carries source_type="native-acme" and source_id=order id, visible on the batch state item (spec 10.2 traceability)
- Intake `NotPrimary` maps to HTTP 503 (spec 11.3 row 1); QueueFull maps to retry-after
- finalize retry is idempotent: re-submitting a finalized order returns the same cert, no duplicate log entry
- CSR validation failures produce ACME problem documents without touching intake

## Out of Scope
- Other adapters (AWS PCA etc., adapter-pattern epic)
- Proof serving to relying parties (read-path epic)

## Testing
- Unit; integration: full order -> finalize -> cert against the memory-backend pipeline; E2E covered by ca-e2e-demo

## Demo
Demo ACME client issues one cert end-to-end; `awslocal dynamodb query` shows the batch item with source_type=native-acme and the order's source_id.

nodes.title: ACME order/authz/http-01 flow with typestate state machine
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the RFC 8555 order lifecycle on top of the ACME core: new-order, authorization, and http-01 challenge routes, with the order state machine enforced by typestate (spec 22.4) and dev-mode auto-validation so the 60-second demo issues without real DNS (spec 18.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Routes: new-order, order fetch, authz fetch, challenge respond per RFC 8555 7.4-7.5
- Order transitions pending -> ready enforced at compile time via typestate (spec 22.4); invalid transitions are unrepresentable
- http-01 challenge: dev-mode flag auto-validates instantly; non-dev mode performs the real HTTP token fetch
- Failed/expired authorizations produce ACME problem documents and mark the order invalid
- Fuzz targets extended to order/challenge request payloads (spec 19.3)

## Out of Scope
- finalize/cert issuance (ca-acme-issuance)
- DNS-01/TLS-ALPN-01 challenge types; real DNS/HTTP challenge infrastructure

## Testing
- Unit; fuzz (spec 19.3); integration: in-process ACME client walks account -> order -> authz -> ready

## Demo
Scripted client walks a full order to ready state against the dev-mode server.

nodes.title: Batch state persistence (batch#{batchId} DDB items)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 4 (spec 11.1): persist batch state as `batch#{batchId}` items with status, start_index, end_index, leaf_count, epoch, created_at, committed_at, source_type, source_id per the spec 8.2 schema, including the adapter-traceability fields (spec 10.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `persist_batch_state(batch_id, start, end, status, epoch)` writes a Pending item with all spec 8.2 attributes
- `BatchStatus` is a closed-set enum (Pending/Committed/Abandoned) per spec 22.3
- `source_type`/`source_id` from the batch's entries are persisted for audit traceability (spec 10.2)
- Epoch included on the conditional write (spec 11.2)
- Query helper lists Pending batches (needed by recovery scans)

## Out of Scope
- The commit transaction that flips Pending to Committed (ca-commit-transaction)
- Admin inspection surfaces (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backend), integration (LocalStack DDB)

## Demo
After a demo-mode batch: `awslocal dynamodb query` on `log#{logId}` shows the batch item with source_type=native-acme.

nodes.title: MTC certificate assembly and delivery handles
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 9 (spec 11.1): after commit, build the deliverable MTC certificate for each batch entry - TBSCertificateLogEntry + MTCProof (inclusion proof against the just-committed checkpoint) + CA signature - and complete the per-entry delivery handles opened at intake.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Inclusion proof generated from the freshly written tiles for each index in the batch
- Assembled certificate serializes and round-trips via mtc-serialization
- Each assembled cert verifies against the committed checkpoint using tree-primitives verification
- Completion handles resolve with (Index, certificate); failures resolve with a typed error so ACME finalize can report accurately

## Out of Scope
- Proof-server Lambda and relying-party verification library (read-path epic, spec 12)
- ACME transport of the cert (ca-acme-issuance)

## Testing
- Unit; property: every entry of an arbitrary committed batch yields a verifying certificate (spec 19.2)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-ca-service cert_assembly`; example prints one issued certificate and locally verifies its inclusion proof.

nodes.title: Parallel S3 entry writer with partial-failure retry
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 5 (spec 11.1): serialize each batch entry and write N parallel S3 objects under `entries/` using the fixed-width zero-padded key layout of spec 8.1, with retry of only the missing objects on partial failure (spec 11.3 row 5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `write_entries(start, entries)` performs bounded-concurrency parallel PutObject
- Key format matches spec 8.1 (`entries/000/000/000000.entry`, lexicographic = index order)
- Partial failure retries only unwritten objects; re-put of an identical immutable object is safe/idempotent (spec 11.2, 8.1 invariants)
- Entry bytes produced via mtc-serialization; round-trip verified
- Fault-injection test proves resumption after a mid-batch failure

## Out of Scope
- Tile writes (tree-updater)
- Null-entry gap fill (ca-abandoned-batch-recovery)

## Testing
- Unit with memory-backend fault injection; property: key encoding is order-preserving and reversible; integration (LocalStack S3)

## Demo
After a demo batch: `awslocal s3 ls s3://mtc-log-local/entries/ --recursive` shows contiguous zero-padded entry objects.

nodes.title: Write-path lease check with epoch capture (single-region)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement write-path step 1 (spec 11.1, 11.4): read the lease via the storage facade, verify this holder is primary, reject with `NotPrimary`/`LeaseExpiringSoon` (expires_at < now + 5s), and capture the lease epoch into the service's `current_epoch` atomic for the batch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `read_lease` consulted at the top of every batch; epoch captured once per batch (spec 11.4)
- Wrong region/holder yields `NotPrimary` (maps to HTTP 503 at the edge per spec 11.3 row 1)
- Expiring-soon guard uses injected Clock with the 5s margin from spec 11.4
- Single-region dev lease provider seeds a static long-lived lease item (region, holder_id, epoch=1) so the write path runs without the multi-region protocol
- Epoch value is what all downstream conditional writes use (spec 11.2)

## Out of Scope
- Lease renewal, takeover, epoch increment (multi-region epic, spec 8.3)
- Standby-mode 503 service behavior (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backend): happy path, wrong region, expiring-soon
- Integration: lease item in LocalStack DDB

## Demo
Run dev binary with seeded lease: batches proceed; delete the lease item and observe `NotPrimary` rejection.

nodes.title: ca-service binary: config, wiring, health, graceful shutdown
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the runnable `ca-service` binary: config loading, backend wiring per spec 9.4 (memory vs LocalStack/AWS vs SoftHSM), mounting ACME routes plus minimal health endpoints, dev-mode flags (fast cadence, fake clock), and graceful shutdown that drains the intake queue.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One binary starts orchestrator + ACME server from a single config; backend selection (memory/localstack) requires no code change (spec 9.4)
- `/healthz` and `/readyz` endpoints respond (minimal subset of spec 20.5)
- SIGTERM drains the in-flight batch before exit; queued-but-unbatched entries fail with `Shutdown`
- Dev profile enables fast cadence and FakeClock (spec 18.1, 18.4)
- Works under cargo-watch hot reload (spec 18.7)

## Out of Scope
- Fargate/CDK deployment (foundation-infra epic)
- Admin API/UI routes (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit: config parsing/validation; integration: spawn binary against LocalStack + SoftHSM, hit healthz, issue one cert

## Demo
`cargo run -p ca-service` then `curl localhost:PORT/healthz`; issue a cert with the ACME test script.

nodes.title: Sample ACME client auto-issuing certs in a loop for make demo
nodes.description:
## Goal
Complete the §18.1 demo loop: a sample ACME client that auto-issues certificates continuously so `make demo` shows a living CA (batches filling, tree growing) with zero manual input.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Demo issuer (sidecar process/container started by `make demo`) drives the ACME endpoint in a loop using seeded names from `dev-entrygen`
- Rate configurable via the dev profile (default ~1 cert per 2 s); clean shutdown with `make demo-down`
- Issued certs visible in the admin UI and via `mtcctl cert list` within one dev-mode batch interval
- `DEMO_ISSUER=off make demo` disables the loop for quiet debugging
- Loop logs are structured and prefixed so demo output stays readable

## Out of Scope
- ACME endpoint implementation (ca-service epic)
- Load/soak-level issuance rates (§19.7, testing epic)

## Testing
- Unit: rate limiter / backoff logic
- Integration: one loop iteration issues successfully against the dev stack
- E2E: demo smoke asserts cert count increases over a 30 s window

## Demo
`make demo` → admin UI batch view fills with new entries every few seconds without touching anything.

nodes.title: CI demo smoke test enforcing the 60-second budget
nodes.description:
## Goal
CI-enforced smoke test and timing budget for the demo (§18.1): prove `make demo` works from a clean checkout and stays fast, so the flagship 60-second promise never rots.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tests/e2e/demo-smoke.sh`: runs `make demo`, waits for readiness, asserts admin UI returns 200, `mtcctl status` succeeds, at least one signed checkpoint exists, then `make demo-down` leaves no containers
- Records wall-clock bring-up time; fails if warm start exceeds 60 s (budget constant defined in one place; cold image pulls excluded from the hard gate)
- Wired as a required CI job (§22.13) using cached images and a prebuilt workspace
- On failure, per-component logs dumped as CI artifacts
- Script passes shellcheck

## Out of Scope
- Multi-region smoke (`dev-multiregion-harness` ships its own)
- Full issuance-path E2E scenario suites (§19.13, testing epic)

## Testing
- E2E: this ticket is the E2E layer for the demo path

## Demo
CI run shows "demo-smoke: PASS (42 s)"; locally `tests/e2e/demo-smoke.sh` gives the same verdict.

nodes.title: million-entries fixture: deterministic large-log snapshot
nodes.description:
## Goal
The `million-entries` fixture (§18.5): a deterministic large-log snapshot for performance testing, realistic demos, and reproducing bugs that only appear at depth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generator (xtask or script) drives the batch builder + tree updater directly (bypassing ACME) with seeded entries from `dev-entrygen`, under FakeClock acceleration
- Produces exactly 1,000,000 entries; final tree head is byte-stable across regenerations (expected root documented)
- Saved via the fixture framework as `fixtures/million-entries` with provenance (seed, generator version) in the manifest
- `make fixture-load name=million-entries` restores it and a sampled inclusion proof verifies via `mtcctl log inclusion`
- Generation is streamed (bounded memory) and completes in documented, laptop-feasible time

## Out of Scope
- Fixture engine changes (`dev-fixture-engine`, `dev-fixture-targets`)
- Benchmarks consuming the fixture (`make bench`, testing epic)

## Testing
- Integration: reduced-size (10k) generation asserted byte-stable in CI; full 1M run in the nightly lane
- E2E: load fixture → sampled inclusion proofs verify via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=million-entries` → admin UI shows a 1M-entry tree; proof verification round-trips instantly.

nodes.title: make dev: cargo-watch hot reload of the CA service
nodes.description:
## Goal
`make dev` hot reload (§18.7): `cargo-watch` rebuilds and restarts the CA service on source change while LocalStack/SoftHSM stay up, keeping the edit→observe loop at seconds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make dev` starts (or reuses) the demo infrastructure, then runs the CA service in the foreground under `cargo watch` with debounce
- Watches `crates/`; ignores `target/`, `fixtures/`, `docs/`
- Restarted service re-attaches to existing LocalStack state — no re-provisioning; admin UI reflects the restart within one refresh
- Rebuild-to-serving latency for a one-line change measured by the E2E script and documented in `docs/dev-environment.md` (target: a few seconds in debug mode per §18.7)
- Works alongside the demo issuance loop (issuer retries through restarts)

## Out of Scope
- Admin UI asset live-reload (admin-surface epic)
- Watch-triggered test runs (developers use `cargo watch -x test` ad hoc)

## Testing
- Unit: none (glue)
- E2E: script touches a source file, asserts the service process is replaced and health returns ready

## Demo
`make dev`, edit a log line in the batch builder, save → service restarts in seconds and the new line appears in output.

nodes.title: mtcctl repl: interactive, scriptable CLI command shell
nodes.description:
## Goal
`mtcctl repl` (§18.6): an interactive, scriptable command shell over the full mtcctl command tree — the agent-preferred REPL (OQ-10): deterministic, output-captured, no per-command process spawn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl repl` starts a readline loop (history, Ctrl-D exit) dispatching lines through the existing clap command tree in-process, reusing one API client connection
- Non-interactive: `mtcctl repl --script file` and piped stdin execute line-by-line, echoing commands; stop-on-error by default with `--keep-going` override
- Deterministic output: no ANSI when stdout is not a TTY; `--output json` respected per command; each command's output delimited for machine parsing
- Built-ins: `help`, `exit`; a failing command does not kill the interactive session
- Exit code reflects last (or first failing) command in script mode

## Out of Scope
- New admin operations (only re-exposes existing commands)
- evcxr REPL (`dev-repl-evcxr`)

## Testing
- Unit: line parsing, dispatch, stop-on-error semantics
- E2E: shell test pipes a script through `mtcctl repl` against the demo stack and asserts delimited JSON outputs (§19.13)

## Demo
`mtcctl repl` → `status`, `batch list`, `cert issue --domain demo.test` interactively; then the same via `--script` with byte-identical output.

nodes.title: Time travel: dev-mode clock admin API and make time-advance
nodes.description:
## Goal
Time travel (§18.4): dev-mode admin API control of the FakeClock plus `make time-advance days=N`, enabling instant exploration of expiry, batch cadence, and retention behavior without waiting wall-clock time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dev-only admin API routes (enabled only in dev mode): `POST /dev/clock/advance` accepting `{days|hours|seconds}`, `GET /dev/clock` returning simulated now; absent/404 in non-dev builds
- Dev-mode wiring hands the shared `FakeClock` instance to the CA service's `Arc<dyn Clock>` injection point so cadence loops and validity checks respond immediately to advancement
- `make time-advance days=N` calls the endpoint and prints old → new simulated time
- Advancing past certificate validity windows makes them expire, observable via `mtcctl` and the admin UI
- OpenAPI spec updated for the dev routes (§17.2 codegen pipeline)

## Out of Scope
- FakeClock primitive (`dev-fake-clock`)
- Time-triggered pruning/retention flows (pruning epic verifies using this tool)

## Testing
- Unit: route handlers, dev-mode gating
- Integration: advancing during a running dev stack shifts the next batch timestamp
- E2E: `make time-advance days=400` → previously valid cert reported expired (§18.4)

## Demo
`make demo`, issue a cert, `make time-advance days=400`, `mtcctl cert lookup` shows it expired — under a minute of wall time.

nodes.title: Structured logging + OpenTelemetry tracing foundation (telemetry crate)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create the shared telemetry crate providing the structured-logging and distributed-tracing foundation of §20.1: JSON `tracing` subscriber, standard fields, correlation IDs, redaction, and OTEL export.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/telemetry` exposes an init API installing a `tracing-subscriber` with JSON output (bunyan-style per §20.1)
- Every log entry carries the standard fields: `timestamp, level, message, service, region, correlation_id, log_id, epoch, batch_id` (§20.1)
- Correlation ID generated at request entry and propagated through nested spans; spans emit structured timing data
- Sensitive-data redaction: a marked-sensitive field provably never appears in captured output (unit test)
- Optional OTEL layer via `tracing-opentelemetry` exporting OTLP, enabled by env config (§20.1); otel-collector service added to the dev compose
- Cited types (`LogId`, `Epoch`, `BatchId`) come from core newtypes (§22)

## Out of Scope
- Metric registry/exporters (obs-metrics-core)
- Instrumenting CA-service components (obs-service-instrumentation)

## Testing
- Unit: subscriber output captured and asserted (fields, redaction, correlation propagation)
- Integration: OTLP spans received by local collector in compose (`--features integration`, §19.1)

## Demo
`make demo` then inspect JSON logs for standard fields; `docker compose logs otel-collector` shows exported spans.

nodes.title: E2E-via-CLI harness, shell helpers, and CI job
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the `tests/e2e/` harness per spec 19.13 and 19.1: E2E tests are plain shell scripts driving `mtcctl` against the full demo environment — a deliberate agent affordance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tests/e2e/` layout with a runner (`make e2e`) that boots the demo environment (LocalStack + SoftHSM per 19.1), discovers `*.sh` tests, runs each hermetically, and prints a pass/fail summary
- Shared shell helper library: assertions, wait-for/retry, JSON extraction via jq
- Rust-authored E2E tests supported alongside shell scripts (19.1)
- First smoke test lands: issue -> lookup -> inclusion verified, matching the 19.13 example verbatim
- CI job runs the E2E suite with service logs uploaded on failure

## Out of Scope
- Additional demo-scenario tests (issue/verify/revoke/prune scripts ship with their feature epics)
- Soak-mode load driving (test-soak-harness)

## Testing
- E2E (19.1, 19.13); unit tests for any Rust runner code

## Demo
`make e2e` on a laptop boots the env and passes the issuance-and-verification smoke test.

nodes.title: Docs: adding a new admin operation end-to-end
nodes.description:
## Goal
Document the §17.5 workflow so any contributor or agent can add an admin operation: update OpenAPI -> `make api-gen` -> server handler -> clap subcommand -> htmx UI -> E2E test -> help text/tooltips.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/adding-an-admin-operation.md` walks the seven §17.5 steps using the status/log-inspect operation as the worked example, with real file paths (`api/admin.openapi.yaml`, `crates/admin/src/handlers/`, `crates/mtcctl/`, `crates/admin/templates/`, `tests/e2e/`)
- Documents the parity annotations (`x-cli-command`, `x-ui-view`) and privileged-op tagging conventions
- Documents output-format and exit-code conventions for new subcommands, and the CLI-help/UI-tooltip requirement
- Linked from the repo README/AGENTS context so agents discover it

## Out of Scope
- General agent harness docs (agent-harnessing epic)
- Operation-specific runbooks (observability epic)

## Testing
- Doc-only PR; CI verifies referenced paths exist (simple link/path check script if available)

## Demo
Follow the doc to add a trivial echo operation on a branch; both `mtcctl` and the UI gain it and the parity check passes.

nodes.title: Dev-mode fake clock control endpoint on the admin API
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose the dev-mode fake clock over the admin API (§18.4): the CA service's injected `Clock` is controllable so `make time-advance` (owned by local-dev-experience) has something to call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations (dev-only tag): get current simulated time; advance by duration (e.g. `days=400`)
- Handler drives the injected fake `Clock` through the AppState seam; returns new simulated time
- Compiled/enabled only in dev mode — in non-dev config the routes are absent (404), verified by test
- `mtcctl` dev subcommand (e.g. `mtcctl dev time-advance --days N`) wired for scriptability, marked dev/test only in help
- Advancing time emits a log line with old/new time for auditability

## Out of Scope
- The `Clock` trait and fake-clock implementation (ca-service epic)
- `make time-advance` wrapper target (local-dev-experience epic)

## Testing
- Unit: advance math, dev-gating (routes absent outside dev)
- Integration: advance clock against demo stack, assert service-observed time moved

## Demo
`mtcctl dev time-advance --days 400 && mtcctl status` shows checkpoint timestamps jumped forward.

nodes.title: Automated CLI/UI parity check over the OpenAPI spec
nodes.description:
## Goal
Enforce §17.1 full parity mechanically: a CI-run test walks every operation in `api/admin.openapi.yaml` and fails if it lacks a CLI subcommand or a UI surface mapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Convention: each OpenAPI operation carries `x-cli-command` and `x-ui-view` extensions (or an explicit `x-parity-exempt` with justification)
- Test parses the spec, asserts every `x-cli-command` resolves to a real path in the mtcctl clap tree, and every `x-ui-view` resolves to a registered UI route/template
- Missing or dangling mappings fail `cargo test` with an actionable message naming the operation
- Existing operations annotated; check wired into the standard test run (CI required check via existing pipeline)
- Convention documented for future operation tickets

## Out of Scope
- Runtime behavioral equivalence between CLI and UI (covered by per-operation E2E)
- CI infrastructure itself (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit: the parity test itself, plus negative fixtures (spec with missing annotation fails)

## Demo
Delete an `x-cli-command` line locally, run `cargo test -p admin parity`, watch it fail with the operation named.

nodes.title: Privileged-command confirmation flow (--confirm / --yes)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §17.3 authorization UX: privileged mtcctl commands require explicit `--confirm` or an interactive confirmation prompt, skippable with `--yes` for automation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shared helper in `crates/mtcctl` that privileged subcommands call before issuing the API request
- Behavior: `--confirm` proceeds; interactive TTY prompts y/N; non-TTY without `--confirm`/`--yes` fails with a clear error and non-zero exit
- `--yes` skips prompting (automation path) and is logged to stderr
- Prompt text names the operation and its target (e.g. 'initiate failover to us-west-2')
- Helper adopted by any already-merged privileged command; documented convention for future ones

## Out of Scope
- Server-side privilege enforcement (adm-auth-middleware)
- Specific privileged operations themselves (their own tickets)

## Testing
- Unit: TTY/non-TTY matrix, flag combinations, exit codes
- E2E: shell script asserts a privileged stub refuses without `--yes` and proceeds with it

## Demo
`mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2` prompts; `--yes` proceeds non-interactively.

nodes.title: mtcctl repl: interactive command shell
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl repl` (§17.3, §18.6): an interactive, agent-friendly command shell that reuses the existing clap tree — deterministic, scriptable, output captured.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl repl` starts a line-oriented shell; each line is parsed with the same clap definitions as one-shot invocation (no divergent grammar)
- Works with piped stdin for scripting (reads until EOF, exits 0); errors on a line are reported but do not kill the session in interactive mode
- Session-scoped settings persist (`--output json` set once applies to subsequent commands)
- `help`, `exit`/EOF, and command history (interactive TTY only) supported
- `--output` behavior identical to one-shot mode so captured output is stable

## Out of Scope
- The evcxr Rust REPL / `make repl` (local-dev-experience epic)
- Tab-completion of server-side values

## Testing
- Unit: line parsing reuses clap tree; error-continues semantics
- E2E: pipe a script of commands into `mtcctl repl` against the demo stack, assert outputs

## Demo
`echo -e 'status\nbatch list' | mtcctl repl` prints both results in order.

nodes.title: Seed skill: add-admin-endpoint.md (OpenAPI to server to CLI to UI)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed `.claude/skills/add-admin-endpoint.md` per §23.1: add an admin operation end-to-end — OpenAPI → server → CLI → UI → test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Skill covers the full flow: edit the OpenAPI spec, regenerate code, implement the axum route, add the CLI command, add the UI affordance, add tests at each layer
- "Files involved" lists the 3–5 canonical files for each step
- Common pitfalls include violating CLI/UI parity (§23.2 `cli-ui-parity`) and hand-editing generated code
- Passes `make skill-lint`

## Out of Scope
- Any admin feature work; changes to the OpenAPI codegen pipeline itself

## Testing
- `make skill-lint`; skill validated by using it to trace an existing admin endpoint end-to-end, noted in the PR (§19.13 spirit)

## Demo
Follow the skill to locate every layer (spec, generated code, route, CLI, UI, tests) of an existing admin operation.

nodes.title: Abandoned-batch recovery: null_entry gap fill
nodes.description:
## Goal
Enforce the spec 11.2 invariant that abandoned index ranges become permanent gaps filled with `null_entry`: batches left Pending by a crash or lost lease (spec 11.3 row 3) must be resolved so the tree stays dense and the counter never rolls back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Startup and periodic scan finds Pending batches past a staleness threshold (or with a superseded epoch)
- Their allocated ranges are filled with spec-compliant `null_entry` objects via the entry writer, then the batch is marked Abandoned
- Committed batches are never touched; recovery is idempotent under repeated runs and crashes mid-recovery
- After recovery, the next committed checkpoint's tree_size covers the filled gap and inclusion proofs for the null entries verify against it

## Out of Scope
- Multi-region takeover and epoch fencing semantics (multi-region epic)
- Orphan S3 checkpoint cleanup (observability/pruning epics)

## Testing
- Unit: simulated crash between steps 3 and 8 via memory-backend fault injection; integration: kill/restart against LocalStack

## Demo
Kill the demo service mid-batch (fault flag), restart, and observe the gap filled with null entries while new issuance proceeds at the next indices.

nodes.title: CA service docs: lifecycle, invariants, adapter guide
nodes.description:
## Goal
Meet the epic's documentation obligations (spec 25.6 documentation parallel track): a ca-service crate README with the write-path lifecycle diagram (spec 11.1), critical invariants (spec 11.2), the failure-mode table (spec 11.3), and an adapter-author guide covering the spec 10.3 responsibilities.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README with a mermaid lifecycle diagram matching spec 11.1 steps 1-9 and the linearization point called out
- Invariants section maps each spec 11.2 invariant to the code/test that enforces it
- Adapter guide walks a future adapter author through LogEntry construction and EntryIntake submission (spec 10.3, 10.4)
- `cargo doc` clean for ca-service public items (missing_docs warnings resolved); doc examples compile as doctests

## Out of Scope
- Operational runbooks (observability epic, spec 21.2)
- Read-path and admin documentation (their epics)

## Testing
- Doctests; CI doc build gate

## Demo
Open the rendered README in the repo and `target/doc` locally; adapter guide followed start-to-finish against the mock intake.

nodes.title: Dev-experience documentation: quickstart, target catalog, troubleshooting
nodes.description:
## Goal
Documentation for the dev experience (§18): fresh-clone quickstart, the full make-target catalog, and troubleshooting — making the "everything runnable on a laptop" goal (§1) discoverable without tribal knowledge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README quickstart: clone → `make doctor` → `make demo` → open `localhost:8080`, with expected-output snippets
- `docs/dev-environment.md` documents every §18.8 target with purpose, args, and owning component; kept in sync via the `make help` smoke test
- Troubleshooting section maps common failures to `make doctor` checks and fixes
- Walkthroughs for each dev-experience feature shipped at time of writing (time travel §18.4, fixtures §18.5, REPLs §18.6, hot reload §18.7), extended as later targets land
- Verified by a scripted fresh-clone run in a clean container

## Out of Scope
- Agent-facing context docs (`AGENTS.md`, §23 — agent-harnessing epic)
- Operational runbooks (§21.2, observability epic)

## Testing
- E2E: quickstart commands executed verbatim by a CI script (doc-drift guard)
- Lint: markdown link check

## Demo
Hand the README to someone new: they reach a running CA and issue a cert without asking a single question.

nodes.title: Proof generation service core implementing the 12.2 pipeline
nodes.description:
## Goal
Library implementing spec 12.2: read latest-checkpoint pointer, fetch checkpoint object, plan tiles, fetch tiles via the storage facade, extract sibling hashes, construct and serialize `MTCProof`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ProofService::inclusion_proof(index) -> Result<MTCProof, ProofError>` generic over the storage facade so memory and LocalStack backends both work (section 9.6)
- Typed errors: `NoCheckpoint`, `IndexBeyondCheckpoint`, `TileMissing`, `TileCorrupt`; malformed tile bytes yield errors, never panics (section 19.8 'malformed tiles to proof generator')
- Returned proof verifies against the checkpoint using tree-primitives verification
- Checkpoint returned alongside the proof so callers can verify end-to-end
- Property test: arbitrary log contents written via the facade -> generated proof round-trips serialization and verifies (section 19.2)
- Integration test against LocalStack behind `--features integration` (section 19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Lambda/HTTP wrapper (read-proof-server-lambda)
- Tile LRU cache (storage-facade owns it, Phase 2)
- Consistency proofs (read-consistency-gen)

## Testing
Unit (memory backend), property, adversarial malformed-tile fixtures, integration (LocalStack).

## Demo
With `make demo` running: `cargo run -p mtc-read --example gen-proof -- --index 42` prints a verified proof.

nodes.title: Tile path planner: map (tree_size, leaf_index) to tiles for the inclusion path
nodes.description:
## Goal
Pure planning function for spec 12.2 step 3: given a checkpoint tree size and a leaf index, compute the ordered tile coordinates (level, tile index) and intra-tile hash offsets needed to assemble the inclusion path, using the 256-leaf tile model (sections 2, 8.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `plan_inclusion(tree_size, index) -> Result<TilePlan, PlanError>` in a new read-path crate; `TilePlan` lists tile coordinates plus which hash positions within each tile are required
- `index >= tree_size` rejected with a typed error, never a panic
- Partial (right-edge) tiles handled correctly at every level
- Unit tests cover tree sizes 1, 255, 256, 257, and multi-level tile boundaries
- Property test: for arbitrary N <= 2^20 and i < N, hashes extracted per the plan reproduce exactly the inclusion proof computed directly by tree-primitives (section 19.2)

## Out of Scope
- Fetching tile bytes from storage (read-proof-gen-core)
- Consistency-proof planning (read-consistency-gen)
- Merkle hashing/proof math itself (core-mtc-library tree-primitives)

## Testing
Unit + property (proptest, sections 19.1-19.2). No external dependencies.

## Demo
After merge: `cargo test -p mtc-read`; doctest example prints the tile plan for tree_size=1000, index=513.

nodes.title: Relying-party verification core: leaf hash, proof application, checkpoint signature
nodes.description:
## Goal
A minimal-dependency `mtc-verify` crate implementing spec 12.1 steps 4-6: reconstruct the leaf hash from `TBSCertificate`, apply the inclusion proof to compute the expected subtree root, and verify the CA checkpoint signature (ECDSA P-256 in v1, section 4; no cosigners, section 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `verify_inclusion(entry, proof, checkpoint, ca_pubkey) -> Result<Verified, VerifyError>` with no service/storage dependencies, embeddable in RP code
- `VerifyError` enumerates distinct failure reasons (wrong root, bad signature, malformed proof, size mismatch) to feed the failure-breakdown telemetry (section 20.2)
- Never panics on adversarial input: tampered proofs, truncated hashes, absurd sizes all return errors (19.8)
- Uses the domain-separated hashing from tree-primitives; leaf/interior separation asserted (19.2)
- Property test: proofs generated by tree-primitives for arbitrary trees verify; any single-bit mutation of proof, entry, or root fails

## Out of Scope
- X.509 parsing and path validation (read-verify-cert)
- Landmark/signatureless mode (read-verify-signatureless)
- ML-DSA (feature-gated, core-mtc-library owns qux-pqc integration)

## Testing
Unit, property (19.2), adversarial fixtures (19.8); fuzzing follows in read-fuzz-verify.

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-verify`; doctest example verifies a fixture proof end-to-end.

nodes.title: Proof operations: mtcctl log inclusion/consistency/verify + UI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the Phase 4 'CLI commands for proof inspection and verification' (§17.3): `mtcctl log inclusion`, `log consistency`, and `log verify`, with a matching UI form for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: inclusion proof for an index, consistency proof between two sizes, verify-cert-against-log; handlers delegate to read-path proof generation and the verification library
- `mtcctl log inclusion --index N` prints the proof and local verification result; `--output json` includes `verified: true|false` (§19.13 example shape)
- `mtcctl log consistency --from A --to B` generates and verifies; invalid ranges (A>B, B>tree size) fail cleanly with non-zero exit
- `mtcctl log verify --pem FILE` verifies a certificate end-to-end against the log
- UI page/partial for proof queries showing verification outcome (parity); CLI help + tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Proof generation internals and the verification library (read-path epic)
- Self-auditor consistency sweeps (adm-audit-ops / observability)

## Testing
- Unit: handler validation edges against memory backend
- Integration: proofs against LocalStack demo log
- E2E: extend `tests/e2e/issuance-and-verification.sh` — issue, then verify inclusion via CLI

## Demo
`mtcctl cert issue --domain d.test > c.pem && mtcctl log verify --pem c.pem --output json | jq .verified` prints true.

nodes.title: mtcctl log inclusion: generate and verify an inclusion proof
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl log inclusion` (spec 17.3): generate the inclusion proof for an index and verify it locally, matching the 19.13 usage pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl log inclusion --index N` prints a human-readable proof summary (checkpoint size, path length, verified status)
- `--output json` emits `{verified, proof_b64, checkpoint, index}` so `jq .verified` works verbatim per 19.13
- Non-zero exit code when the proof does not verify or the index is out of range
- Reads storage directly via the proof-generation core, so it works against `make demo` LocalStack state without the HTTP server
- Unit tests plus a golden-JSON output test

## Out of Scope
- `log verify` (read-cli-verify) and `log consistency` (read-cli-consistency)
- Fetching via the HTTP proof-server (E2E covers that path)

## Testing
Unit; E2E arrives in read-e2e-issue-verify (19.13).

## Demo
`make demo`, then `mtcctl log inclusion --index 0 --output json | jq .verified` prints `true`.

nodes.title: mtcctl log verify: verify a certificate against the log
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl log verify` (spec 17.3): verify a certificate PEM against the log using the mtc-verify library, in both full and signatureless modes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl log verify --pem cert.pem` prints each 12.1 step with PASS/FAIL and an overall verdict
- `--signatureless --landmarks FILE` exercises step 6-prime
- `--output json` includes the `VerifyError` failure-reason enum for scripting and telemetry (20.2)
- Distinct non-zero exit codes for revoked vs proof-invalid vs parse failure
- Unit tests with fixture certs: valid, tampered proof, revoked serial

## Out of Scope
- Cert issuance (`mtcctl cert issue`, ca-service/admin-surface)
- Revocation management commands (revocation epic)

## Testing
Unit with fixtures; E2E in read-e2e-issue-verify (19.13).

## Demo
After `make demo` issues certs: `mtcctl log verify --pem /tmp/cert.pem` shows all seven 12.1 steps passing.

nodes.title: E2E shell test: issue, fetch proof, verify via CLI and HTTP
nodes.description:
## Goal
The canonical read-path E2E from spec 19.13: a shell script driving mtcctl against the full demo environment, covering issue -> proof -> verify including the served HTTP path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tests/e2e/issuance-and-verification.sh`: issue a cert via `mtcctl cert issue`, look up its index, run `mtcctl log inclusion --output json | jq .verified` asserting `true` (19.13 verbatim), then `mtcctl log verify --pem` asserting success
- Additionally curls the local proof-server `/v1/proof/{index}` and verifies the returned proof, exercising the served path
- Negative case: a tampered PEM makes `log verify` exit non-zero
- Wired into `make test-e2e` (18.8) and green in CI against the LocalStack demo

## Out of Scope
- Revocation and pruning E2E scenarios (their epics)
- Multi-region failover E2E (multi-region epic)

## Testing
E2E (19.1, 19.13); shell driving mtcctl.

## Demo
`make test-e2e` lists `issuance-and-verification.sh` passing.

nodes.title: Wire proof-server into the local demo environment (CloudFront stand-in)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Make the read path part of the 60-second demo (section 18.1): proof-server runs as a local process in `make demo`, with direct LocalStack S3 tile access standing in for CloudFront.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo` starts proof-server on a documented port, wired to LocalStack S3/DDB via the cloud-aws env config (section 9.4)
- Local-mode tile fetch path documented, including what CloudFront would add in AWS (12.3)
- `make doctor` (18.8) checks the proof-server health endpoint
- Smoke check in the demo pipeline: after the sample ACME client issues certs, `curl` of `/v1/proof/0` returns a proof that verifies
- Works on a laptop with zero cloud credentials

## Out of Scope
- Multi-region demo wiring (`make demo-multiregion`, multi-region epic)
- A local caching proxy container emulating CloudFront TTLs (nice-to-have, not required)

## Testing
Integration/E2E smoke inside the demo environment (section 19.1).

## Demo
`make demo`, then `curl localhost:<port>/v1/checkpoint/latest` returns the signed checkpoint.

nodes.title: Lambda proof-server binary with local serve mode
nodes.description:
## Goal
The proof-server Lambda (sections 7, 12.2, 12.3): HTTP surface over the proof generation core, deployable as a Lambda and runnable as a plain local HTTP server for the laptop environment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Axum router shared between a `lambda_http` entrypoint and a `--serve --port N` standalone mode
- Routes: `GET /v1/proof/{index}`, `GET /v1/checkpoint/latest`, plus `/health/liveness` and `/health/readiness` (section 20.5)
- S3/DDB clients and facade constructed once at module init and reused across invocations (section 12.3)
- 404 with problem+json for unknown index; 503 while no checkpoint exists
- Explicit Cache-Control per route, rationale documented against 8.1 immutability invariants (short TTL for latest-checkpoint-relative responses)
- Unit tests drive the router with the memory backend via `tower::ServiceExt`
- Integration test boots the binary against LocalStack and asserts a served proof verifies

## Out of Scope
- CDK deployment constructs (read-cdk-infra)
- Entry/cert download routes (read-cert-download)
- CloudFront (read-cdk-infra); provisioned concurrency is infra config, not code

## Testing
Unit, integration (LocalStack, `--features integration`, section 19.1).

## Demo
`make demo` up, then `cargo run -p proof-server -- --serve --port 9090` and `curl localhost:9090/v1/proof/0`.

nodes.title: Certificate-level verification: parse, revocation check, X.509 path composition
nodes.description:
## Goal
Complete the relying-party flow (spec 12.1 steps 1-3 and 7): parse the certificate, check `signatureAlgorithm == id-alg-mtcProof`, decode `signatureValue` as `MTCProof`, check `serialNumber` against the revoked-ranges list (16.1), run standard X.509 path validation, and compose with read-verify-core into one `verify_certificate` entry point.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Accepts DER and PEM; wrong `signatureAlgorithm` yields a typed error (step 1)
- Revocation check against `RevocationList` (start,end) ranges including boundary indices, with a configurable max-list-age policy (16.1, 16.2)
- X.509 path validation via an established crate, with the MTC proof replacing per-cert signature verification (step 7)
- `verify_certificate` returns the same `VerifyError` reason taxonomy as the core
- Fixture tests: valid cert passes; revoked cert fails; revoked-then-reissued index fails per 19.6
- Delivered as 2-3 PRs: (1) parse/extract, (2) revocation check, (3) path-validation composition

## Out of Scope
- Revocation list generation/signing (revocation epic)
- Signatureless mode (read-verify-signatureless)

## Testing
Unit, property (range boundary conditions), adversarial fixtures kept as regression corpus (19.3).

## Demo
`cargo run -p mtc-verify --example verify-cert -- cert.pem` against a demo-issued cert prints step-by-step PASS.

nodes.title: Signatureless verification via predistributed landmarks
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement spec 12.1 step 6-prime: verify the computed subtree root against a predistributed landmark hash instead of a checkpoint signature — the signatureless optimization that motivates MTC (sections 1, 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `LandmarkSet` type loadable from a file (format documented); `verify_signatureless(entry, proof, landmarks)` matches the computed subtree root against a landmark
- Unknown/expired landmark returns a typed error signaling fallback-to-full verification, so the signatureless-to-full fallback rate is observable (section 20.2)
- Landmark age exposed on success for landmark-age telemetry (20.2, OQ-4)
- Helper to derive a `LandmarkSet` from a checkpoint + log state for demo/test use
- Property test: a landmark derived from any subtree verifies every entry inside that subtree and rejects every entry outside it

## Out of Scope
- Landmark publication cadence and distribution channel (CA service/observability; OQ-4 says start hourly)
- Full-mode verification (read-verify-core)

## Testing
Unit, property (19.2).

## Demo
Example: derive landmarks from the demo log, then verify a demo-issued cert with no signature check and print the landmark age.

nodes.title: CDK constructs: proof-server Lambda + CloudFront distribution (synth-tested)
nodes.description:
## Goal
CDK (TypeScript) constructs for the read path per sections 5, 12.3: proof-server Lambda with provisioned concurrency, and a CloudFront distribution fronting S3 tiles and the Lambda. Synth assertions only, no cloud deploy (section 1 non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR1 `ProofServerLambda` construct: Rust Lambda packaging hook, provisioned concurrency configured (12.3), IAM policy contains only read actions on the log bucket and DDB table, env wiring for bucket/table names, instantiable per-region (primary and standby both serve proofs, 12.2)
- PR2 `ReadPathDistribution` construct: S3 origin for `tiles/`, `entries/`, `checkpoints/` and Lambda origin for `/v1/*`; cache behaviors assert long-TTL immutable for tile/entry paths and short TTL for latest-checkpoint and revocation paths (8.1, 16.2)
- Fine-grained `aws-cdk-lib/assertions` tests for every claim above; `cdk synth` of the read-path stack green in CI

## Out of Scope
- CDK app skeleton, pipelines, account bootstrap (foundation-infra)
- Revocation push-notification wiring (revocation epic)
- Any actual deployment or AWS spend

## Testing
Unit (CDK synth fine-grained assertions) only, per calibration.

## Demo
`npx cdk synth ReadPathStack` renders the template; `npm test` shows assertion suite green.

nodes.title: Certificate and entry download endpoints on proof-server
nodes.description:
## Goal
Proof-server serves 'inclusion proofs and certificate downloads' (section 7 component table). Add entry and assembled-certificate download routes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `GET /v1/entry/{index}` returns the raw `TBSCertificateLogEntry` bytes from `entries/` (section 8.1)
- `GET /v1/cert/{index}` returns the assembled certificate (entry + MTCProof) in DER via the mtc-serialization assembly routines, with PEM via content negotiation or `?format=pem`
- 404 with typed problem body for out-of-range or pruned indices
- Long-lived `Cache-Control: immutable` on entry responses, entries never change once written (8.1 S3 invariants)
- Unit tests (memory backend) and one LocalStack integration test per route

## Out of Scope
- Proof route itself (read-proof-server-lambda)
- Revocation list distribution routes (revocation epic, section 16.2)
- Pruning semantics (pruning epic decides what 'pruned' returns; here it is just 404)

## Testing
Unit, integration (LocalStack, section 19.1).

## Demo
With the local server running: `curl localhost:9090/v1/cert/0 | openssl x509 -inform DER -noout -text`.

nodes.title: mtcctl log consistency: consistency proofs between tree sizes
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl log consistency` (spec 17.3): generate and verify a consistency proof between two tree sizes, supporting audit-style inspection of append-only growth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl log consistency --old N --new M` prints a proof summary and verified status
- `--output json` emits `{verified, proof_b64, old_size, new_size}` so `jq .verified` works (17.3 output formats)
- Non-zero exit when the proof fails to verify; distinct exit code and message for out-of-range sizes or `old > new`
- Reads storage directly via the consistency generation core, working against `make demo` LocalStack state without the HTTP server
- Unit tests plus a golden-JSON output test

## Out of Scope
- Consistency proof generation internals (read-consistency-gen)
- Inclusion proof CLI (read-cli-inclusion)
- Self-auditor scheduling (observability epic)

## Testing
Unit with fixtures (19.1); follows the 19.13 CLI-driven E2E pattern.

## Demo
`make demo` until two checkpoints exist, then `mtcctl log consistency --old 256 --new 512 --output json | jq .verified` prints `true`.

nodes.title: Consistency proof generation: planner extension and service method
nodes.description:
## Goal
Extend the proof pipeline with consistency proofs between two tree sizes, generated from stored tiles and checkpoints, backing `mtcctl log consistency` (17.3) and the 19.2 consistency property.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `plan_consistency(old_size, new_size) -> Result<TilePlan, PlanError>` added to the tile planner
- `ProofService::consistency_proof(old_size, new_size)` fetches tiles via the storage facade and returns the serialized proof plus both checkpoints when stored
- Typed errors for `old > new`, either size exceeding the latest checkpoint, and size 0; no panics on any input
- Property test: for arbitrary valid size pairs, hashes extracted per the plan reproduce the tree-primitives consistency proof and the proof verifies (19.2 'consistency proofs verify between any two tree sizes')
- Unit tests at tile boundaries: (256,512), (255,257), (1,256), and equal sizes

## Out of Scope
- CLI command (read-cli-consistency)
- Self-auditor scheduled consistency checking (observability epic)
- Inclusion proofs (read-proof-gen-core)

## Testing
Unit + property on the memory backend (19.2); one LocalStack integration case added to the existing suite (19.1).

## Demo
With `make demo` state: `cargo run -p mtc-read --example gen-consistency -- --old 256 --new 512` prints a verified proof.

nodes.title: Differential verification against the bwesterb/mtc Go reference
nodes.description:
## Goal
Spec 19.5: run every certificate through two independent verification paths — our mtc-verify (Path A) and a Go binary wrapping bwesterb/mtc (Path B) — and fail on any disagreement, catching symmetric issue/verify bugs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Harness shells out to the Go reference wrapper from the conformance suite and asserts verdict agreement per 19.3 Layer 4 semantics (both-accept requires structural agreement; both-reject is fine; splits fail)
- Runs over the fixture corpus plus demo-issued certs
- Divergence output is actionable: input hexdump, both verdicts, parsed structures
- Wired as a nightly CI job (19.3 notes cross-language tooling cost), also runnable locally behind a `differential` feature

## Out of Scope
- Differential parsing of individual spec types (core-mtc-library conformance suite)
- Building/vendoring the Go wrapper itself (external dep)

## Testing
Differential/integration (19.5); nightly CI.

## Demo
`cargo test --features differential -p mtc-verify` runs the corpus with zero mismatches; `make test-conformance` includes it.

nodes.title: Relying-party integration guide and read-path API docs
nodes.description:
## Goal
Documentation the spec assigns alongside implementation (25.6 'Documentation vs Implementation' parallel track): how a relying party verifies MTC certificates and how to consume the read-path API.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/read-path.md`: narrative walkthrough of the 12.1 verification flow (full and signatureless), endpoint table for the proof-server routes, and a worked mtc-verify code example
- Rustdoc on the mtc-verify public API with compile-tested examples (`cargo test --doc` green)
- Notes on caching semantics and why tiles are immutable (8.1, 12.3)
- Linked from the repo README/docs index

## Out of Scope
- Runbooks (observability/operational epics, section 21.2)
- Admin API docs (admin-surface)

## Testing
Doc tests (`cargo test --doc`); markdown lint via CI baseline.

## Demo
`cargo doc -p mtc-verify --open` shows the documented API; `docs/read-path.md` renders with the worked example.

nodes.title: Structured fuzzing of the verification path
nodes.description:
## Goal
Spec 19.3 Layer 3 for the read path: the verification code must never panic on structurally plausible but semantically invalid inputs — the class of bugs byte-level fuzzing misses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cargo-fuzz target `verify_proof` using an `arbitrary`-derived `ArbitraryProofInput` (semi-valid proofs, entries, checkpoints); harness asserts no panic and no unbounded allocation (19.3 properties)
- Second target feeding raw bytes through the MTCProof parse -> verify pipeline end to end
- Seed corpus checked in under `fuzz/corpus/` (19.3 corpus management)
- Bounded-iteration fuzz smoke run wired into CI; any crash input minimized and added as a permanent unit regression test

## Out of Scope
- Byte-level parse fuzz targets for spec types (`Checkpoint`, `Tile`, etc. — core-mtc-library owns 19.3 Layer 2)
- Nightly differential fuzzing (read-differential-verify covers differential)

## Testing
Fuzz (cargo-fuzz) + unit regression fixtures (19.3).

## Demo
`cargo fuzz run verify_proof -- -runs=10000` completes with zero crashes.

nodes.title: OpenAPI contract and generated client for read-path endpoints
nodes.description:
## Goal
Spec-first contract for the read-path HTTP surface using the foundation OpenAPI codegen pipeline (mandated for the admin API in 17.2; extended here to the read surface), producing a generated Rust client for tests and scripting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `openapi/read-path.yaml` covers proof, latest-checkpoint, entry/cert download, and health routes with error schemas (problem+json)
- `make api-gen` (section 18.8) regenerates the client crate; CI fails on uncommitted drift
- Contract test: generated client exercises every route against the in-process router (memory backend), asserting success and error shapes match the spec

## Out of Scope
- Admin API spec (admin-surface epic)
- Client retry/backoff policy tuning (post-v1)

## Testing
Unit/contract tests; codegen drift check in CI (section 22.13 baseline).

## Demo
`make api-gen && cargo test -p read-client` passes; diff shows no drift.

nodes.title: Benchmarks: proof generation latency, verification throughput, proof size budget
nodes.description:
## Goal
Criterion benchmarks establishing the read-path performance baseline for later regression tracking (spec 19.11), plus an assertion on the compact-proof promise (~736 bytes, section 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Benches: inclusion proof generation over memory-backend fixture trees at 2^10 and 2^20 leaves; `verify_inclusion` throughput
- Unit test asserts serialized MTCProof size for a 2^20-leaf tree is <= 1024 bytes, with the budget constant documented against the ~736-byte figure in section 2
- Wired into `make bench` (18.8) with results printed in a comparable format
- Runs on a laptop in under a few minutes; no LocalStack required

## Out of Scope
- CI performance-regression gating and history tracking (testing-infra, Phase 8)
- Lambda cold-start measurement (needs real AWS; excluded per section 1 non-goals)

## Testing
Bench (criterion) + one unit size assertion.

## Demo
`make bench` prints the proof-gen and verify tables with the size assertion passing.

nodes.title: make demo-multiregion: three-region local simulation environment
nodes.description:
## Goal
`make demo-multiregion` (§18.3): three local region stacks (us-east-1 primary; us-west-2, eu-west-1 standby) with simulated CRR and Global Tables replication — the roadmap's "multi-region simulation in dev environment" (§24 Phase 5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Compose topology: per-region LocalStack + CA service instance with region-scoped config and ports (admin UIs on 8080/8081/8082), plus replicator instances matching the production CRR fan-out
- Primary holds the lease and issues; standbys run read-only mode and serve status (lease/epoch protocol)
- `make demo-multiregion` gates on all three regions healthy; `make demo-multiregion-down` cleans up fully; idempotent re-runs
- Smoke: a cert issued in the primary is visible from a standby's state within the configured lag bound
- Region set and lag configurable in one file; defaults documented

## Out of Scope
- Partition and failover scenarios (`dev-partition-failover-scenarios`)
- Chaos test suite (§19.9, testing epic)

## Testing
- Integration: replicator wiring per link
- E2E: bring-up smoke asserting the lease is held by exactly one region and standby replication lag is within bound

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion` → three admin UIs side by side; issue in us-east-1, watch the entry surface in eu-west-1 seconds later.

nodes.title: Implement lease/epoch protocol core (acquire, renew, claim, fencing primitives)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the primary-region lease and epoch protocol (spec 8.2, 8.3) as a `coordination` crate built on the `ReplicatedKv` trait. Critical-path anchor for all multi-region work (spec 25.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `primary-region-lease` item per spec 8.2 schema: `region`, `expires_at`, `epoch`, `holder_id` under PK `log#{logId}`
- `Epoch` and `HolderId` newtypes (spec 22.1); epoch checked arithmetic, strictly monotonic
- Operations: `read_lease`, `acquire`, `renew` (conditional on holder_id + epoch; constants 20s cadence / 60s TTL per spec 8.3)
- `claim_lease` atomically takes over an expired lease AND increments epoch in one conditional write; typed error if lease unexpired or epoch changed
- Takeover only permitted when `expires_at` is past the 60s safety margin (spec 8.3)
- `epoch_condition()` helper producing the epoch condition fragment all coordination writes must carry (spec 8.3)
- Conditional failures map to typed errors (`LeaseHeld`, `LostLease`, `EpochAdvanced`) per spec 22.6
- Same test suite passes against memory backend and LocalStack DDB (spec 9.7)

## Out of Scope
- Background renewer task (mr-lease-renewer); wiring fencing into CA writes (mr-epoch-write-fencing)
- Full Kani invariant proofs (mr-kani-lease-epoch) — only a basic no-panic harness here

## Testing
Unit; property (proptest: N concurrent claim attempts yield exactly one winner and unique epochs); integration (LocalStack DDB); basic Kani no-panic harness.

## Demo
`cargo run -p coordination --example lease-demo` — acquire, renew, expire, takeover with epoch bump printed against the memory backend.

nodes.title: Kani proofs of lease/epoch invariants (mandatory)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Machine-checked verification of the lease/epoch protocol with Kani (spec 19.12) — explicitly not optional; core to the trust story (spec 24 Phase 5) and the auditor-facing differentiator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Protocol logic factored into a pure, verification-friendly state machine (KV effects modeled as transitions) with no behavior change; production code paths call the same logic
- Harness: mutual exclusion — no reachable state where two holders both hold a current-epoch lease (spec 19.12)
- Harness: epoch strictly increases on every takeover (spec 8.3)
- Harness: takeover only possible when the lease is expired past the 60s safety margin (spec 8.3)
- Harness: a fenced write carrying a stale epoch can never be accepted (spec 13.4 split-brain impossibility)
- Harness: absence of panics and integer overflow in protocol arithmetic
- All harnesses run in the CI Kani job within its time budget; harness intent documented in the crate README

## Out of Scope
- Kani for tree primitives (core-mtc-library) and write-path linearization (ca-service) per spec 19.12
- Loom tests (mr-loom-renewer-batch)

## Testing
Kani (primary); unit tests for the refactored state machine.

## Demo
`make kani` (or `cargo kani -p coordination`) prints all lease/epoch harnesses VERIFIED; required CI check is green.

nodes.title: Failover exposure: mtcctl failover status/initiate + UI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose manual failover on the admin surface (§13.2, §17.3): `mtcctl failover status` (readiness assessment) and `mtcctl failover initiate` (privileged), plus UI equivalents. Orchestration internals belong to multi-region; this ticket is the API/CLI/UI exposure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: failover readiness (replication lag, standby health, prerequisites) and initiate (privileged; requires `--to <region>` and `--reason`, per §13.2 justification + incident ref)
- Handlers delegate to the multi-region failover orchestrator; admin layer holds no promotion logic
- `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2 --reason "..."` goes through the confirmation flow (adm-privileged-confirm) and streams/echoes step progress from the idempotent promotion procedure (§13.3)
- Initiate tagged `x-privileged`; request without elevated principal gets 403 (adm-auth-middleware enforcement, covered by test)
- `mtcctl failover status --output json` stable for runbook automation
- Failover UI panel: readiness display + initiate form with confirmation (parity with §13.2 'CLI or admin UI')

## Out of Scope
- Promotion procedure, readiness computation, standby mode (multi-region epic)
- Automated failover (non-goal, §1)

## Testing
- Unit: handler delegation, privileged gating, required-args validation
- Integration: `make demo-multiregion` — initiate against simulated partition
- E2E: chaos-style shell script partitioning a region then failing over via CLI (§18.3)

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion && make partition-region us-east-1 && mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2 --reason drill --yes`.

nodes.title: Lease operations: mtcctl lease show/renew + Lease UI page
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose lease state over the admin surface (§17.3, §17.4): `mtcctl lease show` (current holder, expiry) and `mtcctl lease renew` (force renewal, dev/test only), plus the Lease UI view with history and force-renew.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: get lease state (holder region, epoch, acquired/expiry times, recent transitions) and force-renew (tagged dev/test-only, absent or 403 outside dev mode)
- Handlers read from the lease/epoch protocol implementation; no lease logic duplicated in the admin layer
- `mtcctl lease show` human + `--output json`; `mtcctl lease renew` clearly marked dev/test in help and refuses outside dev mode
- Lease UI page: current holder, expiry countdown, transition history, force-renew button (dev mode); updates on lease-changed SSE events
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Lease/epoch protocol internals and Kani harnesses (multi-region epic)
- Failover commands (adm-failover-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against memory-backend lease state; dev-gating of renew
- Integration: `make demo-multiregion` stack — show reflects real holder; renew extends expiry
- E2E: shell script asserts holder/epoch fields present via CLI

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion` then `mtcctl lease show`; watch expiry move after `mtcctl lease renew`.

nodes.title: Local CRR and Global Tables replication simulator with configurable lag
nodes.description:
## Goal
Local replication simulator (§18.3): simulated S3 CRR and DynamoDB Global Tables replication between LocalStack instances with configurable lag — the substrate the three-region environment is built on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replicator binary (`crates/dev-replicator`) copies new S3 object versions source→target (polling ListObjectVersions), preserving keys, version order, and Object Lock metadata
- DDB replication tails the source table (Streams or scan-diff) and applies to target with last-writer-wins parity to Global Tables semantics
- Configurable per-link lag (`REPL_LAG_MS`); pause/resume via signal or local control endpoint (the partition hook)
- Emits a replication-lag log line/metric per link
- Runs as N instances for arbitrary directed-link topologies

## Out of Scope
- Three-region compose topology (`dev-multiregion-harness`)
- Production CRR/Global Tables configuration in CDK (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit: dedup/ordering, lag scheduling
- Integration: two LocalStack containers — object written to A appears in B after the lag, not before; pause halts propagation
- Property: applying the same event stream twice is idempotent

## Demo
Start two LocalStacks + replicator with 5 s lag; `aws s3 cp` to A; watch the object appear in B five seconds later.

nodes.title: make partition-region and scripted local failover exercise
nodes.description:
## Goal
Partition simulation and the scripted failover exercise (§18.3, §13): `make partition-region X` / `make heal-region X` plus an end-to-end local failover demo driven by `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make partition-region X` disconnects region X's containers from the shared network and pauses its replicator links; `make heal-region X` restores both
- Partitioned primary loses lease renewal; standbys keep serving reads (observable in admin UIs)
- `tests/e2e/failover-demo.sh`: partition us-east-1 → `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2` → issuance resumes in the new primary at a bumped epoch; on heal, writes from the old primary are rejected (no split-brain, lease/epoch invariants §13)
- Scenario is re-runnable without full environment teardown
- Both targets no-op with a clear message when the multi-region environment is not running

## Out of Scope
- Failover command implementation (multi-region + admin-surface epics)
- Automated failover (explicit non-goal, §1)

## Testing
- Integration: network disconnect/heal mechanics
- E2E: the failover demo script in the nightly lane (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion`, `make partition-region us-east-1`, `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2` → watch us-west-2 take over issuance live.

nodes.title: Chaos scenario: chaos-primary-loss
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the chaos-primary-loss scenario (spec 19.9): kill the primary mid-batch; pass criterion is that the new primary promotes and no committed cert is lost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scenario kills the primary container mid-batch (entries in flight, prior batches committed) in the multi-region sim
- Scripted operator step performs `mtcctl failover initiate` to the recommended standby (manual failover is the v1 model, spec 13.2)
- Pass: promotion succeeds; every checkpoint-committed cert remains verifiable post-failover — RPO zero (spec 13.5)
- Uncommitted in-flight entries are cleanly abandoned and their index gaps filled with `null_entry` (spec 13.3 step 5)
- `make chaos-primary-loss` runs the scenario with a pass/fail exit code; tagged for nightly CI

## Out of Scope
- Chaos framework/fault-injection infrastructure (testing-infra)
- Other chaos scenarios (independent tickets per spec 25.6)

## Testing
Chaos/E2E (spec 19.9, 19.13).

## Demo
`make chaos-primary-loss` prints the scenario timeline (kill, failover, verify) and PASS.

nodes.title: Chaos scenario: chaos-split-brain
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the chaos-split-brain scenario (spec 19.9): two regions attempt promotion concurrently; pass criterion is that exactly one succeeds (the epoch invariant).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scenario partitions the primary, then triggers `promote()` on both standbys simultaneously in the multi-region sim
