- Pass: exactly one `claim_lease` succeeds; the loser receives a typed `LeaseHeld`/`EpochAdvanced` error and remains Standby
- Post-checks: a single writer exists; storage audit finds zero coordination items written under the losing epoch (spec 13.4); log remains verifiable end-to-end
- Scenario repeated N times with randomized timing to shake out orderings
- `make chaos-split-brain` with pass/fail exit code; tagged for nightly CI

## Out of Scope
- Chaos framework infrastructure (testing-infra)
- Kani-level proof of the same invariant (mr-kani-lease-epoch)

## Testing
Chaos/E2E (spec 19.9, 19.13).

## Demo
`make chaos-split-brain` shows both promotion attempts, one winner, one clean loser, and PASS.

nodes.title: `make demo-multiregion`: three-region local topology + partition injection
nodes.description:
## Goal
One command brings up three CA instances simulating us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 with simulated replication, plus `make partition-region` for network partition injection (spec 18.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo-multiregion`: compose profile with 3 CA services, per-region LocalStack, replication sim wired between them (spec 18.3)
- Exactly one instance acquires the lease and becomes Primary; the other two report Standby
- `make partition-region us-east-1` isolates that instance (compose network disconnect or toxiproxy); its lease expires and becomes takeover-eligible (spec 8.3)
- `make heal-region us-east-1` restores connectivity
- `mtcctl` can target each region's admin API (flag or env)
- Startup and teardown scripted; runs entirely on a laptop; dev README section documents the flow (runbook prose stays in operational-tooling)

## Out of Scope
- Failover execution in the sim (mr-failover-initiate and mr-chaos-* exercise it)
- Replication shim internals (mr-replication-sim)

## Testing
Integration script asserting one Primary and two Standbys post-boot; E2E smoke of partition, lease expiry, and heal in nightly CI (spec 19.1, 19.13).

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion`; `mtcctl status` per region shows one Primary, two Standbys; `make partition-region us-east-1` — lease expires and shows takeover-eligible; `make heal-region us-east-1`.

nodes.title: Epoch-conditional fencing on every coordination write
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ensure every DynamoDB coordination write includes `epoch` in its ConditionExpression so old primaries cannot write after epoch advance — the property that makes split-brain impossible (spec 8.3, 13.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Counter UpdateItem, batch item writes, and `latest-checkpoint` / `latest-revocation` pointer writes (spec 8.2) all carry the epoch condition via `epoch_condition()`
- ConditionalCheckFailed on epoch mismatch maps to `LostLease`; on `LostLease` the write path stops retrying and halts issuance (role-transition wiring lands in mr-standby-mode)
- Property test: interleaved writes from two simulated epochs — no stale-epoch write ever takes effect, committed data never overwritten
- Integration test on LocalStack: bump epoch out-of-band, verify every write type is rejected
- `#[must_use]` on fencing results (spec 22.10)

## Out of Scope
- Promotion procedure (mr-promotion-procedure); standby role machine (mr-standby-mode)
- Kani write-fencing proof (mr-kani-lease-epoch)

## Testing
Unit; property (proptest); integration (LocalStack DDB) per spec 19.1 and the spec 25.4 exemplar ticket.

## Demo
`make demo`, then dev script force-bumps the epoch out-of-band; service logs `LostLease` and halts issuance with no further write attempts in the log.

nodes.title: Manual failover: `mtcctl failover initiate` privileged command + API
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl failover initiate --to <region> --reason <text>` (spec 13.2, 17.3): the deliberate human decision that orchestrates verified promotion in v1 (automated failover is a non-goal, spec 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Privileged command: interactive `--confirm` or `--yes` for automation (spec 17.3 authorization)
- Runs readiness checks first; refuses when target is not caught up unless `--force` (recorded in output and audit trail)
- Triggers `promote()` on the target region via its admin API; streams step-by-step progress; exit code reflects outcome
- `--reason` and operator identity recorded in an auditable record
- Re-invoking after partial failure resumes safely (delegates to promote idempotency, spec 13.3)
- E2E test in the multi-region sim: initiate makes target Primary and the old primary is fenced out

## Out of Scope
- UI button (mr-failover-ui); failover runbook document (operational-tooling)
- Automated failover decision-making (v2, spec 13.5)

## Testing
Unit; integration; E2E via CLI in multi-region sim (spec 19.13).

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion`; `make partition-region us-east-1`; `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2 --reason "demo"` (spec 18.3) — us-west-2 becomes primary and issues.

nodes.title: Failover readiness assessment: API + `mtcctl failover status`
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the spec 13.2 pre-failover verification as an admin API endpoint plus `mtcctl failover status` (spec 17.3): is it safe to fail over, and to where?

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI-first `GET /failover/status` route (spec 17.2) reporting: primary reachability, per-standby freshness (latest checkpoint replicated, S3 CRR current), and recommended candidate selected by data freshness (spec 13.2 checks 1-3)
- `mtcctl failover status` renders assessment human-readable and via `--output json` (spec 17.3)
- Works when primary is unreachable — assessment computed from standby-visible replicated state
- Lagged-standby integration test: readiness is false with a machine-readable reason
- Generated OpenAPI client used by CLI (no hand-rolled HTTP)

## Out of Scope
- Initiating failover (mr-failover-initiate); UI rendering (mr-failover-ui)
- Route 53 health check infrastructure (mr-multiregion-cdk)

## Testing
Unit; integration (memory backend with simulated replication lag); E2E via CLI (spec 19.13).

## Demo
`make demo` with a second standby instance; `mtcctl failover status` shows ready/not-ready with reasons; stall the standby's replication feed via test hook and watch it flip to not-ready.

nodes.title: Admin UI: lease and failover views with SSE (CLI parity)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Deliver CLI/UI parity (spec 17.1) for lease and failover: a lease page and a failover control view in the htmx + Askama admin UI (spec 17.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `handlers/lease.rs` + `pages/lease.html` per spec 17.4 layout: current holder, region, epoch, `expires_at` countdown, recent transitions, dev-only force-renew button
- Failover view: readiness assessment (same API the CLI consumes) and an Initiate Failover control gated by a typed-confirmation dialog (privileged, mirrors `--confirm`)
- SSE stream pushes lease events (renewals, takeovers, stand-downs) live without polling (spec 17.4)
- Askama compile-time-checked templates; no JS beyond vendored htmx + vanilla helpers
- Failover progress rendered live during promotion

## Out of Scope
- Dashboard/batches/audit views (admin-surface epic)
- Readiness/promotion logic (consumed via API only)

## Testing
Unit (template render with fixture state); E2E: drive a failover from the UI against the multi-region sim (spec 19.13 layers, webapp-driven).

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion`; open the admin UI lease page, watch the countdown tick via SSE, click Initiate Failover, watch the standby promote live.

nodes.title: Lease renewer background task with epoch view and stand-down signaling
nodes.description:
## Goal
Background task that renews the lease every 20s (spec 8.3), maintains the service's atomic epoch view (spec 13.3 step 4), and signals lease loss to the rest of the CA service.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tokio task renews every 20s using the injected `Clock` trait (spec 22.11); interval constants shared with the protocol crate
- Publishes current epoch via an atomic (`SeqCst`, per spec 13.3) readable by the write path
- On renewal failure with `LostLease`/`EpochAdvanced`: emits a stand-down signal (watch channel) consumed by the CA service
- Transient errors retried with backoff but never past the 60s TTL safety margin — gives up and signals before expiry
- Emits metrics/log events: renewal success/failure, time-to-expiry (feeds application self-report, spec 13.1)
- Fake-clock tests prove missed renewals produce the stand-down signal strictly before TTL expiry

## Out of Scope
- Standby lease monitoring loop (mr-standby-mode)
- Loom interleaving tests (mr-loom-renewer-batch)

## Testing
Unit with fake `Clock`; integration against memory backend (spec 19.1). Loom coverage arrives in mr-loom-renewer-batch.

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl status --output json` twice, 20s apart — lease `expires_at` visibly refreshed by the renewer.

nodes.title: Loom concurrency model check: lease renewer vs batch builder
nodes.description:
## Goal
Exhaustively model-check interleavings of the lease renewer, batch builder, and stand-down signaling with Loom (spec 19.12) to rule out races that traditional testing misses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cfg(loom)`-gated sync shim for the shared epoch atomic and stand-down channel in the coordination crate
- Loom test: the batch builder never commits a coordination write after the renewer has observed lease loss (epoch view `SeqCst` ordering per spec 13.3)
- Loom test: no deadlock among renewer, batch builder, and the Primary-to-Standby transition
- Loom test: no window where a write passes the fencing check under an epoch the renewer already knows is stale
- Shuttle randomized test covering the same properties at larger state sizes (spec 19.12)
- Runs in the CI loom job with a documented preemption bound

## Out of Scope
- Loom/Shuttle CI scaffolding (testing-infra)
- Intake-handler concurrency beyond its hand-off to the batch builder

## Testing
Loom; Shuttle (spec 19.12).

## Demo
`make loom` (or `cargo test -p coordination --features loom --release`) enumerates interleavings and passes; CI job green.

nodes.title: Old-primary recovery: detect higher epoch and stand down
nodes.description:
## Goal
A failed primary that returns must observe the new lease holder and higher epoch, then demote itself to standby read-only without a single successful write (spec 13.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- On startup and on every renewal attempt, the service compares lease holder/epoch; different holder with higher epoch forces transition to Standby before any write is attempted
- Any in-flight write from the old epoch fails with `LostLease` (fencing) and is not retried under the stale epoch
- Two-instance integration test: old primary resumes after simulated partition heal — exactly one writer exists at all times; storage audit shows zero stale-epoch writes accepted
- Recovery/demotion emits event + metric (feeds spec 20 observability)

## Out of Scope
- Chaos scenario automation (mr-chaos-old-primary-recovery)
- Automated failback to the recovered region (non-goal, spec 1)

## Testing
Unit; integration with memory backend partition simulation (spec 19.1).

## Demo
Two instances on a shared backend; block the primary's backend access until its lease expires, promote the standby, unblock — old primary logs a stand-down event and reports `Standby`.

nodes.title: Idempotent promotion procedure (verify, abandon, claim, gap-fill, resume)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `CaService::promote()` exactly per spec 13.3 — idempotent and safe to re-run after partial failure, with zero RPO for committed work (spec 13.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Step 1: read latest checkpoint, verify signature (`PromoteError::InvalidCheckpoint` on failure); `wait_for_crr` when the tile snapshot is inconsistent with the checkpoint
- Step 2: query pending batches and mark each abandoned (epoch-conditional writes)
- Step 3: `claim_lease` atomically increments epoch; Step 4: local epoch view stored `SeqCst`
- Step 5: first post-promotion batch fills index gaps with `null_entry`, then issuance resumes
- Idempotency: test kills `promote()` at every step boundary and re-runs; state converges, no duplicate abandonment or double epoch bump
- Test proves RPO zero: every checkpoint-committed entry verifiable after promotion

## Out of Scope
- CLI/API trigger (mr-failover-initiate); readiness assessment (mr-failover-readiness)
- Chaos automation (mr-chaos-* tickets)

## Testing
Unit; integration (memory backend + LocalStack); property (promote applied n times equals once) per spec 19.1.

## Demo
`mtcctl repl` — call `promote` against a standby wired to a snapshot; observe epoch bump, gap-fill batch, and resumed issuance in logs.

nodes.title: Simulated cross-region replication (S3 CRR + DDB Global Tables) with configurable lag
nodes.description:
## Goal
A local replication shim that copies S3 objects and DDB items between per-region LocalStack instances with configurable lag, enabling laptop-scale multi-region behavior (spec 18.3; zero-cost local sim per spec 1 non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria
- S3 CRR simulator: replicates writes from a source-region bucket to peer-region buckets after a configurable delay
- DDB Global Tables simulator: replicates coordination-table writes across instances with configurable lag; conflict semantics (last-writer-wins) documented
- Lag configurable per link at runtime, including stall (infinite lag) to support chaos-crr-stall (spec 19.9)
- Runs as a compose sidecar; clean shutdown; replication position observable for readiness checks
- Unit tests for ordering and lag behavior; integration test across two LocalStack instances

## Out of Scope
- Three-region topology and make targets (mr-demo-multiregion)
- Chaos scenario definitions (mr-chaos-* tickets)

## Testing
Unit; integration (two LocalStack instances) per spec 19.1.

## Demo
Start two LocalStack instances + the sim with `lag=5s`; put an object in region A; watch it appear in region B five seconds later.

nodes.title: Standby read-only mode and region role state machine
nodes.description:
## Goal
CA service instances run as Primary or Standby; standbys monitor the lease but never write (spec 8.3, 13.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role state machine per spec 22.4: `Primary`, `Standby`, `StandingDown`; illegal transitions unrepresentable
- In Standby: entry intake rejected/paused via the `EntryIntake` seam, batch builder idle, read/status endpoints stay live
- Standby periodically reads the lease item (lease expiry monitoring, spec 13.1) and records data-freshness metrics (replicated checkpoint age)
- Stand-down signal (from renewer or fencing) transitions Primary to Standby cleanly: in-flight work abandoned, no partial coordination writes
- Role, lease view, and epoch exposed on the health endpoint (spec 20.5); CLI surfacing lands in mr-lease-cli
- Transition events logged and emitted for SSE consumption (spec 17.4)

## Out of Scope
- Promotion to Primary (mr-promotion-procedure)
- Old-primary rejoin specifics (mr-old-primary-standdown)

## Testing
Unit (state machine transitions); integration: two instances sharing a memory backend — standby performs zero writes while primary issues (spec 19.1).

## Demo
Run two CA instances against one shared backend; second instance reports `Standby` on its health endpoint and refuses `mtcctl cert issue`.

nodes.title: Health endpoints: /health/liveness, /readiness, /primary, /audit
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the four §20.5 health endpoints on the CA service so ALB/Route 53 checks (§3) and operators get truthful process, readiness, primaryship, and audit status.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `GET /health/liveness` → 200 while the process runs
- `GET /health/readiness` → 200 only when storage backends reachable and config loaded; 503 otherwise
- `GET /health/primary` → JSON `{primary, epoch, region}` derived from lease state (§8.3); standby answers `primary:false` without erroring (§3 standby rejects writes, not health)
- `GET /health/audit` → most recent `audit#{tree_size}` record summary from DDB (§8.2, §20.5); explicit `status: none` before first audit, `stale` past cadence threshold
- All endpoints unauthenticated-safe: no sensitive data in bodies (§20.1)

## Out of Scope
- The self-auditor itself (obs-auditor-core); this only reads its records
- Route 53/ALB CDK wiring — foundation-infra/multi-region epics

## Testing
- Unit: each endpoint against memory backend in every state (ready/not-ready/primary/standby/no-audit)
- E2E: demo env `curl` of all four endpoints scripted in `tests/e2e/` (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo` then `curl localhost:8080/health/readiness` and `/health/primary` show live status.

nodes.title: Chaos scenarios: split-brain, old-primary recovery, clock skew
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the epoch-invariant chaos scenarios from the spec 19.9 table — the scenarios that exercise the core multi-region trust story (roadmap Phase 5 chaos scenarios).

## Acceptance Criteria
- chaos-split-brain: both regions attempt promotion -> exactly one succeeds (epoch invariant asserted)
- chaos-old-primary-recovery: failed primary returns -> automatically stands down to read-only
- chaos-clock-skew: +/-60s skew between regions -> lease semantics remain correct
- Each scenario has an automated pass criterion matching the 19.9 table, is registered in the chaos runner, and runs in the scheduled CI chaos job
- Failures capture region logs and epoch/lease state for debugging

## Out of Scope
- Infrastructure-fault scenarios (test-chaos-infra-scenarios)
- Fixes to lease/epoch bugs these scenarios find (filed against multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Chaos/integration (19.9)

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=chaos-split-brain` shows one promotion succeeding, one rejected, PASS.

nodes.title: Chaos scenario harness for the local multi-region simulation
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the chaos-engineering framework per spec 19.9: named scenarios with machine-checked pass/fail criteria, running fault actions against the local multi-region simulation — no cloud spend per section 1 non-goals.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scenario abstraction: named scenario = setup + injected fault + pass criterion, mirroring the 19.9 table schema
- Fault action library: kill region process, CRR delay/stall, DDB lag, HSM down, clock skew, entry flood — built on test-fault-injection plus process control of the dev simulation
- Runner: `make chaos SCENARIO=<name>` and `make chaos` (all), emitting machine-readable results per scenario
- First scenario end-to-end: chaos-primary-loss (kill primary mid-batch -> new primary promotes; no committed cert lost)
- Chaos suite wired as a scheduled CI job (not per-PR)

## Out of Scope
- Remaining 19.9 scenarios (test-chaos-epoch-scenarios, test-chaos-infra-scenarios)
- The multi-region simulation environment itself (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Chaos/integration (19.9); unit tests for the runner and fault actions

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=chaos-primary-loss` kills the primary mid-batch and reports PASS with the promotion evidence.

nodes.title: Loom and Shuttle CI integration and authoring conventions
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire Loom interleaving tests and Shuttle randomized concurrency tests into CI per spec 19.12, ahead of the Phase 5 lease-renewer/batch-builder concurrency tests (roadmap section 24), with sentinel tests proving the wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dedicated CI job runs loom tests with `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom"`; loom tests are excluded from the normal `cargo test` run
- Shuttle job with a fixed iteration budget; failing schedules are persisted with documented reproduction steps
- Sentinel loom test and sentinel shuttle test in mtc-testutil keep both jobs green before component tests land
- Conventions doc: `cfg(loom)` type-swapping pattern (loom::sync vs std::sync), test placement, and when to use Shuttle vs Loom (19.12: Shuttle for properties too expensive to model-check exhaustively)
- Ships as 2 PRs: (1) Loom job + sentinel + doc, (2) Shuttle job + sentinel + doc

## Out of Scope
- The real concurrency tests (multi-region and ca-service epics author them)
- Kani wiring (test-kani-ci)

## Testing
- Loom + Shuttle (sentinel tests); CI-config validation

## Demo
`make loom` runs the interleaving suite locally; CI shows the loom and shuttle jobs green on a PR.

nodes.title: Chaos scenario: chaos-clock-skew
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the chaos-clock-skew scenario (spec 19.9): with up to plus/minus 60s of clock skew between regions, lease semantics must remain correct.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Per-region fake `Clock` skewed independently via the admin API (injected Clock per spec 18.4, 22.11)
- Standby skewed +60s: takeover attempt (`promote()`) is refused while the lease is inside the 60s safety margin — no premature takeover (spec 8.3)
- Primary skewed -60s: renewals either keep the lease alive or the primary stands down cleanly; at no point do two writers exist
- Sweep over the skew grid {-60s, -30s, 0, +30s, +60s} for primary x standby (25 combinations) asserts the epoch invariant and single-writer property for every cell
- `make chaos-clock-skew` with pass/fail exit code; nightly CI tag

## Out of Scope
- Chaos framework infrastructure (testing-infra)
- Fake-clock admin plumbing (local-dev-experience epic, spec 18.4)

## Testing
Chaos/E2E (spec 19.9, 19.13); property-style skew sweep.

## Demo
`make chaos-clock-skew` prints the skew matrix with per-cell single-writer verdicts and PASS.

nodes.title: Chaos scenario: chaos-old-primary-recovery
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the chaos-old-primary-recovery scenario (spec 19.9): a failed primary returns after failover; pass criterion is that it stands down to read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scenario: partition the primary, fail over to a standby, then heal the partition so the old primary reconnects
- Pass: old primary observes the higher epoch and different holder, transitions to Standby, and serves reads (spec 13.4)
- Storage audit confirms zero writes accepted from the old primary after the epoch advance (fencing held throughout)
- Old primary participates as a valid failover candidate again once caught up (readiness reflects it)
- `make chaos-old-primary-recovery` with pass/fail exit code; nightly CI tag

## Out of Scope
- Chaos framework infrastructure (testing-infra)
- Stand-down implementation itself (mr-old-primary-standdown)

## Testing
Chaos/E2E (spec 19.9, 19.13).

## Demo
`make chaos-old-primary-recovery` shows partition, failover, heal, stand-down event, and PASS.

nodes.title: Chaos scenarios: chaos-crr-stall and chaos-ddb-lag
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the two replication-lag scenarios (spec 19.9): a 30-minute CRR stall must make failover wait for catchup; DDB Global Tables lag must produce stale-but-never-incorrect reads and no split-brain.

## Acceptance Criteria
- chaos-crr-stall: replication sim stalls S3 CRR; `mtcctl failover status` reports not-ready with reason; `failover initiate` blocks in `wait_for_crr` (spec 13.3 step 1) and completes only after catchup — pass: failover waits
- chaos-ddb-lag: inject DDB replication lag; pass: no split-brain, and standby-visible state is stale, never incorrect (monotonic, verifiable)
- Stall/lag durations configurable per run; scenarios use compressed timescales (seconds standing in for the spec's 30-minute fault) so the suite completes in nightly CI
- `make chaos-crr-stall` and `make chaos-ddb-lag` targets with pass/fail exit codes; nightly CI tags
- Delivered as two independently shippable PRs, one per scenario

## Out of Scope
- Chaos framework infrastructure (testing-infra)
- Replication sim lag mechanics (mr-replication-sim)

## Testing
Chaos/E2E (spec 19.9, 19.13).

## Demo
`make chaos-crr-stall` shows failover refusing then completing after catchup; `make chaos-ddb-lag` shows stale-not-incorrect reads; both PASS.

nodes.title: Per-region SoftHSM keys with dev key-replication ceremony
nodes.description:
## Goal
Simulate spec 14.2 Option A locally: each simulated region owns a SoftHSM token holding a replicated copy of the signing key, so no cross-region HSM dependency exists on the hot path and a promoted region can sign immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make key-ceremony` provisions per-region SoftHSM tokens and replicates the signing key via wrapped export/import — key material never lands on disk in plaintext (spec 14.2 replication ceremony, dev-scale)
- Each region's CA instance signs using only its local token; hot path never calls another region's HSM (spec 14.2)
- After failover, the promoted region signs checkpoints with its local key; test verifies signature continuity (same public key) across the failover boundary
- `make demo-multiregion` provisions tokens automatically
- Ceremony steps self-documenting via script help (runbook prose stays in operational-tooling)

## Out of Scope
- CloudHSM clusters/CDK; key rotation ceremonies

## Testing
Integration (three SoftHSM tokens, sign-after-failover); E2E inside the multi-region demo (spec 19.1).

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion`, fail over to us-west-2, then `mtcctl log verify` — new checkpoints validate against the same CA public key.

nodes.title: `mtcctl lease show` / `lease renew` commands
nodes.description:
## Goal
CLI surface for lease inspection and dev-only forced renewal per the spec 17.3 command tree, plus lease fields in `mtcctl status`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl lease show`: holder, region, `expires_at`, epoch; supports `--output json|yaml` (spec 17.3)
- `mtcctl lease renew`: dev/test only — gated to dev profile and privileged confirmation (`--confirm`/`--yes`)
- `mtcctl status` includes lease + epoch + role summary (spec 17.3)
- Commands consume generated OpenAPI client routes (spec 17.2); no hand-rolled HTTP
- Human output covered by a golden-file test; JSON output validated against the OpenAPI schema in tests

## Out of Scope
- Failover subcommands (mr-failover-readiness, mr-failover-initiate)
- UI lease page (mr-failover-ui)

## Testing
Unit; E2E via CLI against `make demo` environment (spec 19.13).

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl lease show` displays the live lease with expiry countdown; `mtcctl lease renew --yes` visibly refreshes `expires_at`.

nodes.title: CDK: coordination Global Table replicas + Route 53 health checks (synth-only)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Infrastructure-as-code for multi-region coordination: the `mtc-log-coordination` DynamoDB Global Table replicated to three regions (spec 8.2) and Route 53 health checks for detection (spec 13.1). Synth assertions only — no cloud deployment or spend (spec 1 non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Global Table construct with replicas in the three target regions, PK/SK per spec 8.2
- Route 53 health check per region: HTTPS endpoint, 10s interval, fail after 3 consecutive failures (spec 13.1)
- Fine-grained `aws-cdk-lib/assertions` tests for table replication config and health check parameters, plus a snapshot test
- Stack synthesizes cleanly in CI; no stack requires deployment to validate

## Out of Scope
- CloudWatch alarms/dashboards on lease metrics (observability epic)
- Any real AWS deployment (spec 1 non-goals)

## Testing
Unit (CDK assertions + snapshot) per spec 19.1.

## Demo
`npx cdk synth MultiRegionCoordinationStack` renders the template; CDK assertion tests pass in CI.

nodes.title: Anomaly response: page immediately and freeze issuance
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §20.2 mandate: on self-auditor anomaly, page immediately and freeze issuance until an operator intervenes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Anomaly result writes an issuance-freeze flag item to the coordination table with epoch-conditioned write semantics (§8.2, §8.3)
- Batch builder checks the flag before committing; when frozen, new batches are rejected with a distinct error and intake returns 503 (§20.2)
- Paging path: shared alerting SNS topic construct + anomaly CloudWatch alarm defined in CDK with synth assertions (topic is reused by obs-cw-dashboards-slo-alarms); local dev emits a CRITICAL structured log and an SSE event to the UI (§17.4)
- Privileged unfreeze exposed via admin API and `mtcctl` requiring `--confirm` (§17.3 authorization), recorded with operator identity for the admin-actions report (§20.3)
- E2E: tamper a tile in the demo env → audit → issuance blocked → unfreeze → issuance resumes

## Out of Scope
- Anomaly-detection logic itself (obs-auditor-core)
- The self-auditor-anomaly runbook (operational-tooling epic, §21)

## Testing
- Unit: flag write/read, batch-builder gate, unfreeze authorization
- Integration: LocalStack freeze/unfreeze cycle
- E2E: scripted tamper→freeze→unfreeze scenario in `tests/e2e/` (§19.13, §19.8)
- CDK synth assertions for topic + alarm

## Demo
`make demo`, corrupt a tile via helper script, `make audit`, watch ACME issuance 503, then `mtcctl` unfreeze with `--confirm` restores issuance.

nodes.title: Self-auditor engine crate (audit algorithm + signed audit records)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §20.2 self-auditor algorithm as a backend-agnostic library crate (`crates/auditor`) — the substitute for external transparency in our cosigner-free deployment (§25.8, P0).

## Acceptance Criteria
- One audit pass executes §20.2 steps 1–5: read latest checkpoint pointer; independently fetch tiles and recompute the root; verify the CA signature over the checkpoint; compare against prior audit records for append-only consistency; verify recent batches' entries are accessible and hash to the expected leaves
- Step 6: signs an audit proof with a dedicated auditor key (distinct from the CA checkpoint key) via the `Hsm` trait and writes the `audit#{tree_size}` record (§8.2)
- Result type is `Ok { tree_size, root }` or `Anomaly { reason }` with machine-readable reason classification; corrupt/truncated input never panics (§19.3 posture)
- Runs entirely against storage traits: memory backend in unit tests, LocalStack in integration tests

## Out of Scope
- Lambda packaging/scheduling (obs-auditor-lambda)
- Freeze/paging response (obs-audit-anomaly-freeze)
- Adversarial fixture suite (obs-audit-adversarial-tests)

## Testing
- Unit: each audit step in isolation on memory backend
- Property (`proptest`): audits of honestly-built logs of arbitrary size always pass (§19.2)
- Integration: full pass against LocalStack S3/DDB (§19.1)

## Demo
`cargo run -p auditor --example audit-once` against the demo log prints the recomputed root and writes an audit record.

nodes.title: Self-auditor Lambda: packaging, EventBridge schedule, CDK construct
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship the periodic self-auditor Lambda (§3 component table, §24 Phase 6): package the auditor engine for Lambda, schedule it, and define its infrastructure as CDK code validated by synth assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cargo-lambda`-built binary wrapping `obs-auditor-core` with the AWS backend; structured logs + audit-outcome metric emitted per run
- CDK construct: EventBridge schedule (hourly default per OQ-8, configurable), least-privilege IAM (read tiles/checkpoints in S3, read/write `audit#` items in DDB), error alarm
- `cdk synth` assertions cover schedule expression, env vars, and IAM policy — no real deployment (§1 non-goals)
- Deploys and runs under LocalStack via the dev environment; an invoked run writes a fresh `audit#{tree_size}` record end-to-end

## Out of Scope
- Audit algorithm changes (obs-auditor-core)
- Anomaly paging/freeze wiring (obs-audit-anomaly-freeze)

## Testing
- Unit: handler glue with memory backend
- Integration: LocalStack Lambda invoke → record visible in DDB (`--features integration`, §19.1)
- CDK synth assertion tests in TypeScript

## Demo
`make demo` then `awslocal lambda invoke` the auditor; `mtcctl audit history` (or DDB scan) shows the new audit record.

nodes.title: Audit operations: mtcctl audit run/history/verify + Audit UI page
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose the self-auditor on the admin surface (§17.3, §17.4): `mtcctl audit run` (on-demand trigger), `audit history`, and `audit verify` (independent log-consistency verification), plus the Audit UI view. Self-auditor exposure is part of the cosigner-free trust story (§25.8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: trigger audit run, list audit history (result, timestamp, checked range), run independent consistency verification
- Handlers delegate to the self-auditor service; admin layer performs no auditing itself
- `mtcctl audit run` returns run ID and outcome (or polls to completion with `--wait`); `audit history --output json` stable; `audit verify` exits non-zero on inconsistency (usable in scripts/CI)
- Audit UI page: history table with pass/fail badges, manual-run button; updates on audit-completed SSE events
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Self-auditor Lambda/implementation and scheduling (observability epic)
- Compliance reports (adm-report-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against stubbed auditor in memory backend
- Integration: demo stack — trigger run, see result in history
- E2E: `tests/e2e/audit.sh` runs audit via CLI and asserts pass

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl audit run --wait && mtcctl audit history`; same in the Audit page.

nodes.title: Wire self-auditor into make demo and add make audit
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire the self-auditor into the local demo (§18.1) and add `make audit` (§18.8), so every demo run continuously demonstrates the transparency story (§25.8) on a laptop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo` starts the self-auditor on a periodic dev-mode interval (from the dev profile) against the local stack
- `make audit` triggers one full audit pass on demand and prints a human-readable verdict summary
- Audit results surface in the admin UI audit view and via `mtcctl`
- A dev-only corruption helper script damages one tile; the next audit pass fails loudly, naming the tile — the documented "seeing is believing" check
- Auditor log lines are clearly attributed in demo output

## Out of Scope
- Self-auditor implementation (observability epic)
- Compliance report generation (§20.3)

## Testing
- Integration: auditor pass against demo-stack state
- E2E: demo smoke extended — audit verdict OK; corruption helper flips it to FAIL

## Demo
`make demo` → `make audit` prints PASS; run the corruption helper, `make audit` prints FAIL identifying the corrupted tile.

nodes.title: Adversarial tamper-detection test suite for the self-auditor
nodes.description:
## Goal
Prove the self-auditor actually catches misbehavior: an adversarial fixture suite (§19.8) exercising every §20.2 detection obligation, since the auditor is the whole trust story without cosigners (§25.8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures on the memory backend for: corrupted tile bytes; deleted/missing entry object; forked history (checkpoint inconsistent with prior audit record); invalid CA signature on checkpoint; rolled-back tree size; batch entry whose hash mismatches its leaf
- Each fixture yields `Anomaly` with the correct reason classification — no silent pass, no panic
- Property test: honestly-built random logs never flag (zero false positives); a random single-byte mutation within the recomputed range is always detected (§19.2)
- Suite runs in CI in <30s with no external dependencies (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Chaos/fault-injection at the infrastructure level (testing-infrastructure epic, §19.9)
- Fuzzing wire-format parsers (core-mtc-library epic, §19.3)

## Testing
- Unit + property + adversarial layers (§19.1, §19.2, §19.8); this ticket IS the test suite

## Demo
`cargo test -p auditor --test adversarial` shows each tamper class detected with its reason code.

nodes.title: Audit admin surface: mtcctl audit run/history/verify, UI audit page, make audit
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose the self-auditor to operators with full CLI/UI parity (§1 goals): `mtcctl audit` subcommands (§17.3), the Audit UI view (§17.4), and the `make audit` target (§18.8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI additions for trigger-run / list-history / get-record flowing through `make api-gen` (§17.5)
- `mtcctl audit run` triggers an on-demand audit; `mtcctl audit history` lists `audit#` records; both support `--output json` (§17.3)
- `mtcctl audit verify` runs the auditor engine client-side directly against storage — independent verification that does not trust the service (§17.3, §20.2)
- UI audit page: history table, manual-run button, SSE-pushed new results (§17.4 key views)
- `make audit` runs the self-auditor manually against the demo env (§18.8)
- E2E shell test: issue → `make audit` → `mtcctl audit history` shows the new record

## Out of Scope
- Audit engine internals (obs-auditor-core); freeze/unfreeze op (obs-audit-anomaly-freeze)
- Generic UI shell/navigation (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers and CLI arg parsing
- E2E: CLI-driven scenario in `tests/e2e/` (§19.13)

## Demo
`make audit && mtcctl audit history --output json`; open the UI Audit page and click Run.

nodes.title: Per-certificate forensics: mtcctl cert lookup + cert UI view
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement §20.2 per-certificate forensics: a single lookup that reconstructs everything known about one issued cert, via API, CLI, and UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admin API endpoint aggregating for an index: parsed TBSCert contents, batch info (ID, timestamp, `source_type`/`source_id`, region of primary at issuance — §8.2 batch item), covering checkpoint, revocation status, pruning status, source metadata (§20.2)
- Revocation, pruning, and served-proof-audit-trail fields degrade to explicit `unavailable` until those subsystems ship — never fabricated
- `mtcctl cert lookup --index N` human-readable and `--output json` (§17.3)
- UI cert lookup view (§17.4 key views) rendering the same aggregation
- E2E: issue via demo, look up index 0, TBSCert and batch fields match what was issued

## Out of Scope
- Served-proof audit trail collection (read-path epic emits it; this ticket only renders when present)
- Revocation/pruning status sources (their epics)

## Testing
- Unit: aggregation against memory backend, including degraded fields
- Integration: LocalStack-backed lookup
- E2E: CLI scenario in `tests/e2e/` (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo` then `mtcctl cert lookup --index 0` prints the full forensic record.

nodes.title: Metrics registry with Prometheus and CloudWatch EMF exporters
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the typed metrics facade for the §20.1 metric set with Prometheus-compatible exposition and CloudWatch EMF emission, usable from Fargate services and Lambdas.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Typed constructors for all 13 metrics in the §20.1 table with correct instrument kinds (histogram/counter/gauge) and exact spec names
- Label support, e.g. `entries_by_source_total{source_type}` (§20.1, §10)
- Prometheus text exposition served at `/metrics` on an admin port
- CloudWatch EMF JSON emitter behind config, compatible with LocalStack log ingestion (no real AWS spend, §1)
- Metric-name constants exported from one module so dashboards/alarms (CDK) can assert against them
- Unit tests: register → record → export round-trip for each instrument kind; names match spec table exactly

## Out of Scope
- Wiring metrics into CA service components (obs-service-instrumentation)
- Dashboards/alarms (obs-cw-dashboards-slo-alarms)

## Testing
- Unit: registry, exporters, naming conformance (§19.1, no external deps); registry+Prometheus, EMF emitter, and /metrics endpoint land as separate PRs

## Demo
Run the demo env, `curl localhost:<admin-port>/metrics` shows the registered metric families.

nodes.title: Compliance report framework: signed envelopes + issuance log report
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the §20.3 compliance-reporting framework — signed report envelopes generated via `mtcctl report` — proven by the issuance-log report as its first vertical slice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Report envelope: type, date range, generated-at, generator identity, content hash, signature by a **separate reporting key** (§20.3) held behind the `Hsm` trait (SoftHSM in dev)
- Deterministic content ordering so identical inputs produce byte-identical signed reports
- `mtcctl report issuance --from --to`: all certs in range with full audit trail and per-source segmentation (§20.3, §17.3)
- `mtcctl report verify <file>` validates the signature and content hash; tampered reports fail (extension of the §17.3 report subcommands)
- JSON output plus human-readable summary (§17.3 output formats)

## Out of Scope
- Other report generators (obs-report-audit-slo, obs-report-operational, obs-adapter-observability)
- Reports UI view (obs-report-ui)
- Reporting-key ceremony/rotation procedures (operational-tooling epic)

## Testing
- Unit: envelope signing/verification, deterministic serialization, issuance query against memory backend (§19.1)
- E2E: issue → `mtcctl report issuance` → `verify` passes; byte-flip → `verify` fails (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo`, then `mtcctl report issuance --from <t0> --to now | mtcctl report verify -` prints a valid signed report.

nodes.title: Instrument CA service pipeline with spans and §20.1 metrics
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire the §20.1 span hierarchy and metric set into the CA write path so every issuance is traceable end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Top-level `issue_batch` span contains nested `lease_check`, `allocate_indices`, `tree_update`, `hsm_sign`, `commit` spans (§20.1); correlation ID flows from intake to commit
- Metrics emitted at the right sites: `issuance_latency_seconds`, `batch_commit_latency_seconds`, `hsm_signing_latency_seconds`, `batches_committed_total`, `batches_abandoned_total`, `entries_by_source_total{source_type}`
- Lease/epoch metrics from the coordinator: `lease_renewals_total`, `lease_renewals_failed_total`, `epoch_advances_total` (§20.1)
- Tile cache hit/miss counters instrumented in the storage facade (§20.1); replication-lag gauges emitted where measurable in local sim, stubs documented otherwise
- Integration test: one issuance on memory backend asserts expected span tree and metric deltas

## Out of Scope
- Read-path (proof-server) instrumentation — read-path epic
- Dashboards and alarms

## Testing
- Unit: span/metric emission with in-memory backend (§19.1)
- Integration: LocalStack issuance produces spans + counters (`--features integration`)

## Demo
`make demo` issues certs; `curl /metrics` shows counters advancing; JSON logs show the nested `issue_batch` span timings.

nodes.title: Tree visualization in admin UI (SVG, SSE-updated)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the §20.2 tree visualization feature: an SVG render of recent tree state showing recent batches, landmark positions, pruning watermark, revoked ranges, and audit checkpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admin API data endpoint returning a bounded tree summary: recent batches with index ranges, landmark positions, pruning watermark, revoked ranges, audit checkpoints (§20.2)
- SVG render via `templates/components/tree-viz.html` + vendored vanilla `static/tree-viz.js` — no build toolchain, assets embedded with `rust-embed` (§17.4)
- Pruning/revocation/audit overlays degrade gracefully (layer hidden with a note) while those subsystems are unshipped
- SSE-driven refresh when new batches or audit results land (§17.4 real-time updates)
- Askama templates compile-time checked; endpoint payload size bounded for large trees

## Out of Scope
- Generic UI shell, layout, navigation (admin-surface epic)
- Log inventory dashboard tiles (obs-log-inventory-dashboard)

## Testing
- Unit: summary endpoint against memory backend fixtures
- E2E: demo env page load contains SVG nodes for committed batches; SSE event appends a batch (webapp test harness, §19.1)

## Demo
`make demo`, open the admin UI Tree view, issue certs, watch new batch nodes appear live.

nodes.title: Runbook framework: template, postmortem template, index, structure lint
nodes.description:
## Goal
Establish `docs/runbooks/` per §21.2: a runbook template with the five mandated sections (Detection, Initial assessment, Mitigation steps, Recovery procedure, Postmortem template), a shared postmortem template, an index page listing the eight required runbooks, and a lint script that enforces template structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/runbooks/TEMPLATE.md` contains the five §21.2 sections with guidance comments
- `docs/runbooks/POSTMORTEM.md` template exists (timeline, impact, root cause, action items)
- `docs/runbooks/README.md` indexes all eight required runbooks (§21.2) with status (stub/complete) and maps each to the alerts (§20.1) and chaos scenarios (§19.9) that exercise it
- `scripts/lint-runbooks.sh` (or small Rust/shell tool) fails when a runbook is missing a required section; `make lint-runbooks` target added
- Lint script has tests covering pass/fail fixtures

## Out of Scope
- Content of individual runbooks (separate tickets)
- Wiring lint into CI (ops-docs-ci-quality-gates)

## Testing
- Unit tests for the lint script against good/bad fixture runbooks (§19.1); no property/fuzz/Kani/Loom applicable

## Demo
After merge: `make lint-runbooks` passes; deliberately delete a section from a stub and see it fail.

nodes.title: Runbook: HSM unavailability
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/hsm-unavailability.md` for checkpoint-signing outages, per §14 and §21.2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection: checkpoint cadence alarm, HSM error-rate metrics, batch retry alerts (§20.1); distinguishes transient errors from full outage and connection-pool exhaustion (§19.7)
- Assessment: is this one region (consider failover, cross-ref primary-failure runbook) or both (issuance pause)? References cross-region key management model (§14.2)
- Mitigation: expected system behavior per chaos-hsm-down (§19.9) — batch retries, alerts, eventual stand-down; operator actions for pausing intake and communicating issuance latency breach
- Recovery: resume criteria, backlog drain expectations at capacity numbers from §21.1 (~40 signings/hour at 10K certs/hour), post-recovery self-auditor check
- Drill transcript using the SoftHSM dev backend (stop the SoftHSM/PKCS#11 provider mid-batch in the local env)
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- HSM client retry logic (ca-service epic); key compromise handling (ops-runbook-key-compromise)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual E2E drill in local env (§18)

## Demo
After merge: kill SoftHSM mid-demo, follow the runbook, restore signing.

nodes.title: Runbook: primary region failure and manual failover
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/primary-failure.md` covering detection through promotion for a lost primary region, per §13.1–13.3 and §21.2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection section lists the §13.1 signals: Route 53 health check failures, lease renewal metric stall, checkpoint cadence alarm, standby lease-expiry observation
- Assessment section includes the §13.2 preconditions checklist: primary unreachable, standby caught up (latest checkpoint replicated, S3 CRR current), freshest standby selected
- Mitigation walks `mtcctl failover initiate --to <region> --reason <...>` and annotates each step of the idempotent promotion procedure (§13.3): checkpoint verification, tile snapshot consistency / CRR wait, abandoning in-flight batches, lease claim + epoch increment, gap-fill with null_entry
- Recovery section states RTO/RPO expectations (§13.5: RPO zero for committed work, RTO 5–15 min) and verification steps (`/health/primary`, self-auditor green)
- Runbook validated by a documented drill transcript against the local multi-region sim (§18.3): `make demo-multiregion`, `make partition-region us-east-1`, follow the runbook, chaos-primary-loss pass criterion holds (§19.9)
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Failover CLI implementation (multi-region epic); old-primary recovery/failback (ops-runbook-region-recovery)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint (unit-level); E2E-style manual drill via local sim (§18.3, §19.13)

## Demo
After merge: run the drill above end-to-end following only the runbook text.

nodes.title: Runbook: self-auditor anomaly
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/self-auditor-anomaly.md` for handling a red self-auditor result, per §21.2. The self-auditor is the substitute for external transparency in this cosigner-free deployment (§25.8), so an anomaly is a potential integrity incident.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection: self-auditor alarm, `/health/audit` endpoint (§20.5)
- Assessment: classify anomaly type — inclusion proof failure, checkpoint signature mismatch, tree inconsistency, replayed/stale checkpoint (§19.8) — with severity for each and which are stop-the-world
- Mitigation: when to halt issuance, when to treat as suspected key compromise (cross-ref ops-runbook-key-compromise), evidence-preservation steps (snapshot relevant tiles/checkpoints before any remediation; Object Lock means originals are immutable, §15.3)
- Recovery: re-run audit, forensic verification via per-cert forensics tooling (§20.2), criteria for resuming issuance
- Includes escalation to postmortem template for any confirmed integrity violation
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Self-auditor Lambda implementation (observability epic)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual drill by feeding the local self-auditor a corrupted tile fixture (§18.5)

## Demo
After merge: corrupt a tile in the local env, watch the auditor go red, follow the runbook.

nodes.title: Report operations: mtcctl report issuance/revocation/compliance + Reports UI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose report generation on the admin surface (§17.3, §20.3: reports signed by a separate reporting key, generated via `mtcctl report`): issuance log report, revocation report, and compliance bundle, plus the Reports UI view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: generate issuance, revocation, and compliance reports with time-range parameters; responses include the report artifact (or a storage ref) and its signature
- `mtcctl report issuance|revocation|compliance --from --to` writes the report to stdout or `--out FILE`; `--output json` wraps with metadata (range, signature, generated-at)
- JSON output includes the detached signature (base64) and reporting key ID; E2E asserts both fields are non-empty
- Reports UI page: form to request each report type and download the result (parity)
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Report content assembly and reporting-key signing internals (observability epic)
- Audit runs (adm-audit-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handler parameter validation, empty-range behavior
- Integration: generate reports against demo stack with issued+revoked certs
- E2E: shell script generates compliance bundle and asserts signature + key ID fields present

## Demo
`mtcctl report compliance --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-07-01 --out bundle.tar.gz` then download the same from the Reports page.

nodes.title: Seed operational skills: add-metric.md, write-runbook.md, add-chaos-test.md
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed the three operational skills from §23.1: `add-metric.md` (CloudWatch metric), `write-runbook.md` (runbook template plus alert wiring), and `add-chaos-test.md` (new chaos scenario).

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `add-metric.md` — files involved in metric emission and dashboard/alarm wiring, naming conventions, pitfalls (unbounded cardinality, metrics without alarms)
- PR 2: `write-runbook.md` — runbook template location, alert-to-runbook wiring, expected content structure
- PR 3: `add-chaos-test.md` — chaos framework files, one merged scenario as the worked pattern, pitfalls (non-deterministic assertions, missing invariant checks)
- All three pass `make skill-lint` and fit the ~5-file scoping budget (§23.8)

## Out of Scope
- The metrics, runbook, and chaos frameworks themselves (observability and testing-infrastructure epics)

## Testing
- `make skill-lint`; each skill dry-run against its framework, recorded in the PR description (§19.13 spirit)

## Demo
Use `add-chaos-test.md` to scaffold a no-op chaos scenario, run it locally against the dev environment, then revert.

nodes.title: CloudWatch dashboards and SLO burn-rate alarms as CDK code
nodes.description:
## Goal
Define the cloud-side observability surface as code: CloudWatch dashboards for the §20.1 metric set and alarm coverage for the five §20.1 SLOs, validated purely via `cdk synth` assertions (§1: no real deployment).

## Acceptance Criteria
- CDK dashboard constructs: service-health dashboard (latencies, lease, batch, cache metrics) and CA-specific dashboard (issuance by source, replication lag) using metric names imported/checked against the telemetry constants (obs-metrics-core)
- Alarm set covering the §20.1 SLO table: ACME issuance success 99.9%, issuance p99 <10s, lease renewal 99.99%, HSM signing 99.9%, read-path availability 99.95% — multi-window burn-rate where applicable
- All alarms route to the shared SNS alerting topic construct introduced by obs-audit-anomaly-freeze
- Synth assertion tests verify widget metric names, alarm thresholds, and topic wiring; drift between Rust metric constants and CDK names fails CI

## Out of Scope
- In-app UI dashboards (obs-log-inventory-dashboard)
- PagerDuty/real notification integrations (none — §1 non-goals)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion tests (TypeScript unit layer, §19.1); no live AWS

## Demo
`cdk synth` renders dashboard/alarm JSON; `npm test` in `cdk/` passes the assertion suite.

nodes.title: Log inventory dashboard (UI): always-visible CA state
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §20.2 log inventory dashboard: the always-visible operational picture of the log in the admin UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dashboard tiles for: tree size, total certs issued, currently-valid count, issuance/revocation rate, pruning watermark, storage size by category, per-source intake rates, active relying parties (§20.2)
- Rates computed over a sliding window from metrics; storage sizes from the storage facade
- Fields without a live source yet (revocation rate, pruning watermark, relying parties) show explicit `n/a — subsystem not deployed`
- SSE updates push new values without polling (§17.4)
- Aggregation logic unit-tested with synthetic state

## Out of Scope
- CloudWatch (cloud-side) dashboards (obs-cw-dashboards-slo-alarms)
- Tree SVG visualization (obs-tree-visualization)
- Generic dashboard page shell (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit: tile aggregation and rate windows (§19.1)
- E2E: demo env dashboard reflects an issuance burst (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo`, open the dashboard, run the issuance demo, watch tree size and intake rate tiles advance in real time.

nodes.title: Self-auditor history and SLO compliance reports
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add the §20.3 self-auditor-history and SLO-compliance report generators on top of the report framework.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Self-auditor history report: all `audit#` checkpoints in the date range with outcomes, tree sizes, roots (§20.3, §8.2)
- SLO compliance report: achievement vs each SLI/SLO pair in the §20.1 table over a selectable period, computed from recorded metrics, with pass/fail per SLO and observed values
- Both emitted as signed envelopes via the framework; JSON + human summary; reachable via `mtcctl report` and included in the `mtcctl report compliance` bundle (§17.3)
- Missing metric history yields explicit `insufficient data`, never a fabricated pass

## Out of Scope
- Operational reports (obs-report-operational)
- Alarming on SLO breach (obs-cw-dashboards-slo-alarms)

## Testing
- Unit: generators against synthetic audit records and metric series, including insufficient-data paths (§19.1)
- E2E: demo env produces both reports after `make audit` and an issuance burst (§19.13)

## Demo
`make audit && mtcctl report compliance --from <t0> --to now` shows audit-history and SLO sections in the signed bundle.

nodes.title: Operational reports: revocation, pruning, admin actions, failover, key ceremony
nodes.description:
## Goal
Complete the §20.3 report table with the five operational-record generators, each consuming its owning epic's event records.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generators for: revocation log (justification, operator, timestamp), pruning log (affected ranges), admin actions (all privileged calls with operator identity), failover events (region transitions, timestamps, outcomes), key ceremony events (HSM generation/rotation/replication) — per §20.3 table
- Each generator reads its subsystem's records where shipped and otherwise emits an explicit signed `no data source available` section — reports never silently omit a category; ticket is NOT blocked on those subsystems shipping
- Record schemas consumed via fixture-defined interfaces so owning epics can wire real sources later without changing the generators' envelope output shape
- All included in the `mtcctl report compliance` bundle (§17.3); signed envelopes via the framework
- Fixture-driven unit tests per generator with representative event records

## Out of Scope
- Producing the underlying event records (revocation, pruning, admin-surface, multi-region, operational-tooling epics)
- Issuance/audit/SLO generators (obs-report-framework, obs-report-audit-slo)

## Testing
- Unit: per-generator fixtures including empty/absent sources (§19.1)
- E2E: `mtcctl report compliance` bundle generation in the demo env (§19.13)

## Demo
`mtcctl report compliance --from <t0> --to now` emits a signed bundle with all five sections present (populated or explicitly empty).

nodes.title: Reports UI view: generate, download, and verify signed reports
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §17.4 "Reports" key UI view so operators can generate §20.3 compliance reports from the browser with CLI/UI parity (§17.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reports page lists available report types from the §20.3 table with a date-range form; unavailable generators are shown disabled with a reason
- Generate button calls the admin report API (same OpenAPI operations `mtcctl report` uses, §17.5); completion pushed via SSE (§17.4)
- Completed report downloadable as its signed-envelope file; page shows the envelope's content hash and signature-verification status badge
- Askama template compile-time checked; htmx-only, no build toolchain (§17.4)
- E2E: generate an issuance report from the UI in the demo env and verify the downloaded file with `mtcctl report verify`

## Out of Scope
- Report generators and envelope format (obs-report-framework and successors)
- Generic UI shell/navigation (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit: handler + template rendering against memory backend (§19.1)
- E2E: webapp-driven generate/download verified via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo`, open the Reports view, generate an issuance report, download it, `mtcctl report verify <file>` passes.

nodes.title: Runbook: adapter flood
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/adapter-flood.md` for an intake adapter flooding the issuance pipeline, per §21.2 and the adapter model in §10.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection: per-adapter intake rate metrics and adapter activity reporting (§20.3), queue depth / backpressure alarms, issuance latency SLO burn (§20.1)
- Assessment: legitimate burst vs misbehaving adapter vs abuse; compare observed rate against capacity plan figures (§21.1: 10K certs/hour baseline)
- Mitigation: per-adapter throttle/disable steps via admin surface (`mtcctl adapter pause`), expected backpressure behavior per chaos-adapter-flood pass criterion (§19.9: backpressure works, no entries lost)
- Recovery: drain backlog, verify no accepted entries were dropped (append-only invariant §11.2), re-enable adapter with rate limit
- Drill transcript: flood the ACME adapter in the local env and follow the runbook
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Backpressure/rate-limit implementation (ca-service epic); chaos-adapter-flood scenario harness (testing-infra)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual E2E drill via local load generation (§18)

## Demo
After merge: run a local flood, throttle the adapter following only the runbook, confirm zero lost entries via self-auditor.

nodes.title: Runbook: S3 cross-region replication stall
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/crr-stall.md` for stalled S3 CRR / DDB Global Tables lag, per §21.2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection: replication lag metrics/alarms (§20.1), standby freshness checks
- Assessment: quantify lag; decision table for whether failover is currently safe (per §13.2 the CLI blocks promotion until standby caught up; per chaos-crr-stall §19.9 failover must wait for catch-up)
- Mitigation: steps for the stalled-CRR-plus-attempted-promotion case (§19.8 adversarial scenario) — explicitly forbid forcing promotion past the consistency check; escalation options if the primary is also down (RTO tradeoff per §13.5)
- Recovery: confirm replication current, run self-auditor, verify tile snapshot consistency matches latest checkpoint (§13.3 step 1)
- Drill transcript using the local sim's configurable CRR lag (§18.3)
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- CRR lag metric implementation (observability epic); CRR simulation (dev-experience/testing epics)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual E2E drill via `make demo-multiregion` with injected lag (§18.3)

## Demo
After merge: inject 30-min simulated CRR delay, attempt failover, observe the wait, follow runbook to resolution.

nodes.title: Runbook: old primary recovery and failback
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/region-recovery.md` covering the return of a failed primary (§13.4) and deliberate failback to the original region.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Documents the §13.4 stand-down invariant: returning region reads lease, sees higher epoch + different holder, stands down to read-only; explains why split-brain is impossible (all writes conditional on epoch, §8.3)
- Verification steps: `/health/primary` returns false on old primary, standby-mode metrics green, no stale-epoch write errors in logs
- Failback section: treat failback as a fresh manual failover (cross-reference primary-failure runbook), including CRR catch-up preconditions
- Includes drill transcript against local sim: partition primary, promote standby, heal partition, observe stand-down (chaos-old-primary-recovery pass criterion, §19.9)
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Promotion procedure details (primary-failure runbook)
- Standby read-only mode implementation (multi-region epic)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual E2E drill via `make demo-multiregion` (§18.3)

## Demo
After merge: heal a partitioned region in the local sim and confirm stand-down following only the runbook.

nodes.title: Capacity prediction metrics (S3, DDB, HSM, tree growth)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement §20.4 forward-looking capacity metrics: trend-based projections for storage, coordination, signing, and tree growth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Periodic job computes: projected S3 storage growth by category, DDB item-count growth, HSM signing-rate headroom vs observed peak, tree growth (entries/day trend and time-to-threshold estimate) (§20.4)
- Exposed as `capacity_*` gauges through the metrics facade
- Simple documented model (e.g. windowed linear trend); insufficient-history yields an explicit `unknown` state, not zero
- Unit tests: known synthetic series produce expected projections and thresholds

## Out of Scope
- Dashboard tile rendering (follow-up in obs-log-inventory-dashboard once both exist)
- Auto-scaling or acting on predictions
- Cost modeling (§5 handles cost narrative)

## Testing
- Unit: projection math on synthetic series (§19.1)

## Demo
Run the demo issuance burst, then `curl /metrics | grep capacity_` shows growth projections.

nodes.title: Relying party telemetry (anonymized) ingestion and surfacing
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement §20.2 relying-party telemetry: anonymized aggregate signals about how verifiers experience the log.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ingest hook consuming read-path signals: landmark-age distribution, signatureless→full fallback rate, verification failure breakdown by reason, coarse geographic distribution (§20.2)
- Aggregation-only storage: no per-client identifiers or IPs retained; a test asserts persisted records contain no client-identifying fields (§20.1 sensitive-data rule)
- Surfaced as metrics through the facade and as a dashboard section with `active relying parties` feeding the log inventory view (§20.2)
- Works in the local demo via the verification-loop demo driving the read path

## Out of Scope
- Read-path/proof-server emission of the signals (read-path epic provides the hook)
- Client-side verification library changes

## Testing
- Unit: aggregation and anonymization assertions (§19.1)
- Integration: demo verify loop populates aggregates (§19.1)

## Demo
Run the demo verify loop, open the dashboard RP panel: fallback rate and landmark-age histogram populate.

nodes.title: Runbook: emergency revocation
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/emergency-revocation.md` operationalizing the §16.3 emergency revocation flow, per §21.2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection/trigger section: what qualifies as an emergency revocation (compromised subscriber key, misissuance found by forensics §20.2)
- Procedure annotates each §16.3 step: operator initiation via CLI/UI with justification + incident ref, revocation-processor Lambda generates list, HSM signs, deterministic-key S3 write, atomic DDB latest-revocation pointer update, push-triggered refresh
- Verification: confirm relying parties see the new list (distribution mechanisms §16.2), check revocation log report (§20.3)
- Includes rollback guidance (revocations are append-only in spirit; document un-revocation policy explicitly)
- Time-bound targets stated (end-to-end propagation expectation) and postmortem requirement for every emergency revocation
- Drill transcript: revoke a demo cert in the local env end-to-end
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Revocation Lambda and distribution implementation (revocation epic); key compromise response (ops-runbook-key-compromise)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual E2E drill via CLI in local env (§19.13)

## Demo
After merge: `make demo`, issue a cert, revoke it following only the runbook, verify a relying party rejects it.

nodes.title: Runbook: suspected key compromise
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/key-compromise.md` for suspected compromise of CA signing keys, per §21.2 and threat model §3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection: wrong-signature anomalies from self-auditor, unexplained checkpoints, HSM audit trail discrepancies (§19.8 covers wrong signatures from a "compromised" HSM)
- Assessment: scope determination — which key (checkpoint signing vs reporting key §20.3), which regions given the cross-region key management model (§14.2), blast radius in time (which batches signed since last known-good audit)
- Mitigation: halt issuance in all regions, initiate emergency revocation (cross-ref ops-runbook-emergency-revocation) for affected ranges, preserve HSM audit logs and key ceremony records (§20.3)
- Recovery: key rotation ceremony steps referencing §14.1–14.2, re-establishing relying-party trust in the new key, restart criteria
- States explicitly what is unrecoverable (trust in checkpoints signed during the compromise window) and how the append-only log bounds the damage
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Key rotation tooling implementation; HSM integration code (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; tabletop-exercise transcript (this scenario is not fully drillable locally; document the tabletop per §19.8 red-team scenarios)

## Demo
After merge: tabletop walkthrough recorded in the runbook appendix; `make lint-runbooks` green.

nodes.title: PruningCheckpoint domain type, wire serialization, and fuzz target
nodes.description:
## Goal
Define the pruning checkpoint structure — a signed declaration of `pruned_range = [start, end) at tree_size T` (§15.2) — with newtype-based domain types (§22) and wire serialization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PruningCheckpoint` type: leaf-index range, tree_size, timestamp, signing key id; invalid ranges (start > end, end > tree_size) unconstructible or rejected on parse
- Serialize/parse implemented in the mtc wire-format style; `parse(serialize(x)) == x` round-trip property test (§19.2)
- Malformed input rejected without panic
- Fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_pruning_checkpoint.rs` with seed corpus checked into `fuzz/corpus/` (§19.3); bug-finding inputs become regression fixtures

## Out of Scope
- Signing (prune-checkpoint-signer)
- Persistence/commit (prune-commit-protocol)

## Testing
- Unit, property (proptest round-trip), fuzz (cargo-fuzz)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-core pruning_checkpoint` green; `cargo fuzz run parse_pruning_checkpoint -- -max_total_time=60` finds no crashes.

nodes.title: Sign pruning checkpoints with dedicated HSM-backed pruning key
nodes.description:
## Goal
Sign `PruningCheckpoint` declarations with the dedicated pruning-checkpoint key (§14.1, ECDSA P-256 in v1) via the `Hsm` trait, reusing checkpoint-signer plumbing; pruning is never silent (§15.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sign/verify functions for pruning checkpoints; signature verifies against the published pruning key
- Key id distinct from the log checkpoint signing key (§14.1 key table)
- Works against memory HSM and SoftHSM PKCS#11; SoftHSM path marked non-FIPS via `is_fips_validated()` (§14.4)
- Verification failure on tampered bytes covered by test

## Out of Scope
- Commit/persistence sequence (prune-commit-protocol)
- Key ceremony / rotation tooling (operational-tooling epic)

## Testing
- Unit (memory HSM backend), integration (SoftHSM via PKCS#11)

## Demo
In demo env: helper command signs a sample pruning declaration with SoftHSM and verifies it, printing the key id used.

nodes.title: Pruning commit sequence: sign, persist checkpoint, advance watermark (primary-only)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the commit half of §15.2: plan -> sign -> persist pruning checkpoint to S3 with indefinite retention (§15.3) -> advance DDB watermark epoch-conditionally. Runs only on the primary (lease-enforced).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Checkpoint stored under the checkpoints prefix via `put_with_retention` with indefinite/max retention; bytes immutable thereafter (§8 invariants)
- Watermark advance uses epoch ConditionExpression; epoch bump mid-commit aborts cleanly with no watermark change
- Standby (non-leaseholder) refuses to run the commit
- No deletion performed in this step (deletion is a separate, later step)
- Pruning event record (range, tree_size, timestamp, operator/trigger) appended for the compliance Pruning log (§20.3)
- Retry after partial failure is idempotent

## Out of Scope
- Deletion executor (prune-deletion-executor); workflow orchestration (prune-stepfn-workflow)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backends), integration (LocalStack S3 + DDB), failure-injection test for mid-commit epoch bump

## Demo
Demo env: invoke commit step; show new pruning checkpoint object in LocalStack S3 and advanced `latest-pruning` item.

nodes.title: Deletion executor: remove pruned leaf objects only after Object Lock expiry
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the deletion step of §15.2: after the pruning checkpoint is committed and replicated, remove leaf/entry objects in the pruned range whose Object Lock retention has expired. §15.2/§8 designate S3 lifecycle as the production removal mechanism (prune-cdk-lifecycle); this executor is the workflow's explicit deletion pass so pruned state is deterministic, observable, and testable on LocalStack, and both must agree on eligibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deletes only object keys from the planner's set, all below the committed watermark read from the `latest-pruning` item
- Replication precondition (§15.2 "after commit + replication") checked before any delete; configured no-op in single-region dev mode
- Objects with unexpired retention are skipped and reported, never force-deleted; Compliance-mode AccessDenied treated as an expected, non-fatal outcome (§15.3)
- Tiles needed for proofs of unpruned entries are never deleted; pruning checkpoints never deleted (§15.3)
- Partial-failure resume: re-running completes remaining deletes without error

## Out of Scope
- Workflow orchestration/scheduling (prune-stepfn-workflow)
- Lifecycle CDK rules (prune-cdk-lifecycle)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backend), integration (LocalStack Object Lock: delete refused before retain-until, succeeds after)

## Demo
Demo env with short dev retention: run executor; `awslocal s3api list-objects` shows pruned entries gone, tiles and checkpoints intact.

nodes.title: Object Lock retention validated end-to-end on LocalStack
nodes.description:
## Goal
Deliver the Phase 7 obligation "Object Lock retention validated end-to-end" (§24): prove on LocalStack that Compliance-mode retention actually enforces append-only storage and that pruning respects it (§15.3, §8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- E2E suite: entries written via `put_with_retention` cannot be deleted before retain-until (delete attempt fails)
- With short dev retention + fake-clock advance (§18.4), the full pruning workflow runs and pruned entries are removed only after expiry
- Pruning checkpoints survive all pruning runs (indefinite retention, §15.3)
- Multi-region sim (`make demo-multiregion`, §18.3): replicated objects retain Object Lock attributes across simulated CRR
- Suite gated behind `--features integration` (§19.1) and wired into CI integration lane

## Out of Scope
- CDK synth assertions (prune-cdk-lifecycle)
- CLI-driven scenario test (prune-e2e-demo)

## Testing
- Integration + E2E against LocalStack (single-region and multi-region sim)

## Demo
`make demo` then `cargo test --features integration -p pruning objectlock_e2e` — output shows denied-before/allowed-after deletion transcript.

nodes.title: Pruning planner: compute prunable range and object set honoring retention
nodes.description:
## Goal
Compute the candidate `pruned_range = [start, end)` and the exact set of leaf/entry objects eligible for deletion, given retention policy, injected clock, current watermark, and tree size (§15.2). Interior nodes are retained as needed via the tile structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Planner never includes an entry whose Object Lock retention (via `get_retention`, §9.1) has not expired
- Output range is well-formed: watermark <= start <= end <= tree_size; deterministic given inputs
- Object-key set covers only pruned leaf/entry objects; tiles required for inclusion proofs of unpruned entries are never listed (§15.2)
- Uses injected `Clock` (§18.4, §22.11) — no wall-clock reads

## Out of Scope
- Signing/commit (prune-commit-protocol); deletion (prune-deletion-executor)
- Proof-preservation property suite (prune-proof-property)

## Testing
- Unit, property (never prunes within retention window), Kani harness on range arithmetic (no overflow; well-formed range invariant)

## Demo
`cargo test -p ca-pruning planner`; dry-run helper prints planned range against a fixture tree.

nodes.title: Property tests: pruning preserves proofs for unpruned entries
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the §19.2 invariant: "Pruning a range and verifying a proof for an unpruned entry still works," plus tile-retention sufficiency (§15.2: interior nodes retained naturally by tile structure).

## Acceptance Criteria
- proptest strategy generates trees of arbitrary size, applies planner-produced pruned ranges, then asserts inclusion proofs verify for every unpruned index
- Negative control: removing a tile the planner marked as retained causes proof verification to fail (demonstrates the retained set is tight and necessary)
- Shrunk counterexamples from any failure captured as permanent regression fixtures (§19.3 corpus discipline)
- Runs in the fast unit lane (<30s, §19.1) with bounded case counts; extended case count behind a feature/env flag

## Out of Scope
- Planner implementation changes (prune-planner) beyond bug fixes the tests surface

## Testing
- Property (proptest), unit regression fixtures

## Demo
`cargo test -p ca-pruning proof_preservation` green; run with `PROPTEST_CASES=10000` for the extended sweep.

nodes.title: RetentionPolicy config: 7-year default, configurable, indefinite pruning checkpoints
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the retention policy configuration: default 7 years, configurable (§15.1); computes `retain_until` for entries/tiles/checkpoints; pruning checkpoints retained indefinitely (§15.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RetentionPolicy` type parsed from service config with 7-year default; validation rejects zero/negative durations
- Helper computing `retain_until: SystemTime` for a given write time, used by ObjectLock `put_with_retention` call sites (§9.1)
- Pruning-checkpoint object class returns an indefinite/max sentinel retention
- Dev-mode override permitting short retention (minutes) so pruning is demoable on a laptop with the fake clock (§18.4)

## Out of Scope
- S3 lifecycle CDK rules (prune-cdk-lifecycle)
- Prunable-range computation (prune-planner)

## Testing
- Unit (boundary math, config parsing), property (retain_until monotonic in write time)

## Demo
`cargo test -p ca-pruning retention_policy`; demo env config shows short dev retention in `mtcctl status` output.

nodes.title: Pruning workflow orchestration (Step Functions per ADR) + pruning-worker Lambda
nodes.description:
## Goal
Orchestrate plan -> commit -> delete as the pruning workflow (Phase 7 §24; §7 pruning-worker Lambda), per the OQ-7 ADR decision, runnable end-to-end on LocalStack.

## Acceptance Criteria
- State machine (or Lambda chain per ADR) definition wiring planner, commit protocol, and deletion executor as steps with retries and terminal failure states
- `pruning-worker` Lambda handler binary in the workspace invoking the shared crates
- Scheduled trigger (EventBridge) with fast dev cadence; manual trigger supported
- Workflow no-ops safely when lease not held or nothing is prunable
- Execution observable in LocalStack (status queryable per execution)

## Out of Scope
- CDK constructs and synth assertions (prune-cdk-workflow)
- CLI trigger (prune-cli-admin)

## Testing
- Integration (LocalStack Step Functions execution happy path + failure-state path), unit for handler input/output shapes

## Demo
`make demo`, then start an execution via `awslocal stepfunctions start-execution` and watch it advance the watermark shown in the admin API.

nodes.title: Pruning watermark item in coordination table with epoch-conditional writes
nodes.description:
## Goal
Extend the DDB coordination table with a `latest-pruning` SK item following the §8.2 item pattern (mirroring `latest-checkpoint`/`latest-revocation`): pruned_end, tree_size, s3_key, signed_at, epoch — written only with epoch condition (§8.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Storage facade methods to read and advance the watermark; advance includes `epoch` in ConditionExpression
- ConditionalCheckFailed surfaces as a typed lost-lease error (per §25.4 pattern)
- Watermark only moves forward; regression attempts rejected
- Memory backend parity: same behavior under `cloud-memory`
- Integration test against LocalStack DDB

## Out of Scope
- Commit sequence orchestration (prune-commit-protocol)
- CLI display (prune-cli-admin)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backend), integration (LocalStack DDB)

## Demo
After merge: in demo env, seed a watermark via test helper and read it back with a debug command showing the `latest-pruning` item.

nodes.title: ADR: resolve OQ-7 — Step Functions vs simple Lambda chain for pruning
nodes.description:
