## Goal
Resolve OQ-7 (§26): choose Step Functions or a simple Lambda chain for the pruning workflow (§15.2, Phase 7 §24), recorded as an ADR that downstream tickets implement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- ADR committed under `docs/adr/` comparing both options on: LocalStack fidelity, retry/failure semantics, local debuggability, CDK complexity, agent-driven testability
- ADR ends with an explicit Decision and Consequences section naming the chosen mechanism unambiguously (no "either could work" hedging)
- Spike script checked in that executes a trivial state machine (or chained Lambda) against LocalStack, proving the chosen mechanism runs locally
- ADR restates the local-only constraint (§1 non-goals: no production cloud spend) and how the choice honors it

## Out of Scope
- Implementing the pruning workflow itself (prune-stepfn-workflow)
- CDK constructs (prune-cdk-workflow)

## Testing
- Spike integration check against LocalStack; no permanent test suite obligations beyond the committed spike script

## Demo
`make demo` env up, then run the spike script and show a successful execution in LocalStack logs.

nodes.title: Admin API endpoints for revocation operations
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose revocation operations through the admin API per the §17.5 end-to-end flow, so CLI and UI share one OpenAPI-defined surface (§17.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: OpenAPI additions + `make api-gen`: `GET /revocations/current` (list + metadata), `POST /revocations` (add range/index with required justification + incident ref, privileged), `POST /revocations/distribute` (trigger emergency processing + push, privileged)
- PR 2: axum handlers in `crates/admin`: POST persists a `RevocationRequest` and invokes the processor; distribute triggers the emergency path; responses include new `tree_size`/`s3_key`
- Privileged endpoints record operator identity into the audit record (§20.3); missing justification returns 400
- Handler unit tests on memory backend; integration test via LocalStack covering the full add-then-distribute sequence

## Out of Scope
- CLI subcommands (rev-cli) and UI page (rev-ui)
- AuthN/AuthZ machinery itself (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
Unit, integration (§19.1).

## Demo
`curl -X POST localhost:PORT/api/revocations -d '{...}'` then `GET /revocations/current` shows the new range.

nodes.title: CDK constructs for revocation Lambda, hourly schedule, and SNS topic
nodes.description:
## Goal
Define the revocation infrastructure in CDK (§16.2, §16.3): revocation-processor Lambda, EventBridge hourly schedule rule, SNS push-notification topic, and least-privilege IAM — validated by synth assertions, no real AWS deploy (§1 non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria
- CDK construct `RevocationStack`: Lambda from rev-lambda asset, EventBridge rule `rate(1 hour)` targeting it (§16.2 hourly default), SNS topic for list-published notifications (§16.3 step 6)
- IAM: Lambda role scoped to the `revocations/*` S3 prefix, the coordination-table revocation items, and SNS topic publish only; HSM connectivity supplied via env/secret config, not IAM
- `cdk synth` assertion tests (jest) verify: rule schedule, Lambda env config, topic wiring, and that no wildcard resource grants exist
- Constructs deployable to LocalStack via the dev-env flow so the hourly rule fires locally

## Out of Scope
- CloudFront cache behavior (rev-distribution-cdn)
- Production account deployment (spec §1 non-goal)

## Testing
Unit (cdk synth assertions), integration (LocalStack deploy smoke).

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK app shows RevocationStack assertions green; `make dev-env` brings the rule + Lambda up in LocalStack.

nodes.title: mtcctl revocation subcommands and cert revoke
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the CLI surface from §17.3: `mtcctl revocation list|add|distribute` and `mtcctl cert revoke`, driving the admin API endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `mtcctl revocation list` (human table + `--output json|yaml`), `mtcctl revocation add --start N --end M --justification ... --incident-ref ...` (privileged: requires `--confirm` or interactive confirmation, `--yes` for automation per §17.3)
- PR 2: `mtcctl revocation distribute` (privileged, triggers emergency redistribution) and `mtcctl cert revoke --index N` as sugar for a single-index range add (§16.3 step 1 operator entrypoint)
- Missing justification/incident-ref is a client-side error before any API call
- Help text documents each subcommand; shell completion picks up new commands
- E2E shell test in `tests/e2e/` driving add → list → distribute against the demo env (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Admin API implementation (rev-admin-api)
- `mtcctl report revocation` (observability epic, §20.3)

## Testing
Unit (arg parsing), E2E (§19.1).

## Demo
`mtcctl cert revoke --index 42 --justification "demo" --incident-ref DEMO-1 --yes && mtcctl revocation list`.

nodes.title: CloudFront-fronted revocation list distribution config
nodes.description:
## Goal
Serve the current revocation list through the CloudFront-fronted S3 read path (§16.2) with cache behavior tuned so relying parties meet the 15-minute freshness target.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CloudFront cache behavior for `/revocations/*`: immutable list objects get TTL >= 24h (keyed by tree_size, never mutated per §8.1 invariants); the latest-pointer lookup path gets TTL <= 60s
- Latency budget documented in the construct README: pointer TTL + hourly cadence + push refresh keeps 99% of relying parties within 15 min (§16.2)
- Emergency path decision recorded with the math: push notification + pointer re-fetch, no CloudFront invalidation call needed because pointer TTL <= 60s
- `cdk synth` assertion tests verify the behavior exists, both TTL values, and origin access scoped to the log bucket `revocations/` prefix only
- Local dev: equivalent path served by the LocalStack/dev proxy so the list URL works without CloudFront

## Out of Scope
- The base CloudFront distribution (read-path epic)
- Push notification transport (rev-push-notification)

## Testing
Unit (cdk synth assertions), E2E via local proxy path.

## Demo
`curl` the local read-path endpoint for the latest revocation pointer, then fetch the referenced `revocations/*.signed` object and confirm its bytes match the S3 object.

nodes.title: E2E emergency revocation flow test and demo
nodes.description:
## Goal
Prove the full §16.3 emergency flow end-to-end in the local environment and make it a repeatable demo, covering the §19.1 issue → verify → revoke scenario.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shell E2E in `tests/e2e/` driving `mtcctl`: issue cert → `log verify` passes → `cert revoke` with justification + incident ref → processor Lambda runs → new signed list in S3 → `latest-revocation` pointer advanced → push notification received → `log verify` now fails with Revoked
- Asserts audit record contains operator, justification, incident ref, timestamp (§20.3)
- Measures and prints local end-to-end propagation time (initiate → subscriber refresh) as a proxy for the §16.2 15-minute target
- Wired into `make test-e2e`; demo step added to `make demo` script output
- Test is deterministic: uses fake clock (§18.4) and polls with bounded timeout

## Out of Scope
- Chaos variants (testing-infrastructure epic)
- Multi-region revocation behavior during failover (multi-region epic)

## Testing
E2E (§19.1).

## Demo
`make test-e2e` runs the emergency-revocation scenario; the same script is the demo narrative.

nodes.title: revocation-processor Lambda wrapper (emergency + hourly triggers)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Package rev-processor-core as the event-driven `revocation-processor` Lambda (§5 component table, §7) handling both emergency invocations and the hourly scheduled cadence (§16.2), runnable on LocalStack.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `cargo-lambda` binary crate; event enum for emergency-trigger and scheduled-hourly payloads; S3/DDB/HSM clients cached at module level (§12.3 pattern)
- PR 2: hourly behavior — scheduled run republishes only when pending requests exist or `signed_at` staleness exceeds cadence; emergency run always processes immediately; uses injected `Clock` (§18.4) so `make time-advance` exercises cadence logic
- Emits metrics: list age seconds, publish latency (feeds §16.2 latency target and §20.2 revocation rate)
- Deploys to LocalStack via dev-env compose; integration test invokes the function through LocalStack Lambda and asserts a new signed list + pointer update

## Out of Scope
- CDK constructs, EventBridge rule, SNS topic (rev-cdk-infra)
- Notification delivery (rev-push-notification)

## Testing
Unit, integration (LocalStack, §19.1).

## Demo
`awslocal lambda invoke` with an emergency payload produces a new `revocations/*.signed` object visible via `awslocal s3 ls`.

nodes.title: RevocationList domain type with normalized revoked-range set
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the `RevocationList` domain type per spec §16.1 (`log_id`, `tree_size`, `revoked` ranges, `signed_at`, `signature`) plus a `RevokedRanges` value type with enforced invariants, in a new `crates/revocation` library.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RevocationList` struct uses newtypes from core-mtc-types (§22): `TrustAnchorID`, index/tree-size types
- `RevokedRanges` constructor normalizes to sorted, non-overlapping, adjacency-merged `(start_index, end_index)` ranges; rejects `start > end` and ranges beyond `tree_size`
- `is_revoked(index) -> bool` via binary search; `add_range` returns a new normalized set
- Invalid states unrepresentable: normalized set only constructible via validating constructors
- Unit tests: empty list, single index, adjacent/overlapping merges, boundary indices
- Property tests (`proptest`, §19.2): normalization idempotent; `is_revoked` agrees with naive linear scan for arbitrary range sets; merging two sets preserves membership

## Out of Scope
- Wire serialization and signature bytes (rev-list-serialization)
- Signing (rev-signer); storage (rev-storage-ops)

## Testing
Unit, property (§19).

## Demo
`cargo test -p revocation` green; crate doc example constructs a list and queries `is_revoked`.

nodes.title: RevocationList wire serialization and signing payload
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add TLS-presentation serialize/parse for `RevocationList` (§16.1) including the canonical signing-payload encoding of the fields covered by `signature`, following the wire-format conventions of the mtc-serialization layer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `serialize_tls_presentation` / `parse_tls_presentation` for `RevocationList`; separate `signing_payload()` producing deterministic bytes over `log_id`, `tree_size`, `revoked`, `signed_at` (§16.1)
- Parser never panics on untrusted bytes; refuses inputs claiming impossible sizes; bounded recursion (§19.3 asserted properties)
- `Arbitrary` impl for `RevocationList`; proptest round-trip `parse(serialize(x)) == x` at extended iteration counts (§19.3 layer 1)
- Malformed-input unit tests: truncated buffer, overlapping-range encoding rejected, trailing garbage rejected

## Out of Scope
- Fuzz targets (rev-list-fuzz-target)
- Signature generation/verification (rev-signer)

## Testing
Unit, property (§19.2, §19.3 layer 1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p revocation` shows round-trip proptest passing; `make test-prop` includes the new cases.

nodes.title: Revocation processor core logic (library, backend-agnostic)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the revocation-processor pipeline as a testable library crate per §16.3 steps 2-6: consume pending requests, produce a new signed `RevocationList`, persist it, advance the pointer, emit a refresh event.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `process_revocations()` — load current list via pointer, merge all pending request ranges at current `tree_size`, sign via `RevocationSigner`, write object, conditionally advance pointer, mark requests processed; returns typed outcome
- PR 2: idempotency + failure handling — pointer CAS failure retries with fresh read; crash between S3 write and pointer update is safe (re-run converges); no-op run (no pending requests) produces no new object
- Emits a `RevocationPublished` event through a small notifier trait (implemented in rev-push-notification)
- Unit tests on memory backend: single request, batched concurrent requests, CAS-conflict retry, crash-replay idempotency
- Property test: processing any request sequence in any batching yields identical final revoked-range set

## Out of Scope
- Lambda wrapper and triggers (rev-lambda)
- Push transport (rev-push-notification)

## Testing
Unit, property, integration via memory backend (§19.1, §19.2).

## Demo
`cargo test -p revocation` demonstrates request-to-signed-list pipeline against in-memory backends.

nodes.title: Push notification for near-real-time revocation refresh
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement §16.2/§16.3 step 6: publishing a push notification when a new revocation list commits, so subscribers refresh immediately instead of waiting for the hourly cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RevocationNotifier` trait impl publishing `RevocationPublished { tree_size, s3_key, signed_at }` to the SNS topic; memory impl for unit tests
- Publish happens only after the pointer update succeeds (§16.3 ordering) — no notifications for uncommitted lists
- LocalStack wiring: SQS queue subscribed to the topic in dev compose; example subscriber that re-fetches the list on message
- Integration test: emergency processing run results in a queue message within seconds, and the message's `s3_key` matches the pointer
- Publish failure does not roll back the commit; it is retried and surfaced as a metric/alarm condition

## Out of Scope
- SNS topic CDK definition (rev-cdk-infra)
- Relying-party client caching policy (rev-verify-check)

## Testing
Unit, integration (LocalStack SNS/SQS, §19.1).

## Demo
Run the demo subscriber, `mtcctl revocation distribute`, and watch the refresh message arrive in the terminal.

nodes.title: Revocation request intake and audit records
nodes.description:
## Goal
Model operator revocation requests and persist the audit trail required for the revocation report: range or single index, justification, incident ref, operator identity, timestamp (§16.3 step 1, §20.3 revocation log row).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RevocationRequest` type: target (index or range), `justification: NonEmptyString`, `incident_ref`, operator identity, requested_at; validation rejects empty justification and out-of-bounds ranges
- Requests persisted via storage facade (DDB item pattern consistent with §8.2 conventions) with status pending/processed
- Query API: list pending requests; list all requests in a time range (feeds §20.3 report generation)
- Unit tests: validation failures, pending-to-processed transition, time-range query
- Integration test against LocalStack DDB

## Out of Scope
- Report generation and signing (observability epic, §20.3)
- Processing requests into a list (rev-processor-core)

## Testing
Unit, integration (§19.1).

## Demo
`cargo test -p revocation` shows a request persisted and queried back with full audit fields.

nodes.title: Revocation list signing/verification via Hsm trait with dedicated key
nodes.description:
## Goal
Sign and verify `RevocationList` snapshots using the dedicated revocation-list key (§14.1: ECDSA P-256 in v1) through the `Hsm` trait, mirroring the checkpoint-signer pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RevocationSigner` takes `dyn Hsm` + revocation key id; produces `signature` over `signing_payload()` (§16.1)
- `verify_revocation_list(&list, &public_key)` free function usable by relying parties without HSM access
- Key id is distinct from checkpoint/pruning keys (§14.1 table); wrong-key signatures fail verification
- HSM never asked to sign malformed payloads: signer only accepts validated `RevocationList` values (§19.6)
- Unit tests against memory-backend fake HSM: sign/verify round-trip, tampered payload rejected, wrong key rejected
- Integration test against SoftHSM PKCS#11 backend gated behind `--features integration` (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Key generation/rotation ceremonies (HSM epic scope)
- Processor orchestration (rev-processor-core)

## Testing
Unit, integration (SoftHSM), cryptographic invariant tests (§19.6).

## Demo
`cargo test -p revocation --features integration` signs and verifies a list against SoftHSM in the compose dev env.

nodes.title: Revocation storage: S3 revocations/ objects + DDB latest-revocation pointer
nodes.description:
## Goal
Extend the storage facade with revocation persistence: immutable signed-list objects under `revocations/` (§8.1) and the atomically-updated `latest-revocation` DDB item (§8.2, §16.3 step 5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `write_revocation_list` stores signed bytes at deterministic zero-padded key `revocations/{tree_size:016}.signed` (§8.1, §16.3 step 4); write-once semantics — re-write of an existing key with different bytes errors; `read_revocation_list(key)` round-trips
- PR 2: `latest-revocation` pointer ops with attributes `tree_size, s3_key, signed_at, epoch` (§8.2); update is a conditional write requiring monotonically non-decreasing `signed_at`/`tree_size` and matching epoch — stale-epoch writes rejected (§19.8)
- Unit tests on memory backend; integration tests against LocalStack S3 + DDB behind `--features integration`
- Property test: any sequence of concurrent pointer updates leaves the pointer at the maximal committed snapshot

## Out of Scope
- Object Lock retention validation (pruning-retention epic)
- Processor logic (rev-processor-core)

## Testing
Unit, property, integration (§19.1).

## Demo
Integration test output shows list object landing in LocalStack S3 and pointer advancing in DDB.

nodes.title: Relying-party revoked-range check in verification flow
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement §12.1 step 3: relying-party verification checks the certificate's index against the current revoked-ranges list, with signature-verified list fetching and caching.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: list client — fetch latest revocation list (pointer then immutable object), verify signature via `verify_revocation_list` with a pinned revocation public key, reject stale lists (`signed_at` older than configurable max age, default 2h per §16.2 hourly cadence); cache with max-age expiry plus an explicit `invalidate()` hook a push-notification subscriber can call
- PR 2: verification-pipeline integration — revoked index yields a distinct `Revoked` failure variant, separated from proof/signature failures (feeds §20.2 failure-breakdown telemetry)
- Unit tests: unrevoked passes, revoked fails, tampered list rejected, stale list rejected, `invalidate()` forces refetch
- Property test: for arbitrary revoked-range sets, verification fails iff the index is in the set
- Cryptographic invariant test (§19.6): a revoked cert's index, when removed and re-added, fails verification

## Out of Scope
- Verification library core (read-path epic)
- Push transport (rev-push-notification)

## Testing
Unit, property, cryptographic invariants (§19.6).

## Demo
`mtcctl log verify` on a revoked cert exits non-zero with a Revoked reason; on an unrevoked cert it passes.

nodes.title: Prune operations: mtcctl prune status/run + UI panel
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose pruning on the admin surface (§17.3, §15): `mtcctl prune status` (watermark and pending work) and `mtcctl prune run` (trigger workflow), plus a UI panel for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: pruning status (watermark, eligible ranges, last run) and trigger-run; handlers are thin proxies to the pruning workflow interface
- `mtcctl prune status --output json` stable; `mtcctl prune run` returns an execution ID and non-zero exit on rejected trigger
- UI panel on an appropriate page shows watermark + pending work with a run button
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Pruning Step Functions workflow and retention enforcement (pruning epic)
- Revocation commands (adm-revocation-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against stubbed pruning interface (memory backend)
- Integration: trigger against LocalStack demo, watermark advances
- E2E: `tests/e2e/prune.sh` — load fixture, run prune via CLI, assert watermark moved

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=million-entries && mtcctl prune run && mtcctl prune status`.

nodes.title: Revocation operations: mtcctl revocation list/add/distribute, cert revoke + UI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose revocation on the admin surface (§17.3, §16): `mtcctl revocation list`, `revocation add` (privileged), `revocation distribute` (emergency redistribution), and `mtcctl cert revoke` (privileged single-cert path), plus UI for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: get current revocation list, add range (privileged), trigger emergency distribution, revoke single cert by index (privileged)
- Handlers delegate to the revocation service; privileged ops tagged `x-privileged` and enforced server-side (403 without elevated principal, via adm-auth-middleware)
- `mtcctl revocation add --range A-B` and `mtcctl cert revoke --index N` require the confirmation flow; `revocation list --output json` stable
- `mtcctl revocation distribute` triggers the §16.3 emergency flow and reports distribution outcome
- Revocation UI: list view with add-range and distribute actions behind confirmation (parity)
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Revocation Lambda, list format, distribution mechanisms (revocation epic)
- Revocation report (adm-report-ops)

## Testing
- Unit: handler validation (bad ranges, overlaps), privileged gating
- Integration: revoke-then-list against demo stack
- E2E: `tests/e2e/revocation.sh` — issue, revoke via CLI, `cert lookup` shows revoked (§19.1 demo scenario)

## Demo
`mtcctl cert revoke --index 5 --yes && mtcctl revocation list` shows the entry; UI matches.

nodes.title: post-pruning fixture: deterministic pruned-log snapshot
nodes.description:
## Goal
The `post-pruning` fixture (§18.5): a deterministic snapshot of a log after pruning has run, for validating that proofs for retained entries survive pruning and making pruning-adjacent bugs reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generator builds a seeded log, advances the FakeClock past retention windows (using the `dev-time-advance` machinery), and runs the local pruning workflow to completion
- Saved via the fixture framework as `fixtures/post-pruning` with provenance (seed, pruned range, retention config) in the manifest
- Regeneration byte-stable; expected head and pruned-range boundaries documented
- Loaded state verifies: inclusion proof for a retained entry passes while the pruned range is absent from storage yet the tree head remains valid (§19.2 pruning invariant)
- `make fixture-load name=post-pruning` completes in seconds

## Out of Scope
- Pruning workflow implementation (pruning epic, §15)
- Object Lock retention enforcement E2E (§15.3, pruning epic)

## Testing
- Integration: regeneration byte-stability
- E2E: load → sampled proof for a retained entry verifies via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=post-pruning` → admin UI shows pruned ranges; `mtcctl log inclusion` on a retained entry verifies.

nodes.title: with-revocations fixture: deterministic revoked-cert snapshot
nodes.description:
## Goal
The `with-revocations` fixture (§18.5): a deterministic snapshot containing issued-then-revoked certificates, for reproducing revocation-path bugs and demoing revocation checking.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generator seeds a modest log (~10k entries) via `dev-entrygen`, then revokes a deterministic subset (~1%) through the local revocation flow
- Saved via the fixture framework as `fixtures/with-revocations` with seed and revoked-set provenance in the manifest
- Regeneration is byte-stable; expected tree head and revocation-set hash documented
- `make fixture-load name=with-revocations` → `mtcctl` reports revoked certs as revoked and the rest as valid
- Generation completes in CI-feasible time (<5 min)

## Out of Scope
- Revocation mechanics (revocation epic, §16)
- Post-pruning fixture (`dev-fixture-post-pruning`)

## Testing
- Integration: regeneration byte-stability check
- E2E: load fixture → revocation status assertions via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=with-revocations` → `mtcctl cert lookup` on a known-revoked serial reports revoked instantly.

nodes.title: Runbook: pruning failure
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/runbooks/pruning-failure.md` for failures in the pruning Step Functions workflow, per §15 and §21.2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Detection: pruning workflow failure alarms, stuck-execution alerts (§20.1), storage growth trending beyond plan (§21.1 rates)
- Assessment: classify — transient AWS error, retention-policy violation attempt (Object Lock denial, §15.3), or logic error deleting wrong ranges
- Mitigation: safe-to-retry guidance (workflow idempotency expectations), when to pause pruning entirely; explicit warning that Object Lock denials are the safety system working, not an error to bypass
- Recovery: resume workflow, reconcile pruning log report (§20.3) against expected pruned ranges, run self-auditor to confirm surviving tree integrity
- Includes storage-headroom guidance: how long the system can run with pruning disabled before hitting capacity concerns
- Passes `make lint-runbooks`

## Out of Scope
- Pruning workflow implementation (pruning epic)

## Testing
- Doc structure lint; manual drill by failing the pruning workflow mid-run in LocalStack with `make time-advance days=400` (§18.4)

## Demo
After merge: time-advance past retention in the local env, break the pruning workflow, recover following the runbook.

nodes.title: CDK: S3 lifecycle + Object Lock Compliance config aligned with retention policy (synth-only)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Encode §8 and §15.3 storage invariants in CDK: Object Lock in Compliance mode, lifecycle rules that delete pruned leaf objects only after retention expiry (§8 S3 invariants, §15.2), CRR preserving Object Lock attributes — all validated via `cdk synth` assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Synth assertions: bucket has Object Lock enabled in Compliance mode with default retention matching `RetentionPolicy` (7 years)
- Lifecycle expiration on the entries prefix is >= the Object Lock retention window (deletion only after lock expiry, §8)
- Pruning-checkpoint prefix excluded from lifecycle expiration (indefinite retention, §15.3)
- Replication configuration asserts Object Lock metadata is preserved (CRR, §15.3)
- Versioning enabled asserted (defense in depth, §8)

## Out of Scope
- Runtime deletion logic (prune-deletion-executor)
- LocalStack E2E validation (prune-objectlock-e2e)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion tests (Jest); no cloud access

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK package green; template diff shows lifecycle + Object Lock configuration.

nodes.title: CDK constructs for pruning workflow: state machine, Lambda, schedule (synth-only)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add CDK (TypeScript) constructs for the pruning workflow: state machine, pruning-worker Lambda, and EventBridge schedule (§5, §7), validated by `cdk synth` assertions only (§1 non-goals: no cloud deploy).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Constructs added to the CDK app matching the OQ-7 ADR decision
- Synth assertion tests verify: state machine states/retry config, Lambda runtime + env wiring, schedule rule targeting the workflow
- Least-privilege IAM statements asserted (workflow can only touch log bucket prefixes and coordination table)
- No test requires AWS credentials or network

## Out of Scope
- S3 lifecycle and Object Lock bucket config (prune-cdk-lifecycle)
- Workflow runtime logic (prune-stepfn-workflow)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion tests (Jest) in the infra package; runs in CI unit lane

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK package green; `cdk synth` emits the pruning state machine and Lambda in the template.

nodes.title: mtcctl prune status/run + admin API endpoints via OpenAPI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose pruning to operators per §17.3: `mtcctl prune status` (watermark + pending work) and `mtcctl prune run` (trigger workflow, privileged), backed by admin API routes defined in the OpenAPI spec so CLI and UI share one boundary (§17.1, §17.2, §17.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI paths for prune status and prune run; generated client consumed by the CLI (no hand-rolled HTTP)
- `prune status` shows current watermark, last pruning checkpoint, and planner dry-run pending-work summary; supports `--output json` (§17.3)
- `prune run` is privileged: requires `--confirm` or interactive confirmation, skippable with `--yes` (§17.3); triggers a workflow execution, returns execution id; call recorded for the admin-actions audit log (§20.3)
- Sensible errors when standby (not primary) or when nothing is prunable
- UI can consume the same endpoints (data shape documented); UI tile itself is admin-surface epic work

## Out of Scope
- Admin UI rendering of pruning watermark (admin-surface epic)
- Workflow internals

## Testing
- Unit (route handlers on memory backend), integration (CLI against demo env), E2E smoke

## Demo
`make demo`; `mtcctl prune status`; `mtcctl prune run --yes` then `mtcctl prune status` shows advanced watermark.

nodes.title: E2E scenario test: issue then prune via mtcctl in tests/e2e
nodes.description:
## Goal
Cover the pruning leg of the §19.1 demo scenario ("issue -> verify -> revoke -> prune") as an E2E test in `tests/e2e/` driving `mtcctl` against the full demo environment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Script (shell or Rust per §19.1) that: issues certs, advances the fake clock past dev retention, runs `mtcctl prune run --yes`, and asserts the watermark advanced
- Asserts inclusion proofs for unpruned entries still verify via `mtcctl` after pruning
- Asserts pruned indices are reported as pruned: `mtcctl prune status` shows the watermark above them and a proof request for a pruned index fails with a clear pruned/gone status, not an internal error (§20.2 forensics direction)
- Wired into the CI integration/E2E lane; runs green from a clean `make demo`

## Out of Scope
- Revocation leg of the scenario (revocation epic)
- Object Lock semantics validation (prune-objectlock-e2e)

## Testing
- E2E (CLI-driven against demo env)

## Demo
`./tests/e2e/prune.sh` (or `make e2e-prune`) runs the full scenario and prints the before/after watermark.

nodes.title: Deterministic post-pruning fixture: make fixture-load name=post-pruning
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the `post-pruning` deterministic fixture promised in §18.5: a snapshot of LocalStack + DDB state after a pruning run, loadable for bug reproduction, performance testing, and demos.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make fixture-load name=post-pruning` restores a state with a nonzero pruning watermark, at least one pruning checkpoint, pruned entry gaps, and intact tiles for unpruned proofs
- Fixture generation is scripted and reproducible (regenerate from seed, not hand-edited blobs)
- After load, `mtcctl prune status` and proof verification for an unpruned entry both succeed
- Fixture documented alongside the other fixtures (§18.5)
- Used by at least one integration or E2E test as its starting state

## Out of Scope
- Fixture snapshot/restore infrastructure itself (local-dev-experience epic)

## Testing
- Integration smoke: load fixture, assert expected watermark and object layout

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=post-pruning` then `mtcctl prune status` shows the fixture's watermark instantly — no long pruning run needed.

nodes.title: Pruning watermark metric, workflow metrics, and compliance event exposure
nodes.description:
## Goal
Emit the pruning signals the observability surface depends on: always-visible pruning watermark (§20.2 dashboards, tree visualization), workflow outcome metrics, and queryable pruning event records feeding the Pruning log compliance report (§20.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Watermark gauge metric plus per-run metrics: duration, entries pruned, entries skipped (unexpired lock), result status
- Pruning event records written by the commit step (prune-commit-protocol) are queryable in the shape the compliance reporter needs — "All pruning events with affected ranges" (§20.3)
- Admin API exposes watermark and recent pruning events so the UI tree visualization can render the pruning watermark (§20.2)
- Metrics emitted in the demo env and visible via the local metrics endpoint

## Out of Scope
- Dashboards, SLOs, alert definitions, report generation (observability epic)
- UI rendering (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit (event record shape, metric emission), integration (demo env: run workflow, assert metrics/events present)

## Demo
`make demo`; trigger a prune; local metrics endpoint shows the watermark gauge move and a new pruning event record via the admin API.

nodes.title: Runbook: pruning failure (docs/runbooks/pruning-failure.md)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write the required "pruning failure" runbook (§21.2) in `docs/runbooks/` following the standard structure: detection, initial assessment, mitigation, recovery, postmortem template.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers concrete failure modes: workflow stuck/failed mid-execution, deletion blocked by unexpired Object Lock at scale, watermark/checkpoint mismatch, pruning-checkpoint signing failure, replication-precondition stall
- Detection section names the alerts/metrics that fire (cross-referencing prune-metrics-events)
- Mitigation/recovery steps use real commands (`mtcctl prune status`, `mtcctl prune run`, workflow execution inspection) and were each executed once against the demo env with an induced failure
- Postmortem template included per §21.2

## Out of Scope
- Alert wiring itself (observability epic); metric emission (prune-metrics-events)

## Testing
- Docs lint/link check in CI; one manual walkthrough of recovery steps against demo env recorded in the PR description

## Demo
Induce a failure in demo env (kill workflow mid-run), then follow the runbook to recovery; watermark ends consistent.

nodes.title: with-revocations deterministic test fixture
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide the `with-revocations` fixture from §18.5: a reproducible LocalStack + DDB snapshot containing issued certs with several revoked ranges, for demos, bug repro, and downstream tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make fixture-load name=with-revocations` restores a state with: a populated log, at least 3 revoked ranges (single index, small range, range spanning a batch boundary), a signed current list, matching pointer, and audit records
- Fixture built deterministically by a script (seeded issuance + revocation via processor core), then captured with `make fixture-save`
- After load: `mtcctl revocation list` shows the expected ranges; `mtcctl log verify` fails for a known revoked index and passes for a known valid one (documented in fixture README)
- Fixture used by at least one existing test or demo to prove load correctness in CI

## Out of Scope
- Fixture save/load machinery (local-dev-experience epic)
- post-pruning fixture (pruning-retention epic)

## Testing
Integration (fixture load smoke in CI), E2E consumers.

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=with-revocations && mtcctl revocation list` shows the canned revoked ranges.

nodes.title: cargo-fuzz target for RevocationList parsing
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add the `RevocationList` fuzz target required by §19.3 ("one target per externally-parseable type"), covering both unstructured and structured fuzzing layers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_revocation_list.rs`: arbitrary bytes into `parse_tls_presentation`, asserting no panic, no UB, no excessive allocation (§19.3 layer 2)
- Structured target via `arbitrary` bridge: semi-valid lists fed to range-normalization and `is_revoked` paths without panics (§19.3 layer 3)
- Seed corpus checked in under `fuzz/corpus/parse_revocation_list/` including valid lists from proptest generators (§19.3 corpus management)
- Any crash inputs minimized and added as unit-test regression fixtures
- Targets wired into the repo's existing fuzz CI job

## Out of Scope
- Fuzz harness infrastructure itself (testing-infrastructure epic)
- Differential fuzzing vs bwesterb/mtc (RevocationList is not a Go-reference type)

## Testing
Fuzz (§19.3), unit (regression fixtures).

## Demo
`cargo fuzz run parse_revocation_list -- -runs=100000` completes clean locally.

nodes.title: Emergency revocation runbook
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write the required emergency-revocation runbook (§21.2) in `docs/runbooks/emergency-revocation.md`, grounded in the shipped CLI/UI flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Follows the §21.2 structure: detection (alerts/signals that trigger revocation, e.g. suspected mis-issuance), initial assessment, mitigation steps, recovery procedure, postmortem template
- Mitigation steps are copy-pasteable `mtcctl` commands (`cert revoke`, `revocation add`, `revocation distribute`) with justification/incident-ref conventions and privileged-confirmation notes (§17.3)
- Covers verification of success: pointer advanced, push received, relying-party check fails for revoked index; and the §16.2 15-minute freshness expectation
- Cross-links the suspected-key-compromise runbook boundary (that scenario escalates beyond list revocation)
- Walkthrough validated against the E2E demo; every command in the doc executed successfully in the dev env

## Out of Scope
- Other required runbooks (owning epics per §21.2)
- Alerting/dashboard implementation (observability epic)

## Testing
Doc validation via E2E walkthrough (commands exercised by `make test-e2e`).

## Demo
Follow the runbook top-to-bottom against `make demo` and reach the documented verified-revoked end state.

nodes.title: Admin UI revocation page (view list, initiate emergency revocation)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Add the admin UI page for revocation per §16.3 step 1 and §17.4: view the current revocation list and initiate an emergency revocation with justification + incident ref.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: `templates/pages/revocations.html` + handler in `crates/admin/src/handlers/`: current list metadata (`tree_size`, `signed_at`, range count), revoked-ranges table, and add-range/revoke-cert form with required justification + incident-ref fields plus a privileged confirmation step (§17.3 authorization parity); missing fields rejected server-side with inline error
- PR 2: "Distribute now" button triggering emergency redistribution, result surfaced inline via htmx swap; SSE update (§17.4) refreshes the list fragment when a `RevocationPublished` event lands — no manual reload
- Askama compile-time template checks pass; handler unit tests on memory backend cover render, form-validation errors, and distribute trigger

## Out of Scope
- Tree-visualization overlay of revoked ranges (observability epic, §20.2)
- API endpoints themselves (rev-admin-api)

## Testing
Unit, E2E (browser-less HTTP assertions in `tests/e2e/`).

## Demo
`make demo`, open the admin UI Revocations page, revoke an index with justification, watch the list update live.

nodes.title: Chaos and soak result triage tool
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build a triage tool that consumes chaos/soak run artifacts (produced by the testing-infra harness) and emits a classified, runbook-linked summary — plus trend tracking across archived soak runs (§19.7, §19.9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: parser + classifier — reads run result artifacts (JSON), validates schema, classifies each failure: invariant-violation (committed cert lost, split-brain, append-only breach per §19.9 pass criteria), infra-flake, timeout, known-issue (matched against a curated `known-issues.toml`)
- PR 2: report emitter — `make triage RESULTS=<dir>` writes a markdown summary: per-scenario pass/fail vs §19.9 criteria table, failure classes, and for each failed scenario a link to its runbook (chaos-primary-loss → primary-failure, chaos-hsm-down → hsm-unavailability, etc.); invariant-violations exit nonzero
- PR 3: soak trending — appends run summaries to a JSONL history; `make soak-report` flags cross-run regressions (memory growth, task leaks, latency drift per §19.7/§19.11) beyond configurable thresholds
- Unit tests with fixture artifacts for every classification branch; property test: classifier is total (never panics on arbitrary valid-schema input)
- Runs entirely locally on laptop-produced artifacts (§1 non-goals)

## Out of Scope
- Chaos harness and scenario execution (testing-infra epic); CI perf regression gating (testing-infra)

## Testing
- Unit, property (§19.2); integration against a real local chaos run's output; no fuzz/Kani/Loom

## Demo
After merge: run one chaos scenario locally, then `make triage RESULTS=target/chaos/latest` shows the classified report with runbook links.

nodes.title: Documentation polish: README, operator guide, cross-link pass
nodes.description:
## Goal
Execute the Phase 8 "documentation polish" item (§24): a final pass making the repo navigable and operable from docs alone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: README overhaul — project summary honest about scope (§1: reference blueprint, not production), the 60-second demo (§18.1) as the front-door quickstart, links to architecture spec, runbooks, and make-target catalog (§18.8)
- PR 2: operator guide at `docs/operations/README.md` — day-2 index tying together: all runbooks with their triggering alerts, capacity doc + calculator, dashboards/SLOs (§20.1), compliance reports and `mtcctl report` (§20.3), health endpoints (§20.5), failover quick-reference (§13)
- PR 3: cross-link and accuracy pass — architecture spec section references verified against code reality, stale statements corrected or annotated, every crate has a purpose line in a workspace map doc
- All pages pass `make lint-docs`; no orphan pages (everything reachable from README or docs index)

## Out of Scope
- New feature documentation for unshipped features; runbook content changes (owned by runbook tickets)

## Testing
- Doc lint + link checker (via ops-docs-ci-quality-gates); manual fresh-clone walkthrough: clone → README → `make demo` succeeds following docs only (§18.1)

## Demo
After merge: fresh clone, follow README to a running local CA in under 5 minutes; navigate from README to any runbook in ≤2 clicks.

nodes.title: Security review checklist
nodes.description:
## Goal
Produce the Phase 8 (§24) security review checklist as a structured, trackable document at `docs/security/review-checklist.md`, derived from the threat model (§3) and the system's stated invariants.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Checklist items grouped by area: key handling and HSM boundary (§14, incl. FIPS boundary §14.4), append-only/integrity invariants (§11.2, §8 S3 invariants), epoch-conditional writes and split-brain (§8.3, §13.4), retention/Object Lock (§15.3), revocation path (§16), admin surface authn/authz and audit trail (§17, §20.3), supply chain (cargo-audit/cargo-deny status §22.13), input parsing hardening (fuzz coverage §19.3)
- Every §19.8 adversarial scenario appears as a checklist item with a pointer to the test that covers it (or an explicit gap marker)
- Each item has: id, statement, verification method (test/code inspection/config check), status field (unreviewed/pass/finding/N.A.)
- Machine-checkable format (front-matter or table) with a lint script asserting every item has a status; `make lint-security-checklist` target
- Explicitly scopes out items irrelevant to the non-production stance (§1 non-goals) with rationale rather than silently omitting them

## Out of Scope
- Performing the review (ops-security-review-v1); fixing findings

## Testing
- Unit test for the checklist lint script; doc lint. No property/fuzz/Kani/Loom

## Demo
After merge: `make lint-security-checklist` green; checklist shows full item inventory with statuses all `unreviewed`.

nodes.title: Execute v1 security review
nodes.description:
## Goal
Execute the Phase 8 security review (§24) against the checklist: a structured self-review pass over the codebase with findings recorded and remediation tickets filed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- PR 1: crypto/key-handling review — HSM call sites, signature verification paths, no key material in logs, §14.4 boundary respected; checklist statuses updated with evidence links
- PR 2: storage/integrity review — every DDB write conditional on epoch (§8.3, §11.2), S3 invariants (§8) upheld at all call sites, Object Lock configuration verified in cdk synth assertions (§15.3)
- PR 3: admin surface + supply chain review — authz on every admin route, audit trail completeness (§20.3), cargo-audit/cargo-deny clean or waivers documented (§22.13)
- Every checklist item reaches pass/finding/N.A.; zero remaining `unreviewed`
- Each finding gets severity, description, and a filed beads ticket reference; findings summary lands in `docs/security/review-v1-findings.md`
- Any adversarial scenario (§19.8) lacking test coverage is filed as a testing-infra ticket reference

## Out of Scope
- Remediation implementation (filed as separate tickets in owning epics); external/third-party audit (§1: solo exploration project)

## Testing
- Review evidence cites existing unit/property/fuzz/Kani tests per area (§19); lint scripts keep checklist statuses valid

## Demo
After merge: `make lint-security-checklist` shows 100% reviewed; findings doc enumerates open items with ticket links.

nodes.title: mtcctl ops capacity calculator
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `mtcctl ops capacity` computing the §21.1 capacity model from input parameters, so operators and CI can check headroom without spreadsheet math.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl ops capacity --certs-per-hour N [--batch-size B] [--batch-interval S]` prints derived rates: batches/hour, HSM signings/hour, DDB txns/hour, S3 entry and tile writes/hour, projected storage growth/day
- Flags any derived rate exceeding configured limits (HSM throughput §14.3, service quota constants) with nonzero exit code; `--format json` for scripting
- Defaults reproduce the §21.1 worked example exactly (10K certs/hour → ~40 batches/hour etc.), asserted in a unit test so doc and code cannot drift
- Unit tests for boundary cases (rates below one batch/hour, batch-size 1, zero input rejected via newtype validation per §22.1)
- Property test (`proptest`): derived rates are monotonic in input rate; entry writes/hour equals input rate

## Out of Scope
- Live metrics-based prediction (§20.4, observability); capacity doc prose (ops-capacity-plan-doc)

## Testing
- Unit, property (§19.1, §19.2); E2E via CLI invocation in a smoke test (§19.13); no integration/fuzz/Kani/Loom

## Demo
After merge: `mtcctl ops capacity --certs-per-hour 10000` reproduces §21.1; `--certs-per-hour 10000000` shows the HSM bottleneck flagged.

nodes.title: Capacity planning document
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expand §21.1 into `docs/operations/capacity.md`: a parameterized capacity model for the whole system, distinct from the live capacity-prediction metrics owned by observability (§20.4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Derives all §21.1 rates from first principles: certs/hour, batch size (256), and batch interval → batches/hour, HSM signings/hour, DDB commit transactions/hour, S3 entry writes/hour, S3 tile writes/hour
- Documents the binding constraints and headroom at 1x/10x/100x the 10K certs/hour baseline: HSM signing throughput (§14.3), DDB transaction limits, S3 request rates, tree growth and tile storage over retention window (§15)
- States scaling levers per bottleneck (batch size vs interval tradeoff, issuance latency impact)
- Cost notes cross-referenced to §5 (modeled only — no real AWS spend per §1 non-goals)
- Reviewed against actual constants in the codebase (batch size, cadence) with source links so drift is detectable

## Out of Scope
- Calculator tooling (ops-capacity-calculator); forward-looking metrics (§20.4, observability epic)

## Testing
- Doc lint only; numeric examples in the doc are re-derived by the calculator's tests once ops-capacity-calculator lands

## Demo
After merge: doc renders in repo; worked example reproduces every §21.1 figure.

nodes.title: Documentation quality gates in CI
nodes.description:
## Goal
Wire documentation quality checks into CI so runbooks and docs cannot rot: markdown lint, link checking, and the runbook/checklist structure lints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- markdownlint (or equivalent) configured for `docs/**` with a committed config; violations fail CI
- Link checker (e.g., lychee) validates intra-repo links and anchors in `docs/**` and README; external links checked in a non-blocking scheduled job only (offline-friendly per §1)
- `make lint-runbooks` and `make lint-security-checklist` run as CI steps
- Single `make lint-docs` target runs everything locally exactly as CI does (§22.13: same checks locally and in CI)
- CI job added to the required-checks set; docs-only PRs skip Rust build for fast feedback

## Out of Scope
- Writing/fixing doc content (ops-docs-polish); the base CI pipeline itself

## Testing
- CI-level checks are the test; a fixture with a broken link/section verified to fail in a scratch run before merge

## Demo
After merge: introduce a broken relative link in a draft PR and watch the docs gate fail; `make lint-docs` reproduces locally.

nodes.title: Adversarial suite: lease, epoch, and allocation attacks
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the coordination half of the spec 19.8 adversarial suite: attacks on lease/epoch, index allocation, and replication invariants, each asserting the invariant holds or the write is rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Stalled CRR plus attempted promotion -> promotion refused until catchup (19.8)
- Forced clock skew via the test clock (+/-60s) -> lease semantics remain correct
- Duplicate index allocation attempts -> exactly one succeeds; allocated ranges never overlap
- Stale-epoch writes -> rejected by conditional checks with a typed error
- Runs against the memory backend with fault injection: deterministic and seedable, no LocalStack required (19.1)
- Gated behind `--features integration` and included in the `make redteam` target

## Out of Scope
- Wire/crypto attacks (test-adversarial-wire)
- Chaos process-level scenarios (chaos tickets)

## Testing
- Adversarial/integration (19.8); property test for allocation non-overlap under concurrent attack

## Demo
`make redteam` shows the stale-epoch write rejected and the duplicate-allocation attack producing exactly one winner.

nodes.title: Adversarial suite: wire, proof, and signing attacks
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the wire/crypto half of the spec 19.8 adversarial suite: automated attacks on parsing, proof generation, and signing invariants, each asserting a specific rejection rather than mere absence of crash.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Malformed tiles fed to inclusion-proof generation -> typed error, no panic, no bogus proof (19.8)
- Wrong signatures from a "compromised" HSM (fault-injection wrong-sig mode) -> checkpoint verification rejects with a signature error
- Replayed old checkpoints -> rejected by freshness/monotonicity checks with the expected error class
- Crafted public keys attempting key-hash collisions -> rejected; hash domain separation asserted
- Malformed-input builders (tiles, keys, checkpoints) land in mtc-testutil for reuse by component epics
- Suite gated behind `--features integration` (19.1), runs under the existing `cargo test --all-features` check (22.13); `make redteam` target added

## Out of Scope
- Coordination-layer attacks (test-adversarial-coordination)
- Fixing vulnerabilities found (filed against owning epics)

## Testing
- Adversarial/integration (19.8); unit tests for input builders

## Demo
`make redteam` shows the replayed-old-checkpoint test rejecting with the expected error.

nodes.title: Chaos scenarios: CRR stall, DDB lag, HSM down, adapter flood
nodes.description:
## Goal
Complete the full chaos suite (spec 19.9 table; roadmap Phase 8) with the infrastructure-fault scenarios.

## Acceptance Criteria
- chaos-crr-stall: injected 30-min (simulated) CRR delay -> failover waits for catchup
- chaos-ddb-lag: forced replicated-KV lag -> no split-brain; reads are stale, never incorrect
- chaos-hsm-down: HSM unavailable mid-batch -> batch retries, the observability epic's HSM-down alert signal fires, service eventually stands down
- chaos-adapter-flood: adapter floods entries -> backpressure engages; no accepted entries lost
- All registered in the chaos runner and scheduled CI job; each independently runnable via `make chaos SCENARIO=<name>`

## Out of Scope
- Epoch-invariant scenarios (test-chaos-epoch-scenarios)
- Alerting/metric definitions asserted here (observability epic owns them)

## Testing
- Chaos/integration (19.9)

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=chaos-hsm-down` shows retry, alert, and stand-down sequence ending in PASS.

nodes.title: Performance benchmark harness and regression CI gate
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement spec 19.11: benchmarks tracking p50/p99/p99.9 over time with a CI gate that fails on regression beyond threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Benchmark harness (criterion or latency-histogram based) covering key operations: tree append, inclusion-proof generation, proof verification, serialization round-trip; reports p50/p99/p99.9
- Baseline results stored in-repo (JSON) with a deliberate `make bench-baseline` update path reviewed in PRs
- CI job compares current run to baseline with a configurable threshold (e.g., >10% p99 regression fails); warmup and fixed iteration counts documented to control noise
- History retained across runs (artifact or branch) satisfying the "over time" tracking requirement (19.11)

## Out of Scope
- Service-level latency SLOs and dashboards (observability epic)
- Benchmarks for components not yet built (added by their epics using this harness)

## Testing
- Performance (19.11); unit test for the comparator threshold logic

## Demo
`make bench` runs locally and prints percentile table plus delta vs baseline.

nodes.title: Soak test harness with PR and overnight modes
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the soak harness per spec 19.7: long-running workloads that catch memory leaks, Tokio task leaks, lease starvation, cache eviction issues, and HSM connection-pool exhaustion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Workload driver generating sustained issuance + verification load against the demo environment with configurable rate and duration
- Leak detectors with trend assertions: process RSS, Tokio task count (via the service's runtime-metrics endpoint), open FDs/connections, lease-renewal continuity, cache hit-rate stability
- 10-minute PR mode (19.7) — label-gated to keep PR CI fast — and a scheduled overnight run producing a report artifact
- Failures include time-series of tracked metrics for diagnosis

## Out of Scope
- Latency percentile tracking (test-perf-regression)
- Metric endpoint implementation (observability epic)
- Fixing leaks found (filed against owning epics)

## Testing
- Soak (19.7); unit tests for detectors (synthetic leak triggers detection)

## Demo
`make soak DURATION=10m` runs the short profile locally and prints the leak-check report.

nodes.title: Testing guide: layers, commands, and authoring conventions
nodes.description:
## Goal
Write `docs/testing.md`, the authoritative guide to every test layer in spec 19.1-19.13: what each layer is for, the exact command to run it locally, and how to author new tests — including the agent affordance that E2E tests are plain shell (19.13). Part of Phase 8 documentation polish.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Documents each layer with its command: `cargo test`, `cargo test --features integration`, `make e2e`, `make conformance`, `make differential`, fuzz, `cargo kani`, `make loom`, `make chaos`, `make redteam`, `make soak`, `make bench`, `make compat`
- Decision table mapping ticket types to required test layers, matching the 25.4 ticket template's Testing section
- Documents corpus/fixture conventions: `fuzz/corpus/`, `proptest-regressions/`, conformance vectors, versioned log-state fixtures
- Linked from README and AGENTS.md so agents discover it

## Out of Scope
- Runbooks and operational docs (observability/operational epics)
- CI configuration changes

## Testing
- Doc examples validated: every listed command executes successfully on a laptop

## Demo
Open `docs/testing.md`; copy-paste any command block and it runs.

nodes.title: Cross-version compatibility fixtures and runner
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement spec 19.10: versioned fixtures of historical log states plus a compatibility runner proving current code can always read and extend logs produced by earlier versions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `fixtures/log-states/<version>/` format: serialized log-state snapshot (tiles, checkpoints, entries, metadata) plus a manifest describing producing version and expected invariants
- Capture tool (`make capture-fixture`) snapshots the log state produced by the local demo issuance flow into a new versioned fixture
- Compat runner: for every historical fixture, current code loads it, all checkpoints/proofs still verify, and a fresh append succeeds
- Runs on every PR (fixtures kept small); adding a fixture is documented as part of release/tagging flow
- First fixture captured from the current implementation

## Out of Scope
- Migration tooling for incompatible changes (operational-tooling epic)
- Wire-format versioning design decisions (core-mtc-library)

## Testing
- Integration (fixture load against memory backend); unit tests for manifest parsing

## Demo
`make compat` loads every fixture and prints per-version verification results.

nodes.title: Game day drill script and checklist
nodes.description:
## Goal
Provide a scripted "game day": an orchestrated sequence of fault injections in the local multi-region sim (§18.3) that an operator responds to using only the runbooks, validating the runbook library end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make gameday` runs a scenario sequence (at minimum: primary loss → old-primary recovery → HSM outage → adapter flood) with pauses prompting the operator to execute the matching runbook
- Machine-checked success criteria after each stage reusing §19.9 pass criteria (no committed cert lost, exactly one primary, backpressure held), reported via the triage tool
- `docs/operations/gameday.md` documents the drill: cadence recommendation, scorecard template (time-to-mitigate vs §13.5 RTO targets), and how to record results as a postmortem-lite
- Drill completes on a laptop with no cloud resources (§1 non-goals)
- Runbook gaps discovered during the first recorded drill are filed as tickets

## Out of Scope
- New chaos scenarios (testing-infra); automated failover (§1 non-goal: v1 is manual)

## Testing
- E2E by construction (§19.13); script smoke-tested in CI with operator steps auto-answered in a non-interactive mode

## Demo
After merge: `make gameday` — complete the full drill in under 30 minutes with a green scorecard.

nodes.title: mtcctl adapter commands, API routes, and Adapters UI page
nodes.description:
## Goal
Full CLI/UI parity (§17.1) for adapter operations: `mtcctl adapter list|status|pause` (§17.3) and the Adapters UI view showing per-adapter health and intake rate (§17.4), backed by new admin API routes both consume (§17.5). Decomposes into ~2 shippable PRs: read routes (list/status) across API+CLI+UI, then the pause/resume mutation path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admin API routes (OpenAPI-first, through the §17.2/17.5 codegen pipeline) for adapter list, status, pause, and resume (resume complements the spec'd §17.3 pause); pause is privileged and honors `--confirm`/`--yes` semantics (§17.3)
- `mtcctl adapter list` and `status` show per-adapter health, intake rate, and lag; `--output json` supported for agents (§17.3)
- `mtcctl adapter pause <name>` halts that adapter's intake without losing already-queued entries; state visible in `status` and reversible via resume
- Adapters UI page (htmx + Askama) renders per-adapter health and intake rate with SSE live updates (§17.4)
- CLI and UI exercise the same API routes per the §17.5 end-to-end pattern
- E2E: pause example adapter, drop a PEM (nothing logged), resume, entry logged

## Out of Scope
- Metric collection itself (adapt-health-metrics)
- New adapter implementations

## Testing
- Unit (handlers, CLI arg parsing); integration; E2E via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo-adapter`, open the Adapters UI page, then `mtcctl adapter pause example-dir --confirm` and watch status flip in both CLI and UI.

nodes.title: AWS Private CA adapter (Lambda handler)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the first real adapter (§24 Phase 9; OQ-12 selects AWS Private CA as lowest-friction): consume PCA issuance events, fetch the issued cert, apply policy, re-encode, and submit via EntryIntake. Runs as a Lambda per §10.3 (event-driven source) and §5 compute table ("Adapter services | Lambda or Fargate").

## Acceptance Criteria
- Lambda handler consumes EventBridge PCA issuance events (CloudTrail `IssueCertificate` pattern), fetches the cert via `GetCertificate`, and applies the SDK policy hook
- Re-encodes via adapter-x509; submits with `source_type="aws-pca-adapter"` and `source_id` = certificate ARN (§10.2)
- Idempotent on redelivered events: the same ARN is never logged twice (§10.3)
- Authenticates with short-lived IAM credentials (§10.3); no long-lived secrets in code or config
- Transient `GetCertificate` errors retried with backoff; poison events routed to a DLQ path with a failure metric
- Integration tests run against LocalStack with synthetic EventBridge fixtures and stubbed PCA responses — no real AWS (§1 non-goals)

## Out of Scope
- CDK infrastructure (adapt-aws-pca-cdk)
- Cloudflare/Keyfactor/EJBCA adapters; health UI

## Testing
- Unit (policy, idempotency, error mapping); integration against LocalStack (§19.1); E2E in demo env (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo` then `scripts/simulate-pca-issue.sh` injects a synthetic issuance event; `mtcctl batch list` shows the new entry sourced from aws-pca-adapter.

nodes.title: CDK construct for PCA adapter (synth assertions only)
nodes.description:
## Goal
CDK (TypeScript) construct wiring the PCA adapter as spec'd (§5 compute table: adapter services on Lambda; §10.3 event-driven source): EventBridge rule on PCA issuance events, Lambda, DLQ, least-privilege IAM. Laptop-only per §1 non-goals — validated via `cdk synth` assertions, never deployed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Construct in the CDK app composing: EventBridge rule (CloudTrail `IssueCertificate` pattern) -> PCA adapter Lambda -> SQS DLQ
- IAM role limited to `acm-pca:GetCertificate` plus intake-submission permissions; no wildcard resources
- Adapter stack is opt-in via CDK context flag (post-v1 feature, off by default; default synth output unchanged)
- Jest assertion tests verify the event pattern, DLQ wiring, environment config, and least-privilege policy statements

## Out of Scope
- Deployment to real AWS; any AWS spend
- The Lambda application code itself (adapt-aws-pca)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion unit tests (jest) per project calibration; no integration layer (no real AWS, §1)

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK app passes; `cdk synth --context enablePcaAdapter=true` renders the adapter stack to the terminal.

nodes.title: chaos-adapter-flood scenario + adapter-flood runbook
nodes.description:
## Goal
Prove intake backpressure under adapter flood: implement the `chaos-adapter-flood` scenario (§19.9: "Backpressure works; no entries lost") and write the required adapter-flood runbook (§21.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Flood-generator adapter (built on adapter-sdk) drives EntryIntake at a configurable multiple of normal rate against the local demo environment
- Scenario asserts backpressure engages: submitters receive throttle/retry errors rather than silent drops, and queue depth stays bounded
- Scenario asserts zero loss: every accepted entry appears in a committed batch (accepted count == logged count)
- Runs via the chaos harness make target and is registered in the scheduled CI chaos job (§19.9)
- `docs/runbooks/adapter-flood.md` per §21.2 structure: detection signals (per-adapter lag and intake-rate metrics, §20.3), mitigation steps (`mtcctl adapter pause`), and recovery verification

## Out of Scope
- The chaos harness framework itself (testing-infrastructure epic)
- Other chaos scenarios from the §19.9 table

## Testing
- Chaos/E2E (§19.9) in the demo env; unit tests for the flood generator's rate control

## Demo
`make chaos SCENARIO=adapter-flood` prints a report: backpressure engaged, accepted == logged, zero entries lost.

nodes.title: Adapter health and metrics surface
nodes.description:
## Goal
Build the adapter health/observability surface (§24 Phase 9): per-adapter intake counts, success rate, and lag (§20.3 Adapter activity report; §20.1 `entries_by_source_total` metric labeled by source_type), per-source intake rates for the log inventory dashboard (§20.2), and adapter registry health state exposed via an internal admin API route for health-style consumption (§17.2, §20.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- SDK runtime emits per-adapter metrics: intake count, success/failure counts, policy-reject count, source lag, last-success timestamp (§20.1, §20.3)
- Adapter registry exposes a health snapshot (running / paused / erroring, per-adapter rates) via an internal admin API route (§17.2) that the admin surface and health-style checks can read, following the §20.5 health-endpoint convention
- Paused state is persisted so it survives service restart
- Metrics flow into the local dev metrics view (§18) with per-source intake rates matching §20.2's always-visible dashboard list
- Unit tests: emission on success, failure, and policy rejection; health state transitions including erroring -> running recovery

## Out of Scope
- CLI/UI rendering of this data (adapt-admin-surface)
- Alerting/SLO thresholds (observability epic)

## Testing
- Unit; integration (§19.1): example adapter running in the demo env produces observable per-adapter metrics

## Demo
Run `make demo-adapter`, then curl the adapter-health API route: JSON shows per-adapter status, intake counts, and lag.

nodes.title: Reference adapter SDK core crate (adapter-sdk)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/adapter-sdk/`, the reference SDK third-party CA adapters build on (§10, §24 Phase 9). Provides the `Adapter` trait, a runtime harness for event-driven and polling sources, idempotent retry, a policy hook, and submission via the v1 `EntryIntake` seam (§10.2). This ticket consumes that seam; it does not modify it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `crates/adapter-sdk/` exposing an `Adapter` trait covering the §10.3 responsibilities: source subscription (event-driven or polling), policy decision hook, entry construction, submission, and source-specific retry/idempotency
- Runtime harness runs any `Adapter` as a long-lived task with graceful shutdown and backoff on source errors
- All submissions flow through the v1 `EntryIntake` interface with `source_type`/`source_id` populated for audit traceability (§10.2); resubmitting the same `source_id` is idempotent (no duplicate entries)
- Adapter registry holds heterogeneous adapters as `Vec<Arc<dyn Adapter>>` per §22.7 dispatch guidance
- Unit tests against an in-memory `EntryIntake` stub: happy path, transient-error retry, `source_id` dedup, policy rejection

## Out of Scope
- X.509 re-encoding helpers (adapt-x509-reencode)
- AWS PCA adapter, metrics/health surface, admin commands (separate tickets)
- Any change to the `EntryIntake` trait itself (owned by ca-service, v1)

## Testing
- Unit (in-memory stub, §19.1); property test (proptest, §19.2 style): arbitrary crash/retry interleavings never produce duplicate submissions for one `source_id`

## Demo
`cargo test -p adapter-sdk`; then `make demo` with the bundled no-op adapter submitting a canned entry, visible via `mtcctl batch list`.

nodes.title: Example dir-watch adapter + add-adapter guide
nodes.description:
## Goal
Prove the SDK's public API with a minimal reference adapter — watches a local directory for PEM files, re-encodes them, submits to the log — and ship the "add a new external CA adapter" guide the spec calls for (§23.1 `add-adapter.md` seeded skill; §25.7 dev-experience tickets are first-class).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Example adapter built purely on the public adapter-sdk API (no internal imports), demonstrating each §10.3 responsibility
- Dropping a PEM into the watched directory yields a logged entry with `source_type="example-dir"` and traceable `source_id` (§10.2)
- `docs/add-adapter.md` and `.claude/skills/add-adapter.md` walk through building an adapter end-to-end using the example as the template (§23.1)
- `make demo-adapter` target wires the example adapter into the local dev environment (§18)
- E2E test: drop cert fixture, entry appears in a batch, inclusion proof verifies

## Out of Scope
- Production sources (AWS PCA, Cloudflare, Keyfactor)
- Adapter pause/metrics/UI (separate tickets)

## Testing
- Unit; E2E via CLI driving the demo environment (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo-adapter`, copy `fixtures/example.pem` into the watch dir, then `mtcctl cert lookup` shows the entry with its adapter source fields.

nodes.title: X.509 to TBSCertificateLogEntry re-encoding helpers
nodes.description:
## Goal
Library helpers that re-encode an existing X.509 certificate from a source CA into a spec-compliant `TBSCertificateLogEntry` (§10.1, §10.3 responsibility 3) — the Cloudflare-playground pattern of logging existing certs as MTC entries. Lives in `crates/adapter-x509/` so it parallelizes with adapt-sdk-core.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Function mapping an X.509 cert (DER and PEM) — subject, SANs, validity, SPKI — into MTC assertion/claim types from core-mtc-types
- Unsupported or unmappable certs return typed errors; no panics on any input
- Round-trip: produced entries satisfy `parse(serialize(x)) == x` via mtc-serialization (§19.2)
- Fixture corpus: RSA and ECDSA certs, multiple DNS SANs, IP SANs, edge-case validity windows
- Fuzz target on the X.509 ingestion path per §19.3 (parser never panics on arbitrary bytes), wired into the existing `fuzz/corpus/` layout

## Out of Scope
- Policy decisions about which certs to log (SDK policy hook)
- Source CA connectivity, authentication, event handling

## Testing
- Unit, property (round-trip, §19.2), fuzz (§19.3)

## Demo
`cargo run -p adapter-x509 --example reencode < fixtures/example.pem` prints the resulting TBSCertificateLogEntry as JSON.

nodes.title: Adapter operations: mtcctl adapter list/status/pause + Adapters UI page
nodes.description:
## Goal
Expose intake adapters on the admin surface (§17.3, §17.4, §10): `mtcctl adapter list`, `adapter status` (per-adapter health and intake rate), and `adapter pause` (privileged), plus the Adapters UI view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI operations: list configured adapters, per-adapter status (health, intake rate, last entry), pause/resume (privileged)
- Handlers read from the adapter health/observability surface behind the EntryIntake seam; works with only the ACME adapter configured (v1 reality, §25.9)
- `mtcctl adapter status --output json` stable; `adapter pause <name>` requires confirmation flow and reflects paused state in subsequent status
- Pause/resume tagged `x-privileged` and enforced server-side (403 without elevated principal, via adm-auth-middleware)
- Adapters UI page: per-adapter health/intake tiles with pause/resume controls (parity)
- CLI help + UI tooltips documented

## Out of Scope
- Adapter SDK, AWS Private CA adapter, health-surface internals (adapter-pattern epic)
- EntryIntake trait itself (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Unit: handlers against stubbed adapter registry (memory backend); pause state machine edges
- Integration: pause ACME adapter in demo stack, assert intake stops
- E2E: shell script pauses/resumes via CLI and asserts status transitions

## Demo
`mtcctl adapter pause acme --yes && mtcctl adapter status` shows paused; sample issuance loop stalls, then resume.

nodes.title: Seed skill: add-adapter.md for external CA adapters
nodes.description:
## Goal
Seed `.claude/skills/add-adapter.md` per §23.1: how to add a new external CA adapter behind the `EntryIntake` seam established in v1 (§25.9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Skill documents the adapter seam: the `EntryIntake` trait, the ACME adapter as the reference pattern, adapter registration/configuration, and adapter tests
- "Files involved" gives 3–5 pointers including the trait definition and the reference adapter
- Common pitfalls: bypassing the seam, coupling an adapter to storage internals, vendor types crossing the domain boundary (§22.8)
- Passes `make skill-lint`

## Out of Scope
- The adapter SDK and any concrete adapter implementation (adapter-pattern epic, post-v1)

## Testing
- `make skill-lint`; skill validated by tracing the ACME adapter against the documented pattern, noted in the PR (§19.13 spirit)

## Demo
Open the skill; every referenced path resolves, and the ACME adapter matches the documented adapter pattern step for step.

nodes.title: Azure backend: Cosmos DB ReplicatedKv + Managed HSM
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `ReplicatedKv` on Cosmos DB (ETag-based CAS, bounded-staleness or strong consistency) and `Hsm` on Azure Managed HSM, in `crates/cloud-azure/` (§27.1, §27.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `CosmosKv` implements `ReplicatedKv` using ETag conditional writes; lease/epoch conditional-write semantics match the DynamoDB behavior (§27.2)
- Consistency-level choice (bounded staleness vs strong, §27.2) is a documented config knob with a safe default
- `ManagedHsm` implements `Hsm` over the PKCS#11/KMS-style surface (§27.2 HSM table); signatures verify via the core library
- Shared conformance suite (§9.7) passes against a local Cosmos stub by default; running against the Cosmos DB Linux emulator is supported behind an opt-in flag (it is resource-heavy)
- Unsupported capabilities return typed errors, never panics

## Out of Scope
- Blob storage (mcloud-azure-object-storage); replication-lag probes (mcloud-replication-lag)
- Any real Azure account usage (§1 non-goals)

## Testing
- Unit; property test: concurrent ETag CAS yields one winner; integration against Cosmos stub, opt-in emulator job (§19.1, §19.2).

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-azure` runs KV conformance against the stub; `docker compose --profile azure-cosmos up -d` enables the emulator-backed run.

nodes.title: Azure backend: Blob Storage ObjectStore + Immutable Storage (Locked)
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` (§9) for Azure Blob Storage in a new `crates/cloud-azure/` crate, using Immutable Storage in Locked mode for compliance retention (§27.1, §27.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/cloud-azure/` crate with `BlobObjectStore` implementing `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock`
- Locked immutability policy semantics match S3 Object Lock Compliance mode: no delete/overwrite before retain-until (§27.2)
- Shared `cloud-test-suite` conformance tests (§9.7) pass against Azurite in docker compose
- Immutability behaviors Azurite cannot express are contract-tested against an in-process stub; every gap documented in the crate README
- Azure dependencies feature-gated; default workspace builds unaffected

## Out of Scope
- Cosmos DB ReplicatedKv and Managed HSM (mcloud-azure-kv-hsm)
- GRS replication-lag handling (mcloud-replication-lag); Pulumi stacks (mcloud-pulumi-iac)

## Testing
- Unit tests for API/error mapping; integration via shared conformance suite against Azurite (§19.1). No Kani/Loom/fuzz layers apply.

## Demo
`docker compose --profile azure up -d && cargo test -p cloud-azure --features emulator` — conformance suite green, including retention-denied deletion case.

nodes.title: mtcctl cloud probe: capability verification for long-tail backends
nodes.description:
## Goal
Ship `mtcctl cloud probe` (§27.4): a capability-verification command that tests whether an arbitrary S3-compatible/KV endpoint meets the CA's hard requirements before anyone attempts a deployment on it. Where capabilities are missing, the target is genuinely unsuitable — the tool must say so rather than paper over gaps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl cloud probe --object-store <endpoint> [--kv <endpoint>]` runs live checks: Object Lock create/verify/delete-denied round-trip, conditional-write (CAS) conflict behavior, basic latency/clock sanity
- Emits a suitability report with pass/fail/unsupported per capability and an overall verdict, mapped to the §27.4 guidance (e.g., R2/B2/Wasabi lock support "requires verification")
- Probe against MinIO with Object Lock enabled passes; against an S3-compatible store without lock support it fails with actionable output
- JSON and human-readable output modes; probe leaves no persistent state (cleans up its test bucket/keys where retention allows)

## Out of Scope
- Implementing any long-tail backend (R2/B2/Wasabi adapters)
- HSM probing (§27.4 notes long-tail clouds lack managed HSM; documented, not probed)

## Testing
- Unit for report/verdict logic; integration against MinIO (pass) and LocalStack S3 variants (§19.1); E2E via CLI invocation in compose (§19.13).

## Demo
`docker compose --profile onprem up -d && mtcctl cloud probe --object-store http://localhost:9000` prints a suitability report.

nodes.title: GCP backend: Firestore ReplicatedKv + KMS-fronted Cloud HSM
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement `ReplicatedKv` on Firestore (transactional version-based CAS) and `Hsm` on GCP Cloud HSM via its KMS-fronted API, in `crates/cloud-gcp/` (§27.1, §27.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `FirestoreKv` implements `ReplicatedKv` using Firestore transactions for compare-and-set; conditional-write semantics required by the lease/epoch protocol match the DynamoDB behavior (§27.2)
- `GcpKmsHsm` implements `Hsm`; `KeyHandle` encodes a KMS key resource path rather than a PKCS#11 slot (§27.2 HSM differences)
- Signatures produced through the Hsm impl verify with the core library's verification path
- Shared conformance suite (§9.7) passes against the Firestore emulator
- Hsm impl exercised against a local stub of the KMS API; unsupported capabilities return typed errors, never panics

## Out of Scope
- GCS storage (mcloud-gcp-object-storage); replication-lag probes (mcloud-replication-lag)
- Multi-region Firestore topology beyond documenting the consistency model (§27.2)

## Testing
- Unit; property test: concurrent CAS attempts on one key yield exactly one winner per version; integration against the Firestore emulator and KMS stub (§19.1, §19.2).

## Demo
`docker compose --profile gcp up -d && cargo test -p cloud-gcp --features emulator` — KV conformance plus a lease-style CAS handoff demo test pass.

nodes.title: GCP backend: GCS ObjectStore + Object Retention Lock
nodes.description:
## Goal
Implement the `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` traits (§9) for Google Cloud Storage in a new `crates/cloud-gcp/` crate, using GCS Object Retention Lock for compliance-mode retention (§27.1, §27.2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/cloud-gcp/` crate with `GcsObjectStore` implementing `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` from `cloud-types`
- Retention semantics mirror S3 Object Lock Compliance mode: delete before retain-until is rejected with a typed error (§27.2)
- Shared `cloud-test-suite` conformance tests (§9.7) pass against fake-gcs-server in docker compose
- Retention behaviors the emulator cannot express are covered by contract tests against an in-process stub; gaps listed in the crate README
- GCP dependencies feature-gated so default workspace builds are unaffected

## Out of Scope
- Firestore ReplicatedKv and Cloud HSM (mcloud-gcp-kv-hsm)
